reviewed.summary: The deterministic single-scatter integrator is structurally better than feared: the integral form I = F_sun * INT beta_scat * P/(4pi) * T_sun * T_obs ds is correct, phase functions are properly 4pi-normalized, the Bodhaine-1999-style Rayleigh cross-section with Peck & Reeder dispersion validates to ~1% of published optical depths, shell path lengths are analytic, ray-sphere geometry is adequate at Earth scale in f64, and the Lambertian ground term has correct A/pi * cos(theta) form. However, there is one critical, systemic sign error: every estimator evaluates the phase function at the SUPPLEMENT of the true scattering angle (sun_dir.dot(-view_dir) instead of sun_dir.dot(view_dir)), which reverses forward/backward scattering for Henyey-Greenstein aerosols/clouds (g=0.68-0.75) and underestimates the aerosol phase by a factor of ~120 at the production view geometry; it is masked because all single-scatter tests use rayleigh_fraction=1.0. Additionally, the much-advertised Snell-refraction machinery is real and tested but is never activated by the production prayer-time pipeline (refractive_index stays at its 1.0 default), and the 6 AFGL reference atmospheres are fabricated (5 of 6 silently fall back to US Standard).

allFindings.title: Scattering angle is the supplement of the true angle: forward and backward scattering are reversed for aerosols/clouds
allFindings.why_wrong: The incoming solar ray propagates along -sun_dir and the scattered ray toward the observer propagates along -view_dir, so cos(Theta) = (-sun_dir)·(-view_dir) = sun_dir·view_dir — the code's own comment contradicts its code. The standard sky-radiance relation (Chandrasekhar; used in DISORT/6S/libRadtran and Bruneton & Neyret 2008) is cos(Theta) = cos(SZA)cos(VZA) + sin(SZA)sin(VZA)cos(dphi) = sun_dir·view_dir, with Theta=0 (forward peak, the aerosol aureole) when looking at the sun. The code yields cos_theta=-1 (backscatter) when looking at the sun. Rayleigh P = 0.75(1+cos^2) is symmetric so the bug is invisible in the Rayleigh-only tests (all test atmospheres use rayleigh_fraction: 1.0), but Henyey-Greenstein with the data crate's g=0.68-0.75 (aerosol.rs:82-132, OPAC-like, forward-peaked) is flipped. At the production geometry (pipeline.rs:574 view_zenith=85 deg at the solar azimuth, SZA=96, g=0.70) the HG phase is evaluated at -0.982 instead of +0.982: 0.105 vs 12.96, a ~123x underestimate of the aerosol single-scatter contribution. The identical flip exists in the hybrid order-1 NEE (photon.rs:2468) and in the backward-MC NEE (photon.rs:425: cos_angle = sun_dir.dot(-photon_dir)), so the whole engine is consistently wrong, not self-correcting. Any aerosol- or cloud-laden twilight (i.e., real skies) gets a materially wrong radiance and hence a shifted threshold-crossing SZA for Fajr/Isha.
allFindings.recommendation: Change to let cos_theta = sun_dir.dot(view_dir); (and sun_dir.dot(photon_dir)/sun_dir.dot(current_dir) at all NEE sites, plus the equivalent in the Metal shader and the hg_mueller calls). Add a regression test with rayleigh_fraction=0, g=0.7, sun above horizon: radiance looking 20 deg from the sun must greatly exceed radiance looking 160 deg away.

allFindings.title: Snell refraction is implemented and documented but never activated in the production prayer-time pipeline
allFindings.evidence:
atmosphere.rs:102: refractive_index: [1.0; MAX_SHELLS],     // default: no refraction
single_scatter.rs doc: "Traces the ray shell-by-shell, applying Snell's law at each boundary so the shadow ray follows the physically correct refracted path"
pipeline.rs build_atmosphere() calls builder::build_full(...) and never calls compute_refractive_indices().
allFindings.why_wrong: grep confirms compute_refractive_indices / compute_refractive_indices_from_altitude are called only from #[cfg(test)] code (photon.rs:5720+ inside the tests module starting at line 5008, and twilight-gpu/src/buffers.rs tests). builder.rs contains no refraction setup, and build_atmosphere -> build_full leaves refractive_index at the all-1.0 default, so refract_at_boundary takes its documented identity fast path (geometry.rs:216-218) on every production shadow ray. Atmospheric refraction bends grazing limb rays by up to ~1.1 deg total (0.57 deg per horizon pass, standard value), raising the illumination of the twilight layer at SZA 90-96+; twilight-modeling literature (e.g., Rozenberg 1966; Anderson's twilight ozone work) includes terminator refraction for exactly this reason. The capability is presented in module docs as active physics ("physically correct refracted path") but in the shipped pipeline every ray is straight.
allFindings.recommendation: Call atm.compute_refractive_indices() inside builder::build_full / build_full_with_gas (the Rayleigh extinction it needs is populated there), and add a pipeline-level test asserting refractive_index[0] is approximately 1.000293 after build_atmosphere.

allFindings.title: Claims 6 AFGL reference atmospheres; 5 of 6 silently return US Standard 1976
allFindings.why_wrong: The module header advertises the Anderson et al. (1986) AFGL set (tropical, mid-latitude summer/winter, subarctic summer/winter), and the public AtmosphereType enum accepts all six, but only US Standard data exists; every other selection silently falls back (same pattern in pressure_at, number_density_at, ozone_density_at). A test even enshrines the fallback (all_profiles_fall_back_to_us_standard). For a global prayer-time product this is a fabricated capability: tropical vs subarctic density/ozone profiles differ enough to change twilight radiance, and a user selecting Tropical gets US Standard with no warning. Relatedly, the grid doc is wrong: "Standard altitude grid in km (50 levels from 0 to 100 km)" but ALTITUDE_GRID_KM is a 51-slot array with only NUM_LEVELS=41 real entries plus 10 zero-padding values that would break any consumer iterating the full constant.
allFindings.recommendation: Either add the real AFGL profile tables or remove the unimplemented enum variants (or make selection return an error). Fix the '50 levels' doc and drop the zero padding (use a 41-element array).

allFindings.title: Refraction (when enabled) is applied only to sun-side shadow rays; the observer line of sight is always straight
allFindings.why_wrong: shadow_ray_transmittance traces shell-by-shell with refract_at_boundary, but the LOS march that places the scatter points and accumulates tau_obs is a pure straight line with no Snell refraction, so even with refraction enabled the sun-side and observer-side paths use inconsistent physics. At the production default view_zenith of 85 deg, LOS refraction over a full atmospheric path is a few tenths of a degree, displacing the high-altitude scatter points and the LOS optical depth relative to the refracted reality. A second latent issue: with piecewise-constant n over 1-km shells, refract_at_boundary returns TotalReflection for outward rays within ~0.5 deg of tangent (geometry.rs:237-241, critical angle from adjacent-shell delta-n ~3e-5) — exactly the twilight shadow-ray geometry — producing spurious ducting that a continuously varying n(h) would not (standard practice integrates the ray-curvature ODE, e.g., Auer & Standish 2000, van der Werf 2003, instead of discrete Snell on coarse shells). Currently moot in production because of the refraction-never-enabled finding, but it will bite as soon as that is fixed.
allFindings.recommendation: If refraction is turned on, trace the LOS with the same shell-by-shell refracted walk used for shadow rays (or document the engine as refraction-free and delete the half-wired feature). Replace discrete Snell with Bouguer-invariant ray bending per shell to eliminate artificial TIR near tangency.

allFindings.title: King depolarization factor is a fabricated linear fit with ~13x too little wavelength dependence
allFindings.why_wrong: Bodhaine et al. (1999, Eqs. 5-6: F(N2)=1.034+3.17e-4/lam^2, F(O2)=1.096+1.385e-3/lam^2+1.448e-4/lam^4) gives F(air) = 1.0513 at 400 nm, 1.0488 at 550 nm, 1.0479 at 700 nm — a spread of ~3.4e-3 across the band. The code's formula yields 1.04813 / 1.0480 / 1.04787, a spread of only 2.6e-4 (about 13x too flat), and does not even reproduce the values quoted in its own comment (which are themselves not the Bates/Bodhaine numbers). Net effect on the cross-section is bounded at ~0.3% at 400 nm (sigma 1.669e-26 vs 1.674e-26 cm^2), so the magnitude is small — the constant is a fudge rather than a wrong-order error, and the surrounding Bodhaine formula (Peck & Reeder dispersion, N_s=2.546899e19, Lorentz-Lorenz, tau(550)=0.097) is otherwise correct.
allFindings.recommendation: Replace the linear hack with Bodhaine 1999 Eqs. 5-6 (per-gas King factors composited by mixing ratio) — it is 4 lines — and update the test reference values.

allFindings.title: "Straight-line approximation is exact to f64 precision" is self-contradictory and mischaracterizes the VPL geometry
allFindings.why_wrong: An approximation that neglects bending cannot be 'exact to f64 precision' (f64 implies ~1e-16 relative error; neglected refraction is a physical-model error, not a rounding error). The justification is also one-sided: photon.rs:4624 calls transmittance_between_points_spectrum(atm, scatter_pos, lv.pos, ...) where only lv.pos is the VPL — scatter_pos lies anywhere along the observer LOS, including low altitudes where a near-horizontal segment bends by 0.1-0.5 deg, not < 0.01 deg. The straight-line choice itself is a defensible standard approximation (and consistent with production where refraction is off); only the precision claim is wrong.
allFindings.recommendation: Reword to an honest error bound (e.g., 'neglects refraction; sub-percent transmittance error for the dominant high-altitude segments') or compute the segment with the refracted tracer when the low endpoint is below ~10 km.

allFindings.title: Comment claims adaptive LOS step size; implementation is uniform, capped at 200 steps (~5.7 km near the horizon)
allFindings.why_wrong: ds_base is constant and s = (step+0.5)*ds_base is a uniform midpoint rule — there is no adaptivity anywhere in the loop. With MAX_LOS_STEPS=200 and a near-horizontal twilight LOS of ~1130 km to TOA (sqrt(2*R*100km)), steps are ~5.7 km: per-step tau at 400 nm near the surface is ~0.25 (midpoint-exponential error ~0.3%/step) and each step's optics come from the single shell containing the midpoint even when the step straddles 1-km shells. This is a tolerable but crude quadrature for the twilight regime the engine exists for (SZA 90-108, near-tangent paths), and the comment misrepresents it.
allFindings.recommendation: Either implement what the comment says (e.g., per-shell analytic segments like ray_path_through_shell, or log-spaced steps) or fix the comment; raise the step cap for near-horizontal LOS and add a convergence test at SZA 96-106.

allFindings.title: Comment claims numerically stable quadratic; code uses the classic cancellation-prone form
allFindings.why_wrong: The stable formulation (q = -(b + sign(b)*sqrt_disc)/2; t1 = q/a, t2 = c/q — Press et al., Numerical Recipes 5.6) is precisely what this is NOT: (-b + sqrt_disc) cancels when b>0 and 4ac is small. In practice the damage is bounded — at Earth scale in f64 the absolute error in c = |o|^2 - r^2 is ~1e-2 m^2, giving sub-millimeter t errors away from exact tangency — so this is a false comment rather than a numerical hazard, but it is exactly the kind of unearned claim the maintainer is auditing for, in the most safety-critical geometry routine.
allFindings.recommendation: Use the q-form of the quadratic (cheap, strictly better near tangency, which IS the twilight regime) or correct the comment.

verdict.reasoning: Read the code myself and confirmed every element. (1) single_scatter.rs:222 and :408 compute `cos_theta = sun_dir.dot(-view_dir)` and pass it to henyey_greenstein_phase. (2) Conventions are unambiguous: view_dir points observer-to-sky (line 174: `scatter_pos = observer_pos + view_dir * s`), sun_dir points toward the sun (doc line 124; shadow rays traced along sun_dir; solar_direction_ecef in geometry.rs:282-304 returns away-from-observer vectors with Up=cos(sza)). So the physical scattering angle is cosΘ = (-sun_dir)·(-view_dir) = sun_dir·view_dir (standard Chandrasekhar/DISORT/Bruneton-Neyret convention, Θ=0 forward when looking at the sun); the code computes the supplement, giving backscatter toward the sun. The code's own comment (lines 220-221) states the correct physics that the code then violates. (3) No compensating convention: henyey_greenstein_phase (scattering.rs:32-36) is standard HG peaked at cosθ=+1 for g>0, and aerosol.rs:82-132 stores g=+0.68..+0.75. (4) Rayleigh phase is even in cosθ and all single_scatter.rs test atmospheres use rayleigh_fraction: 1.0 (lines 641, 657, 673, 1204, plus one more), so tests cannot detect the flip — exactly as claimed. (5) Same flip verified at photon.rs:425 (compute_nee; backward photon launched at the sun gives cos_angle=-1 instead of +1), 730 (Stokes NEE), 2468 (hybrid order-1, also feeding hg_mueller for the polarized path), 2863/3213/3926 (sun_dir.dot(-current_dir)), 4375 — so deterministic, hybrid, and backward-MC estimators are all consistently flipped; backward path-continuation sampling is reciprocity-safe so nothing cancels it. (6) Production geometry confirmed: twilight-cpu/src/pipeline.rs:574 sets view_zenith: 85.0 at the solar azimuth; at SZA 96, Θ=11°, HG(g=0.7) gives 12.95 vs 0.105 — I recomputed the ~123x ratio independently. Minor imprecisions only: the pipeline file is in twilight-cpu (finding didn't name the crate), and at SZA≳96° boundary-layer aerosols are mostly in shadow so the prayer-time impact is driven by elevated/stratospheric aerosol, clouds, and the SZA 90-96 part of the scan — but forward/backward scattering reversed for every forward-peaked scatterer in every estimator is unambiguously wrong physics that materially distorts radiance for any real (aerosol/cloud-laden) sky, hence the threshold-crossing SZA.

verdict.reasoning: Every code claim checks out on direct reading. (1) atmosphere.rs:102 initializes `refractive_index: [1.0; MAX_SHELLS], // default: no refraction`. (2) A repo-wide grep shows compute_refractive_indices / compute_refractive_indices_from_altitude are defined at atmosphere.rs:141/167 and called ONLY from #[cfg(test)] modules: single_scatter.rs:1231-1418 (test mod starts line 616), photon.rs:5720-5863 (test mod at 5008), atmosphere.rs:474+ (test mod at 208), twilight-gpu/buffers.rs:957+ (test mod at 437). (3) pipeline.rs build_atmosphere (lines 354-379) calls only twilight_data::builder::build_full / build_full_with_gas (builder.rs:386/424), neither of which contains any reference to refraction; compute_prayer_times (pipeline.rs:393-402) uses that atmosphere directly. The GPU path packs the same all-1.0 array (buffers.rs:172). (4) geometry.rs:216-218 confirms the identity fast path: `if libm::fabs(n_from - n_to) < 1e-15 { return RefractResult::Refracted(dir); }`, so every production ray is straight. (5) single_scatter.rs:279-281 indeed documents the shadow ray as following "the physically correct refracted path" — true only if the never-called setup method runs. The CLI's `atmos_refract: 0.5667` (twilight-cli/main.rs:462) is the NREL SPA horizon-refraction parameter for solar position at sunrise/sunset, not RT limb refraction, so it does not mitigate this. Physics reasoning holds: twilight RT models that resolve the terminator (Blättner et al. 1974 Monte Carlo twilight model; Rozenberg 1966 shadow-geometry treatment) include refraction because it lowers the Earth-shadow boundary at SZA 90+. One quantitative caveat: the cited "up to ~1.1 deg" bending applies to surface-grazing rays that are largely extinguished anyway; at the effective screening height (~10-20 km) bending is ~0.1-0.35 deg, so the net brightness-equivalent SZA bias is roughly 0.1-0.3 deg (~1-2 min of clock time at midlatitudes, more at high latitudes). That is still at or above the pipeline's own 0.1-deg fine-scan precision target (pipeline.rs doc, lines 385-387, "sub-minute precision"), so the systematic bias is material to the product's stated accuracy and high severity is justified.
verdict.correction: Finding is accurate as stated; only the magnitude framing needs tightening: the ~1.1 deg total bending applies to surface-tangent rays that are heavily extinct, so the effective bias from disabled refraction is ~0.1-0.3 deg in SZA (roughly 1-2 minutes of prayer-time shift), not a full degree — still larger than the pipeline's 0.1-deg fine-scan precision target. Additionally, atmosphere.rs:72-81 honestly documents that the default is "no refraction" and requires an explicit call, so this is dead-but-documented capability plus a misleading active-voice doc in single_scatter.rs:279-281, rather than outright fabrication.

reviewed.summary: The deep-twilight variance machinery (forced scattering, exponential transform, VSPG, Dwivedi MIS, weight-window splitting/RR) is individually weight-corrected and mostly sound, but the estimator as a whole is NOT the unbiased estimator the comments claim. The orders-2+ source function never applies the phase function between the incoming chain direction and the view direction (view_dir is not even passed to the chain tracers), the 3-branch initial-direction weights double-count the hemisphere baseline at deep twilight, the scalar/ALIS analog walk kills every chain at the first shell-boundary crossing (the Stokes twin correctly continues), and the NEE/order-1 scattering angle uses the supplement of the physical scattering angle (harmless for Rayleigh, wrong for HG aerosols and internally inconsistent with the BDPT light-vertex phase). On the maintainer's variance concern: the code's own comments document per-call CV of 0.4-1.2 at SZA 106-108 even with 4096-8192 BDPT subpaths, the CLI default is only 100 secondary rays/step with a 2-degree SZA grid, and seeds are deliberately decorrelated across SZA, so threshold-crossing (Fajr/Isha) estimates inherit minutes-level jitter; results are reproducible run-to-run (fixed sza-derived seeds) but the frozen noise shifts with any parameter change.

allFindings.title: Orders 2+ source function omits the phase coupling to the view direction — multiple scattering is computed against an ad-hoc sampling mixture, not the physical phase function
allFindings.why_wrong: The multiple-scattering source toward the observer is J(x,view)=∫ p(ω'→view)/4π · L(ω') dω' (standard backward MC with NEE, cf. MYSTIC/Mayer 2009, libRadtran). The chain's first direction is sampled from a 50/50 mix of [phase function centered on sun_dir] and [cos^n hemisphere around zenith / terminator lobe], with weights that correct only back to that heuristic mixture — the ratio p(ω'→view)/(4π·q(ω')) is never applied and view_dir never reaches the chain. The estimator therefore converges to ∫ q(ω')L(ω')dω' (radiance averaged under the sampling mixture), which equals the physical J only for isotropic L. At twilight L is strongly anisotropic, and at SZA>~100.5 the geometric shadow exceeds the TOA so order-1 is zero and this term is the ENTIRE signal at Fajr/Isha depression angles 15-18°. Rayleigh phase alone varies 0.75-1.5, so systematic radiance errors of tens of percent are plausible, shifting threshold-crossing times by minutes. Comments throughout claim the estimator is 'exactly unbiased', which is only true relative to the heuristic baseline, not the physics.
allFindings.recommendation: Pass view_dir into the chain tracers and multiply the chain's initial weight by p_x(dir·(-view_dir) with correct sign)/(4π·q_mix(dir)), where q_mix is the actual 3-branch mixture density (balance heuristic over the three proposals). All infrastructure (scalar_phase_value, MIS denominators) already exists for the later bounces; apply the same pattern to bounce 0.

allFindings.title: Scalar and ALIS analog walks terminate the whole chain at the first shell-boundary crossing (Stokes twin correctly continues); ground-bounce direction sampling is dead code
allFindings.evidence: if free_path >= boundary_dist { ... cross_boundary(...) ... if !is_outward && pos.length() <= surface_radius + 1.0 { ... weight *= albedo; current_dir = sample_hemisphere(normal, &mut local_rng.dir); scatter_found = false; break; } scatter_found = false; break; } ... if !scatter_found { break; }  // breaks the bounce loop -> chain dies
allFindings.why_wrong: In analog transport, a photon that reaches a shell boundary before its sampled free path must continue into the next shell with a fresh exponential sample (memoryless property) — exactly what trace_photon (line 327-357) and the Stokes trace_secondary_chain (lines 2789-2833, `continue`) do. In trace_secondary_chain_scalar and trace_secondary_chain_alis the boundary crossing sets scatter_found=false and breaks the walk loop, after which `if !scatter_found { break; }` kills the entire chain. Consequences: (1) every analog-mode bounce can only scatter within the current ~2 km shell (P of a few percent for typical visible free paths of tens of km), so multiple scattering is essentially annihilated whenever use_forced is false (SZA<96) and is lost for all ground-bound / tau>=20 / tau<forced_tau_min analog bounces at SZA>=96 — including the shafaq-relevant SZA 96-102 range; (2) after a ground bounce the freshly sampled Lambertian direction is discarded (dead code, RNG consumed), so all ground-reflected multiple scattering beyond the single immediate NEE term is lost; (3) it directly falsifies the docstring 'Identical physics to trace_secondary_chain' (line 2917) and the 'No bias is introduced' claim for thin analog paths (lines 828-831). Bias is always downward (radiance underestimated).
allFindings.recommendation: Replace the two `scatter_found = false; break;` sites with `continue` of the walk loop (or `continue` of the bounce loop to re-scout and re-enable forced scattering from the new position, which is strictly better). When fixing, also add a bounce cap or rely on weight-window RR: the scalar/ALIS bounce loops are unbounded `loop {}` (3053, 3700) unlike the Stokes version's BOUNCE_SAFETY_LIMIT (2713).

allFindings.title: 3-branch initial-direction weights are mutually inconsistent: terminator branch double-counts the hemisphere baseline (up to +50%) while the zenith branch under-weights it; truncation bias is mis-justified under the wrong measure
allFindings.why_wrong: For the documented baseline E = 0.5·E_phase + 0.5·E_hemi, the per-branch coefficients must satisfy alpha_z·c_z + alpha_t·c_t = 0.5 over a common support. The code gives alpha_z·[0.5/(alpha_z+alpha_t)] + alpha_t·[0.5/alpha_t] = 0.5·alpha_z/(alpha_z+alpha_t) + 0.5 > 0.5 — at deep twilight (alpha_z=alpha_t=0.475) the cosine-hemisphere component is weighted 0.75 inside the terminator lobe's support and only 0.25 outside it, instead of 0.5 everywhere. Separately, both lobes truncate the proposal at cos_min = max(0.2, ·) (power_cos_min, lines 913-926): directions with cos_theta below cos_min have ZERO sampling probability, so their baseline contribution (cos_min^2 of the cosine measure ≈ 4-8%, concentrated in near-horizontal directions where deep-twilight radiance actually peaks) is silently dropped, not reweighted. The comment justifies this with the removed mass under the power-cosine PROPOSAL (cos_min^(n+1) ≈ 5e-4), which is the wrong measure — truncating a proposal where the target has mass is bias, not a 'free IS design choice'.
allFindings.recommendation: Use a single balance-heuristic weight for all three branches: w(d) = 0.5·p_target(d) / (alpha_p·q_phase(d) + alpha_z·q_zen(d) + alpha_t·q_term(d)) with untruncated (or floor-mixed) proposals; this also removes the heavy-tail clamping motivation since the mixture denominator bounds weights naturally.

allFindings.title: NEE and order-1 evaluate the phase function at the supplement of the scattering angle; correct only for symmetric Rayleigh, wrong for HG aerosols/clouds, and internally inconsistent with the BDPT light-vertex phase
allFindings.why_wrong: The scattering angle is between incoming and outgoing PROPAGATION directions: for sun→scatter→observer, cosΘ = (-sun_dir)·(-view_dir) = sun_dir·view_dir (Bruneton & Neyret 2008 use ν = v·s; standard in libRadtran/DISORT geometry). The code computes sun_dir·(-view_dir) = -cosΘ, i.e. Θ→π-Θ: looking AT the sun yields cos=-1 (backscatter) instead of +1 (forward). henyey_greenstein_phase is the standard forward-peaked form (scattering.rs:32-36, verified by its own tests), so for aerosol/cloud shells (builder.rs mixes OPAC aerosol g into ShellOptics.asymmetry; clouds g=0.77-0.85) the forward peak is applied at the antisolar point — the sunward twilight arch (exactly where Fajr/Isha luminance comes from) is underestimated and the antisolar sky overestimated. Worse, within one BDPT connection product the eye-vertex phase uses the flipped convention (4620) while the light-vertex phase uses the standard one (4621), so the two are inconsistent regardless of which global convention is intended. Pure-Rayleigh runs (CLI default aerosol=none) are unaffected because Rayleigh is even in cosΘ.
allFindings.recommendation: Adopt the standard convention cosΘ = (propagation_in)·(propagation_out) everywhere: sun_dir·view_dir for order-1, sun_dir·current_dir for chain NEE, connection_dir·view_dir for the BDPT eye vertex; add a regression test with g=0.7 asserting the aureole appears toward the sun.

allFindings.title: Deep-twilight variance is large by the code's own measurements (CV 0.4-1.2 at SZA 106-108), defaults are 100 rays/step on a 2° SZA grid, and seeds are deliberately decorrelated across SZA — threshold crossings (prayer times) inherit minutes-level scatter
allFindings.why_wrong: At SZA > ~100.5 the geometric shadow height exceeds the 100 km TOA, so order-1 is zero and the luminance is 100% MC orders-2+. With per-call CV ~0.4-0.5 at SZA 106 (the code's own measurements) and luminance falling roughly 2.5-3x per degree of SZA, the threshold-crossing SZA has σ of order 0.3-0.5°, i.e. ~1.5-3 minutes of clock time. The pipeline amplifies this: (a) seeds are derived from sza_deg.to_bits() and deliberately DECORRELATED between scan steps, so adjacent grid points have independent noise — the opposite of the common-random-numbers technique that makes threshold crossings smooth; (b) determine_prayer_times linearly (log-)interpolates between two noisy points 2° apart (CLI default sza_step=2); (c) the documented 'heavy-tailed distribution' and 'CV 4+ outliers' mean single seeds can be dominated by one chain. Results are reproducible run-to-run (fixed seeds, single-threaded ALIS accumulation), but the frozen noise re-randomizes with any change of photon count, grid, or parameters — which is exactly the 'jitter' a maintainer observes.
allFindings.recommendation: Use common random numbers across the SZA scan (same base seed per scan, not sza-derived), average 8-16 independent seeds per SZA (CV scales as 1/sqrt(N)), fit log-luminance vs SZA (it is near-linear) over the whole scan before extracting the crossing, reduce sza_step to 0.25-0.5°, and raise the default secondary_rays well above 100. Longer term, the atmosphere is spherically symmetric per wavelength, so orders-2+ could be computed deterministically (successive orders of scattering in pseudo-spherical geometry, as in libRadtran), eliminating MC noise from prayer-time output entirely.

allFindings.title: trace_photon and the Stokes secondary chain apply single-scattering albedo AFTER NEE, while the scalar/ALIS chains correctly apply it BEFORE — the pure-MC and polarized paths overestimate radiance wherever ssa<1
allFindings.why_wrong: Collision points are sampled proportional to total extinction σ_t, so the NEE contribution at a collision must carry σ_s/σ_t = ssa (only scattering redirects sunlight to the observer); this is standard collision-estimator bookkeeping (e.g., MCNP/MYSTIC). The ALIS comment itself asserts the correct ordering. trace_photon, trace_photon_polarized and trace_secondary_chain (Stokes) omit one ssa factor in every NEE term, overestimating radiance by 1/ssa per scatter — material in the ozone Chappuis band (550-650 nm, ssa<1 in the 20-30 km shells), which dominates twilight zenith color. It also guarantees the polarized hybrid mode and the scalar/ALIS hybrid mode converge to different answers, contradicting the docstring 'Identical physics to trace_secondary_chain ... RNG consumption order is identical' (2916-2926) — the Stokes twin in fact also lacks VSPG, Dwivedi MIS, weight windows and the BDPT NEE down-weighting present in the scalar/ALIS versions.
allFindings.recommendation: Move `weight *= optics.ssa` before the NEE evaluation in trace_photon, trace_photon_polarized and trace_secondary_chain, and either bring the Stokes chain up to parity with the scalar tracer or correct its docstring to state the actual differences.

allFindings.title: BDPT light subpaths sample only a small terminator strip (r_frac in [0.97,1), phi within ±11.25°) yet the SZA-sigmoid blend hands BDPT ~100% of the order-2 estimate at deep twilight; the claim that both estimators 'compute exactly the same integral' is false and the stored pdf_fwd MIS machinery is dead code
allFindings.why_wrong: The entry sampling is a hard truncation of the illuminated TOA: sun entry points outside the strip have zero probability and the entry_weight (line 1659) normalizes only within the strip, so the BDPT estimator's expectation is the order-2 integral restricted to that strip — a strict underestimate. A convex blend w_bdpt·A + (1-w_bdpt)·B is unbiased only if A and B estimate the same quantity; here w_bdpt = bdpt_strength(SZA) → ~0.88-0.98 at SZA 105-108, so the full-domain NEE estimate is suppressed exactly where BDPT is truncated, and the systematic deficit grows smoothly with SZA — an SZA-dependent drift superimposed on the luminance curve used for threshold crossing. This is also not MIS in Veach's sense: weights are a global sigmoid of SZA, not per-path balance-heuristic ratios, despite pdf_fwd being computed and stored on every vertex (then marked dead_code).
allFindings.recommendation: Either widen/eliminate the truncation with proper importance weighting (e.g., exponential falloff in phi and r with finite density everywhere), or implement the per-path balance heuristic using the already-stored pdf_fwd so that NEE retains full weight for paths BDPT cannot generate.

allFindings.title: hg_mueller documentation contradicts the code: doc says P33=P34=P44=0 ('effectively unpolarizing') but the matrix is diag(p11,p11,p11,p11), which fully PRESERVES polarization
allFindings.evidence:
/// For the HG approximation, we set P22 = P11 (which is exact for spherical droplets...) and P12 = P33 = P34 = P44 = 0. This makes HG scattering effectively unpolarizing...
pub fn hg_mueller(cos_theta: f64, g: f64) -> MuellerMatrix { let p11 = henyey_greenstein_phase(cos_theta, g); MuellerMatrix { m: [[p11,0,0,0],[0,p11,0,0],[0,0,p11,0],[0,0,0,p11]] } }
allFindings.why_wrong: A diagonal Mueller matrix with all entries equal to P11 transmits Q, U, V unchanged relative to I (polarization-preserving, like an attenuator), which is the opposite of 'unpolarizing' (that would be M = diag(P11,0,0,0) or only M11 nonzero). P22=P11 is indeed exact for spheres (Mie theory, van de Hulst 1981; Hovenier & van der Mee 1983 give the symmetry relations), but P33=P44=P11 with P34=0 is an additional uncontrolled assumption, not what the comment describes. Impact on intensity is second-order (only via polarization cross-coupling at subsequent Rayleigh scatters in the polarized mode), so this is mainly a documentation/correctness-of-claims issue; the scalar production path is unaffected.
allFindings.recommendation: Make code and comment agree: for a deliberately depolarizing aerosol approximation use M = P11·diag(1, a, a, a) with a documented choice (a=0 depolarizing, or Mie-derived P33/P44 ratios from OPAC tables), and fix the doc text.

finding.title: Orders 2+ source function omits the phase coupling to the view direction — multiple scattering is computed against an ad-hoc sampling mixture, not the physical phase function
finding.why_wrong: The multiple-scattering source toward the observer is J(x,view)=∫ p(ω'→view)/4π · L(ω') dω' (standard backward MC with NEE, cf. MYSTIC/Mayer 2009, libRadtran). The chain's first direction is sampled from a 50/50 mix of [phase function centered on sun_dir] and [cos^n hemisphere around zenith / terminator lobe], with weights that correct only back to that heuristic mixture — the ratio p(ω'→view)/(4π·q(ω')) is never applied and view_dir never reaches the chain. The estimator therefore converges to ∫ q(ω')L(ω')dω' (radiance averaged under the sampling mixture), which equals the physical J only for isotropic L. At twilight L is strongly anisotropic, and at SZA>~100.5 the geometric shadow exceeds the TOA so order-1 is zero and this term is the ENTIRE signal at Fajr/Isha depression angles 15-18°. Rayleigh phase alone varies 0.75-1.5, so systematic radiance errors of tens of percent are plausible, shifting threshold-crossing times by minutes. Comments throughout claim the estimator is 'exactly unbiased', which is only true relative to the heuristic baseline, not the physics.
finding.recommendation: Pass view_dir into the chain tracers and multiply the chain's initial weight by p_x(dir·(-view_dir) with correct sign)/(4π·q_mix(dir)), where q_mix is the actual 3-branch mixture density (balance heuristic over the three proposals). All infrastructure (scalar_phase_value, MIS denominators) already exists for the later bounces; apply the same pattern to bounce 0.

verdict.reasoning: The code-level claim is accurate. (1) trace_secondary_chain_scalar (photon.rs:2940-2950) and trace_secondary_chain_alis (3563-3575) have no view_dir parameter; the Stokes variant receives view_dir as prev_dir_in (call at 2517) but uses it only for the polarization reference-plane rotation at 2662 and then normalizes the Stokes vector to I=1 (2672-2675), so no radiometric view coupling survives. (2) The initial chain direction is sampled from a 3-branch mixture — phase function centered on SUN_DIR (2639: scatter_direction(sun_dir, cos_theta_init, phi_init)), cos^n zenith lobe, terminator lobe — with weights (0.5/alpha_p etc., 2631-2657/2974-3000/3602-3625) that by the code's own comment (2620-2627) correct only back to the heuristic baseline E = 0.5*E_phase + 0.5*E_hemi; zenith_importance_weight (4791-4805) corrects to a cosine-weighted hemisphere, not to p(omega'->view)/4pi. (3) The drivers multiply the chain mean by beta_scat * t_obs * ds only (2529-2530, 2549-2550, 4473). Hence the chain estimator converges to int[0.5*p_sun/4pi + 0.5*cos(z)/pi (upper hemisphere)]*L domega', not the standard backward-MC source int p(omega'->view)/4pi * L domega' (Marchuk local estimate; MYSTIC/Mayer 2009) — exactly as the reviewer derived; it equals the physical J only for isotropic diffuse radiance. The order-1 code directly above (2468-2500) applies the correct phase(cos_theta_1)*INV_4PI toward the view, confirming the omission is an inconsistency, not a convention. The 'exactly unbiased' comments and especially the MIS comment at 4255-4256 ('backward chains and BDPT compute exactly the same multi-scattering integral') overstate correctness. HOWEVER, the reviewer's impact analysis overlooks the BDPT connection pass in the production ALIS path (4484-4666), which DOES apply the correct view-phase coupling — cos_theta_eye = connection_dir.dot(view_dir.scale(-1.0)) at 4620, phase_eye*INV_4PI at 4639-4650 — for order-2 paths (BDPT_MAX_LIGHT_VERTICES=1, line 1404), MIS-blended with w_bdpt = sigmoid((sza-102)/1.5) (1479-1484, 4259-4264) while the chain's order-2 NEE is downweighted by w_back (3226, 3932). At Fajr/Isha depressions 15-18 deg (SZA 105-108), w_bdpt is 0.88-0.98, so the dominant order-2 term is mostly computed with the physically correct kernel in the default unpolarized production path (twilight-cpu/simulation.rs:269, twilight-cli/main.rs:1509). The biased kernel still fully governs orders 3+ at all SZAs, ~50-80% of order 2 in the SZA 99-103 ramp (9-13 deg depression, relevant to 12/15-deg conventions), all MS below SZA 99, and the ENTIRE MS signal in polarized mode (hybrid_scatter_radiance at simulation.rs:291 has no BDPT and nee weight 1.0). Chain tests (6996-7097, 7544-7619) assert only non-negativity/finiteness, so nothing constrains this bias. Net effect: a real, undocumented systematic bias plausibly 10-30% of radiance in the affected components, translating to roughly tens of seconds up to ~2 minutes of threshold-crossing shift depending on convention and mode — significant, but not 'the entire signal at Fajr/Isha' as claimed, so critical overstates it for the default path.
verdict.correction: The orders-2+ backward chains (scalar, Stokes, and ALIS variants) genuinely omit the p(omega'->view)/(4pi*q) coupling: view_dir never enters the radiometric weight, and the branch weights correct only to an ad-hoc 0.5*sun-phase + 0.5*cosine-hemisphere baseline, so the chain term converges to a mixture-weighted average of the diffuse field (exact only for isotropic radiance). However, in the default production path (hybrid_scatter_radiance_alis) the dominant deep-twilight order-2 contribution is supplied by the BDPT connection pass (photon.rs:4593-4658), which correctly applies phase_eye(cos_theta_eye) toward view_dir, with MIS weight w_bdpt ~ 0.88-0.98 at SZA 105-108. The bias therefore fully affects orders 3+ everywhere, order 2 partially in the SZA 99-103 ramp and entirely below SZA 99, and ALL multiple scattering in polarized mode (hybrid_scatter_radiance has no BDPT). Expected impact is a systematic ~10-30% radiance bias in those components — on the order of tens of seconds to ~2 minutes in threshold-crossing times — not corruption of the entire Fajr/Isha signal. The MIS comment at 4255-4256 claiming the chains and BDPT 'compute exactly the same multi-scattering integral' is false and should be fixed along with the kernel (weight each chain by phase(-dir, view_dir)/(4pi*q_mix(dir))).

finding.title: Scalar and ALIS analog walks terminate the whole chain at the first shell-boundary crossing (Stokes twin correctly continues); ground-bounce direction sampling is dead code
finding.evidence: if free_path >= boundary_dist { ... cross_boundary(...) ... if !is_outward && pos.length() <= surface_radius + 1.0 { ... weight *= albedo; current_dir = sample_hemisphere(normal, &mut local_rng.dir); scatter_found = false; break; } scatter_found = false; break; } ... if !scatter_found { break; }  // breaks the bounce loop -> chain dies
finding.why_wrong: In analog transport, a photon that reaches a shell boundary before its sampled free path must continue into the next shell with a fresh exponential sample (memoryless property) — exactly what trace_photon (line 327-357) and the Stokes trace_secondary_chain (lines 2789-2833, `continue`) do. In trace_secondary_chain_scalar and trace_secondary_chain_alis the boundary crossing sets scatter_found=false and breaks the walk loop, after which `if !scatter_found { break; }` kills the entire chain. Consequences: (1) every analog-mode bounce can only scatter within the current ~2 km shell (P of a few percent for typical visible free paths of tens of km), so multiple scattering is essentially annihilated whenever use_forced is false (SZA<96) and is lost for all ground-bound / tau>=20 / tau<forced_tau_min analog bounces at SZA>=96 — including the shafaq-relevant SZA 96-102 range; (2) after a ground bounce the freshly sampled Lambertian direction is discarded (dead code, RNG consumed), so all ground-reflected multiple scattering beyond the single immediate NEE term is lost; (3) it directly falsifies the docstring 'Identical physics to trace_secondary_chain' (line 2917) and the 'No bias is introduced' claim for thin analog paths (lines 828-831). Bias is always downward (radiance underestimated).
finding.recommendation: Replace the two `scatter_found = false; break;` sites with `continue` of the walk loop (or `continue` of the bounce loop to re-scout and re-enable forced scattering from the new position, which is strictly better). When fixing, also add a bounce cap or rely on weight-window RR: the scalar/ALIS bounce loops are unbounded `loop {}` (3053, 3700) unlike the Stokes version's BOUNCE_SAFETY_LIMIT (2713).

verdict.reasoning: Read all cited code directly. In /Users/mostafamahdi/twilight/crates/twilight-core/src/photon.rs, trace_secondary_chain_scalar has nesting: while stack (3043) -> bounce loop (3053) -> analog walk `for _ in 0..200` (3099). When `free_path >= boundary_dist` (3137), the code applies the exponential-transform boundary weight (3138-3141), crosses the boundary (3143-3152), and then in BOTH branches sets `scatter_found = false; break;` (ground hit: 3154-3177 including dead `current_dir = sample_hemisphere(normal, ...)` at 3175 and `weight *= albedo` at 3174; non-ground: 3179-3180). The walk loop closes at 3194 and `if !scatter_found { break; }` (3196-3198) breaks the bounce loop, terminating the particle's chain (no labels exist in the file; verified breaks target innermost loops). trace_secondary_chain_alis is identical: boundary kill at 3818-3878 (dead sample_hemisphere at 3873), chain kill at 3901-3903 inside bounce loop at 3700. By contrast, the Stokes trace_secondary_chain handles the exact same case with `continue` at 2831/2833 (resampling a fresh free path in the new shell — correct memoryless analog transport per standard MC RT practice in piecewise-homogeneous layered media), as does trace_photon (continue at 354/357). The applied boundary weight correction and the resampled-but-discarded Lambertian direction prove the break is a bug, not intended truncation. Docstring falsification confirmed: lines 2916-2922 claim 'Identical physics to trace_secondary_chain' with identical RNG trajectories; lines 828-831 claim analog chains 'escape... or actually scatter... No bias is introduced' — both contradicted since the analog walk cannot cross a single non-empty shell boundary. Production relevance confirmed: scalar version is the default unpolarized path (call site 2536; polarized branch at 2514 uses the correct Stokes version), ALIS at 4442; ZENITH_SZA_START=96.0 (930), FORCED_TAU_CUTOFF=20.0 (815), forced_tau_min 0.05->0.02 (849-852), so at SZA<96 every bounce is analog and at SZA>=96 ground-bound/tau>=20/tau<ftm bounces are analog. Bias is systematically downward. Two wording quibbles that do not change the verdict: (1) 'essentially annihilated' is slightly overstated — near-horizontal directions have long in-shell chords (~160 km near tangent) and dense low shells scatter in-shell often, so MS is severely truncated/biased low rather than zeroed; (2) the finding actually understates one consequence — at SZA>=96 ground-bound analog walks mostly die at the first intermediate shell boundary and never reach the surface, so even the ground-bounce NEE term is lost except from the bottom shell. Severity high is right rather than critical: the deep-twilight SZA ~99-108 regime where Fajr/Isha thresholds are evaluated is mostly served by the forced-scatter branch (2718-2727), which is unaffected; the damage concentrates at SZA<96 (shafaq/civil range), in thin high-altitude analog paths, and in ground-coupled/dense chains.

finding.title: 3-branch initial-direction weights are mutually inconsistent: terminator branch double-counts the hemisphere baseline (up to +50%) while the zenith branch under-weights it; truncation bias is mis-justified under the wrong measure
finding.why_wrong: For the documented baseline E = 0.5·E_phase + 0.5·E_hemi, the per-branch coefficients must satisfy alpha_z·c_z + alpha_t·c_t = 0.5 over a common support. The code gives alpha_z·[0.5/(alpha_z+alpha_t)] + alpha_t·[0.5/alpha_t] = 0.5·alpha_z/(alpha_z+alpha_t) + 0.5 > 0.5 — at deep twilight (alpha_z=alpha_t=0.475) the cosine-hemisphere component is weighted 0.75 inside the terminator lobe's support and only 0.25 outside it, instead of 0.5 everywhere. Separately, both lobes truncate the proposal at cos_min = max(0.2, ·) (power_cos_min, lines 913-926): directions with cos_theta below cos_min have ZERO sampling probability, so their baseline contribution (cos_min^2 of the cosine measure ≈ 4-8%, concentrated in near-horizontal directions where deep-twilight radiance actually peaks) is silently dropped, not reweighted. The comment justifies this with the removed mass under the power-cosine PROPOSAL (cos_min^(n+1) ≈ 5e-4), which is the wrong measure — truncating a proposal where the target has mass is bias, not a 'free IS design choice'.
finding.recommendation: Use a single balance-heuristic weight for all three branches: w(d) = 0.5·p_target(d) / (alpha_p·q_phase(d) + alpha_z·q_zen(d) + alpha_t·q_term(d)) with untruncated (or floor-mixed) proposals; this also removes the heavy-tail clamping motivation since the mixture denominator bounds weights naturally.

verdict.reasoning: Read photon.rs myself. The quoted code is real and identical in all three chain variants: zenith branch_w = 0.5/(alpha_z+alpha_t), terminator branch_w = 0.5/alpha_t (Stokes 2640/2647/2655, scalar 2982/2991/2998, ALIS 3610/3616/3623), while the doc comment at 2620-2627 documents baseline E = 0.5*E_phase + 0.5*E_hemi with zenith weight 0.5/alpha_z — code contradicts its own spec. Both shape weights (zenith_importance_weight 4805-4814, terminator_shape_weight 4921-4936) convert to the cosine-hemisphere reference p_cos=cosθ/π, so the expected hemisphere-term coverage is p_cos·[0.5·alpha_z/(alpha_z+alpha_t)·1{supp_z} + 0.5·1{supp_t}], which at deep twilight (alpha_z=alpha_t=0.475, branch_params_for_sza 4851-4872) gives 0.75 in the lobe overlap, 0.25 in zenith-only support, 0.5 in terminator-only support, and 0 where neither lobe reaches — instead of 0.5 everywhere. The lobes overlap heavily (zenith cone half-angle ~74° at n=5; terminator cone ~65° around a 60°-tilted axis), so this is not a disjoint partition; even the commented 0.5/alpha_z would double-count the overlap — only a balance-heuristic mixture pdf (Veach MIS) or disjoint supports is unbiased. initial_weight multiplies chain weight directly (2681, 3037, 3682) with no downstream renormalization; the only related test (6623-6640) checks alpha sums, not weight consistency. The truncation claim also verifies: sample_zenith_biased (4769-4789) samples the truncated CDF on [cos_min,1] with cos_min = max(0.2, (2/(W(n+1)))^(1/n)) (913-926), and the weight's trunc_norm factor makes the estimator compute exactly ∫_{cosθ≥cos_min} p_cos·f, dropping the TARGET's mass cos_min² (4% at the 0.2 floor, 7.7% at n=5) — while the comment at 894-900 justifies it with the PROPOSAL's removed mass cos_min^(n+1)≈5e-4, the wrong measure; truncating a proposal inside the target's support is bias, not a free IS design choice. Two minor imprecisions in the finding: the terminator-only region coincidentally gets the correct 0.5 (and a zero-coverage region exists that the finding omits), and the dropped truncation mass is mostly anti-sunward near-horizontal directions (the sunward bright segment IS covered by the terminator lobe), so the truncation sub-claim's radiance-peak framing overstates impact. Neither caveat changes the core conclusion: the 3-branch initial-direction estimator is deterministically biased (not just high-variance), with distortion maximal exactly at SZA 105-108 where 15-18° Fajr/Isha thresholds are evaluated.
verdict.correction: Finding stands with two refinements: (1) coverage coefficients at deep twilight are 0.75 in the zenith/terminator lobe overlap, 0.25 in zenith-only support, 0.5 (correct) in terminator-only support, and 0 in above-horizon regions covered by neither lobe — not a simple 0.75-inside/0.25-outside split; (2) the truncation-dropped 4-8% of cosine-hemisphere target mass lies mostly in anti-sunward near-horizontal directions, since the sunward bright segment is covered by the terminator lobe, so its practical radiance impact is smaller than the raw mass figure suggests. The mixture-coefficient inconsistency remains the dominant bias.

finding.title: NEE and order-1 evaluate the phase function at the supplement of the scattering angle; correct only for symmetric Rayleigh, wrong for HG aerosols/clouds, and internally inconsistent with the BDPT light-vertex phase
finding.why_wrong: The scattering angle is between incoming and outgoing PROPAGATION directions: for sun→scatter→observer, cosΘ = (-sun_dir)·(-view_dir) = sun_dir·view_dir (Bruneton & Neyret 2008 use ν = v·s; standard in libRadtran/DISORT geometry). The code computes sun_dir·(-view_dir) = -cosΘ, i.e. Θ→π-Θ: looking AT the sun yields cos=-1 (backscatter) instead of +1 (forward). henyey_greenstein_phase is the standard forward-peaked form (scattering.rs:32-36, verified by its own tests), so for aerosol/cloud shells (builder.rs mixes OPAC aerosol g into ShellOptics.asymmetry; clouds g=0.77-0.85) the forward peak is applied at the antisolar point — the sunward twilight arch (exactly where Fajr/Isha luminance comes from) is underestimated and the antisolar sky overestimated. Worse, within one BDPT connection product the eye-vertex phase uses the flipped convention (4620) while the light-vertex phase uses the standard one (4621), so the two are inconsistent regardless of which global convention is intended. Pure-Rayleigh runs (CLI default aerosol=none) are unaffected because Rayleigh is even in cosΘ.
finding.recommendation: Adopt the standard convention cosΘ = (propagation_in)·(propagation_out) everywhere: sun_dir·view_dir for order-1, sun_dir·current_dir for chain NEE, connection_dir·view_dir for the BDPT eye vertex; add a regression test with g=0.7 asserting the aureole appears toward the sun.

verdict.reasoning: I read every cited line plus surrounding context and the finding is accurate on all points. (1) Direction semantics: sun_dir is documented "Direction toward the sun" (photon.rs:258) and used directly as the shadow-ray direction (photon.rs:415, 2466, 3210, 3925); view_dir/photon_dir/current_dir are backward-walk propagation directions away from the observer (scatter_pos = observer_pos + view_dir*s at photon.rs:2438/4348; single_scatter.rs:174). The physical scattering event is incoming propagation -sun_dir, outgoing -view_dir, so cosТ = sun_dir·view_dir (Bruneton & Neyret 2008 ν=v·s; standard in Nishita/libRadtran geometry). The code computes sun_dir·(-view_dir) = -cosТ at photon.rs:425 (and 730 in compute_nee_polarized, which the finding missed), 2468, 2863, 3213, 3926, 4375, and single_scatter.rs:222/408 — verified each is a sun-connection NEE/order-1 on a backward walk, so all are flipped. Sanity check: looking at the sun gives cos=-1 (HG minimum) instead of +1, placing the forward peak at the antisolar point. The comment at single_scatter.rs:219-221 shows the conceptual error (treats the vector TOWARD the sun as the incoming ray). (2) henyey_greenstein_phase (scattering.rs:32-36) is the standard forward-peaked form, confirmed by its own test hg_forward_peaked (scattering.rs:678-689); asymmetry is genuinely positive g (aerosols 0.68-0.75 in aerosol.rs:82-132, clouds 0.77/0.85 in cloud.rs:71-106, scattering-weighted mix in builder.rs:287-306/530-545) — no compensating negation exists. (3) BDPT inconsistency confirmed: trace_light_subpath is a forward trace from the sun (entry_dir = -sun_dir, photon.rs:1637) with lv.dir_in = physical arrival direction (photon.rs:1791-1795); connection_dir points eye→light vertex (diff = lv.pos - scatter_pos, 4596-4611). Line 4621 (lv.dir_in·(-connection_dir)) is the CORRECT standard cosТ for the light vertex while line 4620 (connection_dir·(-view_dir)) is flipped for the eye vertex (correct: connection_dir·view_dir); both multiply in one contribution (4643-4653), so the product is wrong for asymmetric phases under any single convention — the 'consistent alternate convention' defense fails. (4) Scope claim correct: Rayleigh phase 0.75(1+cos²θ) is even so scalar clear-sky runs are unaffected, and the CLI default is aerosol=none (twilight-cli/src/main.rs:96,146); aerosol/cloud/--weather runs are affected. Phase-function sampling along the walk (sample_henyey_greenstein + scatter_direction relative to the current direction) is correct by reciprocity, so the bug is isolated to NEE/order-1/BDPT-eye evaluation, exactly as the finding states.
verdict.correction: Finding is accurate as written. Minor additions: the same flip also exists at photon.rs:730 (compute_nee_polarized), and in the polarized path the flipped angle additionally corrupts the odd Mueller elements (P33/P44 ∝ cosθ) even for Rayleigh at scattering orders ≥2, though the dominant I-channel effect for pure Rayleigh remains negligible. Severity stays high (not critical) because the default clear-sky scalar configuration is unaffected; all aerosol, cloud, and live-weather runs are systematically biased (sunward twilight arch underestimated, antisolar sky overestimated).

finding.title: Deep-twilight variance is large by the code's own measurements (CV 0.4-1.2 at SZA 106-108), defaults are 100 rays/step on a 2° SZA grid, and seeds are deliberately decorrelated across SZA — threshold crossings (prayer times) inherit minutes-level scatter
finding.why_wrong: At SZA > ~100.5 the geometric shadow height exceeds the 100 km TOA, so order-1 is zero and the luminance is 100% MC orders-2+. With per-call CV ~0.4-0.5 at SZA 106 (the code's own measurements) and luminance falling roughly 2.5-3x per degree of SZA, the threshold-crossing SZA has σ of order 0.3-0.5°, i.e. ~1.5-3 minutes of clock time. The pipeline amplifies this: (a) seeds are derived from sza_deg.to_bits() and deliberately DECORRELATED between scan steps, so adjacent grid points have independent noise — the opposite of the common-random-numbers technique that makes threshold crossings smooth; (b) determine_prayer_times linearly (log-)interpolates between two noisy points 2° apart (CLI default sza_step=2); (c) the documented 'heavy-tailed distribution' and 'CV 4+ outliers' mean single seeds can be dominated by one chain. Results are reproducible run-to-run (fixed seeds, single-threaded ALIS accumulation), but the frozen noise re-randomizes with any change of photon count, grid, or parameters — which is exactly the 'jitter' a maintainer observes.
finding.recommendation: Use common random numbers across the SZA scan (same base seed per scan, not sza-derived), average 8-16 independent seeds per SZA (CV scales as 1/sqrt(N)), fit log-luminance vs SZA (it is near-linear) over the whole scan before extracting the crossing, reduce sza_step to 0.25-0.5°, and raise the default secondary_rays well above 100. Longer term, the atmosphere is spherically symmetric per wavelength, so orders-2+ could be computed deterministically (successive orders of scattering in pseudo-spherical geometry, as in libRadtran), eliminating MC noise from prayer-time output entirely.

verdict.reasoning: Code reading confirms every quoted snippet: the CV scaling-history comments at crates/twilight-core/src/photon.rs:1413-1421 (SZA 106 CV 0.641->0.545; 50-seed 0.370->0.262 at 8192 subpaths), the 'CV 4+ variance outliers' comment at 4255-4258, the RNG-stream-sensitivity/heavy-tail comment at 4501-4506, deliberate seed decorrelation across SZA steps at crates/twilight-cpu/src/simulation.rs:215-223 (and the hybrid path seeds from sza_deg.to_bits() at 266-267), and first-downcrossing log-interpolation in crates/twilight-threshold/src/threshold.rs:190-237. I then verified the conclusion empirically with the release binary. (1) Per-call noise: 10 runs each at SZA perturbed by 0.0001 deg (re-seeds completely, physics unchanged) gave mesopic-luminance CV ~0.13 at SZA 105 and 106 and ~0.44 at SZA 107 with one 2.4x heavy-tail outlier; luminance falls ~2.5-3x per degree as claimed. (2) Full pray pipeline jitter: Copenhagen (lat 55.7, 2026-03-01), photons 100-104 (five noise seeds): Fajr sigma ~28 s (spread 75 s), Isha abyad sigma ~36 s (spread 101 s). Lat 65: photons 100-103 (four seeds) gave Fajr 05:12:02 / 05:07:11 / 05:08:49 / 05:07:27 — a 4.9-minute spread (SZA sigma 0.23 deg) from changing the photon count by 1-3. So the headline (minutes-level, parameter-sensitive scatter in threshold crossings) is real and demonstrated. However, two supporting claims are wrong: (a) the prayer pipeline does NOT interpolate between points 2 deg apart — the Pray command defaults to sza_step=0.5 (twilight-cli/src/main.rs:142-144) and pipeline.rs:386-387,628-651 runs a second fine pass at 0.1 deg around each coarse crossing; the 2-deg default belongs only to the diagnostic Mcrt scan command (main.rs:80-82). The actual jitter mechanism is independent per-point noise on the 0.1-deg fine grid combined with first-crossing detection in determine_prayer_times, which both scatters and early-biases the crossing. (b) The 'CV 0.4-0.5 at SZA 106' figure overstates the current configuration — those numbers are scaling history at older subpath counts; measured current CV at SZA 105-106 is ~0.13 (it reaches ~0.44 only at SZA 107). Consequently the claimed sigma of 0.3-0.5 deg / 1.5-3 min is the worst case (deep crossings, high latitude), not the typical mid-latitude case (~0.06-0.09 deg, ~0.5 min sigma).
verdict.correction: The core issue is real but the mechanism and magnitudes need correcting. Accurate statement: the hybrid MC estimator has per-call CV ~0.13 at SZA 105-106 and ~0.44 (heavy-tailed) at SZA 107 in the current default configuration (measured; the 0.4-1.2 figures in photon.rs comments are scaling history at older subpath counts). Seeds are derived from sza_deg.to_bits() and deliberately decorrelated across scan steps, so every scan point carries independent frozen noise. The prayer pipeline scans coarse at 0.5 deg (not 2 deg — that default is only the Mcrt diagnostic command) and refines at 0.1 deg around each crossing, but because the 0.1-deg fine points have independent noise and determine_prayer_times takes the first downcrossing, the crossing both scatters and biases early. Measured end-to-end: changing only the photon count (100->104) moves Fajr/Isha by sigma ~30-40 s (spread up to ~1.7 min) at lat 55.7, and at lat 65 Fajr spread reaches 4.9 minutes across four seeds (SZA sigma 0.23 deg). Results are bit-reproducible for fixed parameters, but the frozen noise re-randomizes with any change of photon count, grid, or location — minutes-level jitter at high latitude, sub-minute to ~1.5 min typically. Mitigations: common random numbers or correlated seeds across SZA steps, averaging multiple independent seeds per SZA, and robust (e.g., monotone-fit) crossing detection instead of first-downcrossing.

reviewed.summary: The production path is largely sound: the tabulated O3 (verified value-for-value against the in-repo Serdyuchenko raw file, correct 293K-first column order, tau(602nm,300DU)=0.041), NO2, and O4 CIA data have correct units and conventions; apply_gas_absorption's extinction/SSA renormalization preserves scattering correctly; the Dobson-unit scaling and the negative-cross-section clamp (justified: 69 real negative noise points exist in the 193K Serdyuchenko data near 382nm) are fine. However, the runtime line-by-line Voigt path -- which is publicly exported, advertised as 'more accurate than the tabulated cross-sections', and used by nothing in the engine -- contains a 100x Doppler-width unit error enshrined by a test, a Voigt evaluator that blows up by orders of magnitude for small y while falsely claiming to be Humlicek-w4/Weideman at 1e-4 accuracy, and a partition-function exponent that is wrong for O2. Separately, twilight-data ships a fabricated 'Serdyuchenko' O3 table that is 100x too small (dead code today, a landmine if wired in), the O2/H2O tables are aliased point samples of narrow lines rather than band averages, and the NO2 profile omits the stratospheric layer that dominates twilight-geometry absorption.

allFindings.title: twilight-data ozone_xsec.rs is a fabricated 'Serdyuchenko' table with Chappuis values 100x too small, contradicting its own doc comment
allFindings.evidence: Doc claims: "Source: Serdyuchenko, A., et al. (2014)" and "The Chappuis band peaks near 600 nm with sigma ~ 5.0e-21 cm^2" -- yet the table reads: "// 560-610 nm: Chappuis band peak region\n4.95e-23, 5.05e-23, 5.10e-23, 5.08e-23, 5.01e-23, ..." and the in-file test pins the wrong magnitude: "assert!(sigma_580 > 4e-23 && sigma_580 < 6e-23, \"Chappuis peak sigma(580nm) = {:.4e}, expected ~5e-23\""
allFindings.why_wrong: The actual Serdyuchenko et al. (2014, AMT 7, 625) Chappuis peak is sigma(602nm, 293K) = 5.11e-21 cm^2 -- I verified this directly against the raw data file shipped in this repo (data/xsec/SerdyuchenkoGorshelev5digits_latest.dat: 602.0 -> 5.10875e-21) and against the correctly generated O3_XS table in gas_absorption_data.rs (5.1088e-21). Every value in ozone_xsec.rs is ~100x too small (wrong exponent, e-23 instead of e-21), and the values are smooth hand-rolled numbers, not actual Serdyuchenko data. The module's own line-23 doc comment states the correct 5.0e-21 figure, contradicting the table 12 lines below it. If this table were used, O3 Chappuis optical depth would drop from ~0.04 to ~0.0004, materially brightening modeled twilight and shifting Fajr/Isha threshold times. Mitigating factor: the module is dead code -- grep shows it is only declared in lib.rs:7 and called by nothing.
allFindings.recommendation: Delete the module, or regenerate it from the real Serdyuchenko file (the repo already has both the data and a correct generator in tools/gen_gas_xsec.py). Fix the tests, which currently codify the 100x error.

allFindings.title: doppler_halfwidth mixes m/s and cm/s, producing Doppler widths exactly 100x too small; a unit test asserts the wrong value
allFindings.evidence: const C_CGS: f64 = 2.99792458e10; // cm/s ... let factor = libm::sqrt(2.0 * R * LN2 / m_kg_per_mol); nu0 / C_CGS * factor * libm::sqrt(temp_k)  -- and the test: "let gamma_d = doppler_halfwidth(13123.0, 296.0, 31.9988); assert!(gamma_d > 1e-4 && gamma_d < 2e-4, \"O2 Doppler HW at 762nm: {:.6e} cm^-1, expected ~1.4e-4\");"
allFindings.why_wrong: sqrt(2*R*T*ln2/M) with R in J/(mol K) and M in kg/mol yields a speed in m/s (~326 m/s for O2 at 296K), but it is divided by c expressed in cm/s (2.998e10). The result is gamma_D = 1.43e-4 cm^-1, while the standard formula (e.g. HITRAN convention, gamma_D = (nu0/c)*sqrt(2 ln2 kT/m); cross-check FWHM = 7.16e-7*nu0*sqrt(T/M_amu)) gives 1.43e-2 cm^-1 for the O2 A-band -- I verified the ratio is exactly 100.000. The test at lines 1294-1309 repeats the same unit slip in its derivation comment and pins the wrong value, so the bug is self-consistently enshrined. Consequence: in o2/h2o_cross_section_lbl the Voigt y parameter is 100x too large, forcing pure-Lorentzian line shapes even at stratospheric pressures where lines are Doppler-dominated (peak cross-sections inflated by ~gamma_D/gamma_L). Mitigating factors: the Voigt profile remains area-normalized regardless of gamma_D, and the LBL functions are called by nothing outside this file's tests (the engine uses the HAPI-generated tables), yet the module doc (line 18-19) advertises this path and o2_cross_section_lbl's doc claims it 'is more accurate than the tabulated cross-sections'.
allFindings.recommendation: Use c = 2.99792458e8 m/s (or convert the speed to cm/s) and fix the test to assert ~1.43e-2 cm^-1. Alternatively delete the unused LBL path entirely.

allFindings.title: weideman_voigt continued fraction is numerically unstable near the real axis: relative errors up to 8e4 for y=1e-6, 8x for y=0.01, 33% for y=0.1
allFindings.evidence: if y < 1e-6 { return libm::exp(-x * x); } ... let n_terms: usize = if s > 6.0 { 20 } else if s > 3.0 { 30 } else if s > 1.5 { 40 } else if s > 0.5 { 60 } else { 80 };
allFindings.why_wrong: I replicated the algorithm exactly in Python and compared against scipy.special.wofz (reference Faddeeva): max relative error is 7.8e4 at (x=0, y=1e-6), 86x at y=1e-3, 8.3x at y=1e-2, 107% at y=0.05, 33% at y=0.1; only for y >= ~0.3 does it reach sub-1% accuracy. This is the well-known failure mode of the truncated Laplace continued fraction: its poles lie on the real axis (it is equivalent to a Gauss-Hermite quadrature rational), so no fixed term count converges as y -> 0 -- which is precisely why Humlicek (1982) introduced dedicated region-IV rational approximations near the real axis. The y < 1e-6 Gaussian cutoff leaves the entire 1e-6 < y < 0.3 band broken. Physically, y ~ 0.01-0.3 corresponds to Doppler-dominated stratospheric lines (P <= ~100 hPa with correct gamma_D), exactly the regime a twilight model traverses. Currently this regime is masked only because the doppler-halfwidth-100x bug inflates y by 100x -- the two bugs accidentally cancel into 'plausible-looking' Lorentzian output.
allFindings.recommendation: Replace with a genuine Humlicek (1982) w4 implementation, Weideman (1994) N=24/32 rational series, or Zaghloul-Ali (2011); validate against wofz over y in [1e-8, 1e3] before use.

allFindings.title: Voigt code claims Humlicek (1982) w4 and Weideman (1994) N=32 with ~1e-4 accuracy, but implements neither; contains LLM conversational artifact
allFindings.evidence: "Uses the Humlicek (1982) w4 algorithm: a 4-region rational approximation accurate to ~1e-4 relative error for all (x, y >= 0)" ... "// Humlicek's region 2 formula uses: w = t1 / (0.5625 + t) where t1 and t are complex expressions. Let me use the known 2-term rational approximation." ... "/// Weideman (1994) N=32 approximation for the Faddeeva function. ... Actually uses the simpler approach: transform to w(z) via the Laplace continued fraction"
allFindings.why_wrong: Humlicek w4's region boundaries (s>=15, s>=5.5, y >= 0.195|x| - 0.176) are copied, but none of Humlicek's rational approximants are present: region 1 is a one-term asymptotic series (measured error up to 0.44% near s=15, not 1e-4), region 2 is a two-term asymptotic (up to 0.91% error, e.g. x=12,y=3), and regions 3 and 4 both fall through to the same continued fraction -- making the region-3/4 branch at line 339 dead logic. The function named weideman_voigt admits in its own doc that it is not Weideman 1994 ('Actually uses the simpler approach'), and 'N=32' appears nowhere (term counts are 20-80). Measured discontinuities at the s=5.5 and s=15 seams are 0.2-0.9%, contradicting the 1e-4 claim by ~two orders of magnitude. The 'Let me use the known...' comment at line 317 is an unedited LLM drafting artifact. The attributions and the accuracy figure are fabricated; the underlying CF is a real method but misdescribed and (per voigt-cf-small-y-blowup) inadequate.
allFindings.recommendation: Rewrite the doc comments to describe what is actually implemented, or implement the cited algorithms. Remove the conversational comment.

allFindings.title: O2/H2O tables are HAPI point samples on a 1-nm grid (lines ~0.05 cm^-1 wide vs ~25 cm^-1 spacing), then point-sampled again at the engine's 41-point/10-nm grid -- no band averaging
allFindings.evidence: wn_grid = np.sort(WAVENUMBERS_CM)  # ascending ... nu, coef = absorptionCoefficient_Voigt(SourceTables=table_name, Environment={'p': p_atm, 'T': t_k}, WavenumberGrid=wn_grid, HITRAN_units=True)
allFindings.why_wrong: HAPI evaluates the cross-section AT the supplied grid points with a default wing cutoff of 50 HWHM (~2.5-5 cm^-1 at 1 atm), while the 1-nm grid spacing is ~17-33 cm^-1. Result, verified in the generated data: at sea level only 39 of 401 O2 grid points are nonzero, and adjacent points in the A-band swing >4 orders of magnitude (761nm: 2.829e-23; 762nm: 3.289e-27). The engine then samples this aliased table at its 10-nm DEFAULT_WAVELENGTHS_NM grid (760nm -> 1.6e-25, giving vertical tau~0.7 treated as representative of a 10-nm bin, where the true band-averaged A-band is nearly black at its center). Standard practice for line absorbers on coarse spectral grids is bin-averaged cross-sections, a band model, or correlated-k (cf. libRadtran REPRAN/correlated-k; DISORT inputs are band-averaged) -- point sampling of unresolved lines yields essentially arbitrary values. Materiality is limited for prayer times because CIE V(lambda)/V'(lambda) weight beyond 700 nm is <1e-4 of peak and the affected H2O/O2 bands (628, 688, 720, 760 nm) carry little visual weight, while the dominant visible absorbers (O3 Chappuis continuum, NO2, O4 CIA) are smooth measured data handled correctly -- hence medium, not high.
allFindings.recommendation: Generate bin-averaged cross-sections: have HAPI compute on a fine grid (e.g. 0.01 cm^-1) and average over each 1-nm (or directly each 10-nm engine) bin; note that averaging transmission rather than cross-section is the rigorous target for thick bands (correlated-k).

allFindings.title: Partition-function ratio (T_ref/T)^1.5 is wrong for O2 (linear molecule, Q_rot ~ T^1) and the '<1% for a diatomic' accuracy claim is false (~19% at 210 K)
allFindings.evidence: /// We approximate Q(T_ref)/Q(T) ~ (T_ref/T)^1.5 for a diatomic, /// which is accurate to <1% for the temperature range of interest. ... let q_ratio = libm::pow(T_REF * inv_t, 1.5);
allFindings.why_wrong: The HITRAN line-intensity conversion uses the total internal partition sum (translation cancels). For a linear/diatomic molecule the classical rotational partition function scales as T^1 (Herzberg; Gamache et al. 2017 TIPS): O2 TIPS gives Q(296)=215.8, Q(210)~153, ratio 1.41 = (296/210)^1.0, whereas the code computes (296/210)^1.5 = 1.674 -- an ~19% overestimate of O2 line intensity at 210 K (~9% at 250 K). The exponent 3/2 is correct only for nonlinear molecules like H2O, so the shared helper is right for the H2O path and wrong for O2, the opposite of what the comment asserts. (Note: this contradicts the orchestrator seed, which had the convention reversed -- linear -> ^1, nonlinear -> ^1.5 is the standard.) Affects only the unused LBL path; the tabulated O2_XS/H2O_XS were produced by HAPI, which uses exact TIPS.
allFindings.recommendation: Pass a per-species exponent (1.0 for O2, 1.5 for H2O), or interpolate actual TIPS Q(T) values; correct the comment either way.

allFindings.title: NO2 profile decays monotonically from the surface and omits the stratospheric NO2 layer that dominates absorption in twilight geometry
allFindings.why_wrong: Standard trace-gas climatologies (AFGL, Anderson et al. 1986, as used by libRadtran/DISORT-family models) place a stratospheric NO2 maximum of roughly (1-4)e9 molecules/cm^3 = (1-4)e15 m^-3 near 25-35 km, contributing a stratospheric column of ~2-3e15 cm^-2 that typically exceeds the clean-background tropospheric column. This profile has 5e10 m^-3 at 25 km and 1e10 m^-3 at 30 km -- about 5 orders of magnitude below climatology -- and integrates to only ~1e15 cm^-2 total, nearly all below 5 km. In twilight geometry (sun 9-18 deg below horizon) the troposphere is in the Earth's shadow and the sunlit grazing path runs through the stratosphere, so NO2 absorption of blue light along the lit path is almost entirely missed; the builder's NO2 surface-density override (builder.rs:472-481) rescales this wrongly-shaped profile, putting observation-driven NO2 at the wrong altitudes. NO2 is a secondary absorber relative to O3 Chappuis, so the prayer-time shift is moderate rather than dominant.
allFindings.recommendation: Adopt the AFGL midlatitude NO2 profile (or similar) with the stratospheric peak; treat the surface override as a tropospheric perturbation on top of a fixed stratospheric layer.

allFindings.title: Entire runtime LBL path (voigt_humlicek, weideman_voigt, o2/h2o_cross_section_lbl) and the generated GAMMA_SELF arrays are dead code shipped as capability
allFindings.evidence: Module doc lines 18-19: "For O2 and H2O, line parameters are also stored for optional runtime line-by-line Voigt computation via the Humlicek (1982) algorithm." -- grep confirms o2_cross_section_lbl/h2o_cross_section_lbl/voigt_humlicek are referenced nowhere outside this file, and O2_LINE_GAMMA_SELF/H2O_LINE_GAMMA_SELF appear only in gas_absorption_data.rs.
allFindings.why_wrong: ~2000 line-parameter constants (including 481 O2 + 1586 H2O gamma_self values) and ~370 lines of Voigt/LBL code are compiled into every build but never called by the engine; the only consumers are the module's own tests, several of which assert physically wrong values (see doppler-halfwidth-100x-units). lorentz_halfwidth (lines 479-491) also ignores self-broadening entirely -- for H2O at ~1.5% VMR with gamma_self ~ 5x gamma_air that is a ~7% halfwidth underestimate, marginal but contrary to the HITRAN convention gamma = (P-p_self)*gamma_air + p_self*gamma_self. gen_gas_xsec.py's compute_hitran_xsec_2d also takes molecule_id/isotope_id arguments it never uses.
allFindings.recommendation: Either delete the LBL path and GAMMA_SELF emission, or fix its three physics bugs, wire it in behind a feature, and include self-broadening for H2O.

verdict.reasoning: Read gas_absorption.rs lines 493-646 and 1280-1340 myself. The code at lines 519-525 computes sqrt(2*R*T*ln2/M) with R=8.314462618 J/(mol·K) and M in kg/mol — a speed in m/s (~326.6 m/s for O2 at 296 K) — then divides by C_CGS = 2.99792458e10 cm/s.
