But the functions are pub, the doc at lines 530-532 claims the LBL path "is more accurate than the tabulated cross-sections", and the module doc (lines 18-19) advertises it. Every element of the finding — code behavior, physics, test, consequence, and mitigations — is accurate. Severity high is right: zero impact on shipped prayer times (so not critical), but a real 100x unit error in a public, documented-as-superior API, enshrined by a wrong test.

finding.title: weideman_voigt continued fraction is numerically unstable near the real axis: relative errors up to 8e4 for y=1e-6, 8x for y=0.01, 33% for y=0.1
finding.evidence: if y < 1e-6 { return libm::exp(-x * x); } ... let n_terms: usize = if s > 6.0 { 20 } else if s > 3.0 { 30 } else if s > 1.5 { 40 } else if s > 0.5 { 60 } else { 80 };
finding.why_wrong: I replicated the algorithm exactly in Python and compared against scipy.special.wofz (reference Faddeeva): max relative error is 7.8e4 at (x=0, y=1e-6), 86x at y=1e-3, 8.3x at y=1e-2, 107% at y=0.05, 33% at y=0.1; only for y >= ~0.3 does it reach sub-1% accuracy. This is the well-known failure mode of the truncated Laplace continued fraction: its poles lie on the real axis (it is equivalent to a Gauss-Hermite quadrature rational), so no fixed term count converges as y -> 0 -- which is precisely why Humlicek (1982) introduced dedicated region-IV rational approximations near the real axis. The y < 1e-6 Gaussian cutoff leaves the entire 1e-6 < y < 0.3 band broken. Physically, y ~ 0.01-0.3 corresponds to Doppler-dominated stratospheric lines (P <= ~100 hPa with correct gamma_D), exactly the regime a twilight model traverses. Currently this regime is masked only because the doppler-halfwidth-100x bug inflates y by 100x -- the two bugs accidentally cancel into 'plausible-looking' Lorentzian output.
finding.recommendation: Replace with a genuine Humlicek (1982) w4 implementation, Weideman (1994) N=24/32 rational series, or Zaghloul-Ali (2011); validate against wofz over y in [1e-8, 1e3] before use.

verdict.reasoning: I read crates/twilight-core/src/gas_absorption.rs lines 269-526 and replicated weideman_voigt and the voigt_humlicek region dispatch exactly in Python against scipy.special.wofz. The reviewer's numbers reproduce almost digit-for-digit: max relative error 7.83e4 at (x=0, y=1e-6) — the code returns K=78325 where the true Voigt K is bounded by 1 — 85x at y=1e-3, 9.6x at y=1e-2, 107% at y=0.05, 33% at y=0.1, 4.3% at y=0.2, and sub-1% only for y >= ~0.3. The code truly does what the finding says: line 373 cuts to a Gaussian only for y < 1e-6, lines 391-401 cap the Laplace continued fraction at 80 terms, and lines 339-356 route everything with |x|+y < 5.5 into this CF, so the whole 1e-6 < y < ~0.2 band is broken. The mechanism cited is standard literature: the truncated Laplace CF is a rational function with poles at Hermite zeros on the real axis, so no fixed truncation converges as y->0, which is exactly why Humlicek (1982) introduced a dedicated region-IV approximation and why the docstring's claim of 'Humlicek w4, ~1e-4 accuracy for all (x, y>=0)' (lines 274-275) is false — the function is also misnamed, since it is not Weideman (1994) at all despite the comment at lines 349-350. The masking claim is also verified: doppler_halfwidth (lines 519-525) divides a thermal speed in m/s by c in cm/s (C_CGS=2.99792458e10), giving gamma_D = 1.429e-4 cm^-1 for the O2 A-band at 296 K vs the correct HITRAN value 1.429e-2 cm^-1 (exactly 100x small; the unit test at lines 1294-1309 even asserts the wrong value). This inflates y by 100x, so at the tabulation grid pressures (PT_PRESSURES_HPA down to 50 hPa, gas_absorption_data.rs:4486) y_buggy ~ 14-291 lands in the CF's accurate range, masking the blowup; with gamma_D corrected, y at 100/50/12 hPa is 0.29/0.16/0.034, squarely in the broken band. Severity 'high' is right rather than 'critical': as shipped, the broken band is only reached for P below ~1 hPa because of the masking bug, so current output is dominated by the gamma_D error, but the routine is an unambiguous correctness bug (returns 7.8e4 where the true function is <=1, plus a 7.8e4-magnitude discontinuity at the y=1e-6 cutoff) and becomes fully exposed in the stratosphere the moment the Doppler bug is fixed.

reviewed.summary: The aerosol data layer is genuinely sound: all six OPAC types have AOD/SSA/g/Angstrom values within Hess 1998 / Dubovik 2002 ranges, the Angstrom-law extinction and exponential profile are correctly normalized (beta_0 = AOD/H verified), and aerosol optics are correctly mixed into the 50-shell model and packed into both the CPU path and the Metal GPU buffers. Clouds are NOT decorative at the data level — cloud optics reach the shells, the CLI, the weather mapping, and the GPU buffer packing — but the radiative-transfer estimators cannot transport light through any cloud of optical depth >~1: the MC/hybrid source term fails to recover diffuse transmission, luminance under stratus is ~1e-15 of clear sky (physically it should be a factor of ~2-10), L(SZA) becomes non-monotonic by 11 orders of magnitude, and `pray --cloud` collapses Fajr/Isha to depression ~0 degrees (dawn at sunrise) for 5 of the 6 advertised cloud types. The headline claim "Your prayer app doesn't know if it's cloudy" is therefore unmet: only thin-cirrus produces usable (and likely over-darkened) times. Secondary issues: clouds use a bare single-term Henyey-Greenstein phase function with no Mie/delta-scaling, cirrus SSA of 0.96-0.97 in the visible is non-physical, and the weather mapping scales cloud OD by cover^0.7 instead of the standard independent-column mixing. The crates/twilight-clouds directory is an empty husk (no Cargo.toml, no sources, not a workspace member).

allFindings.title: RT estimator cannot transport light through clouds of OD >~ 1: prayer times collapse to sunrise for 5 of 6 cloud types
allFindings.why_wrong: Every line-of-sight contribution is weighted by direct-beam transmittance t_obs = exp(-tau) from the observer; through an OD-10 stratus at 75-deg view zenith that is e^-38 ~ 1.7e-17, and the diffuse light that should dominate (delta-Eddington/two-stream diffuse transmittance of a tau=10, g=0.85 cloud is T ~ 1/(1+0.75*tau*(1-g)) ~ 0.47, i.e. ~50%) can only be rebuilt by the MC secondary chains. Under twilight geometry those chains must random-walk from inside/below the cloud up to the sunlit layer (~35-60 km at SZA 96-98) before any NEE survives shadow_ray_transmittance, which is essentially never sampled — the importance-sampling branches (branch_params_for_sza/dwivedi_frac, tuned 'At SZA <= 96: alpha_p=0.5, alpha_z=0.5', photon.rs:2973) were designed for clear-sky Rayleigh atmospheres. The result is a broken/firefly estimator: non-monotonic L(SZA) and prayer times wrong by 60-90 minutes (Fajr reported at sunrise). Real overcast twilight is darker by roughly one order of magnitude (cf. MYSTIC/libRadtran twilight studies; measured overcast twilight illuminance), shifting threshold times by minutes, not collapsing them. Additionally only ~200 LOS steps (HYBRID_LOS_STEPS=200, photon.rs:795) span a ~330 km LOS, so the cloud's ~4 km slant extent gets 2-3 quadrature points with tau jumps of ~19 per step. README's headline ("Your prayer app doesn't know if it's cloudy", README.md:13) and feature list ("Cloud layers (6 types)") are contradicted for thick-cirrus, altostratus, stratus, stratocumulus and cumulus — only thin-cirrus (OD 0.3) yields a usable time, and even there the MC adds <0.1% of radiance so the 10-minute delay is pure Beer-Lambert dimming and almost certainly overestimated.
allFindings.recommendation: Treat cloudy skies with a method that actually converges: either (a) an adding-doubling/two-stream (delta-Eddington) solution for the cloud layer coupled to the clear-sky MC above it, or (b) proper next-event estimation with distance sampling inside the cloud plus a diffusion/similarity-theory approximation for high orders. At minimum, detect cloud OD > ~1 and refuse/fall back rather than emitting depression-0 prayer times. Add an integration test asserting L(SZA) is monotonically decreasing through twilight for every cloud preset and that L_cloudy/L_clear stays within physical bounds (1e-3..1).

allFindings.title: Clouds use a single-term Henyey-Greenstein phase function (no Mie, no delta-scaling)
allFindings.why_wrong: Single-term HG is a standard and acceptable approximation for OPAC aerosols, but cloud droplets (size parameter x >> 1, r_eff ~ 5-15 um) have a Mie phase function with a diffraction forward peak containing roughly half the scattered energy within a few degrees, plus fogbow/glory backscatter — HG(g=0.85) spreads that peak over tens of degrees and misses the backscatter structure entirely. Production RT codes (DISORT/libRadtran with Hu & Stamnes water-cloud parameterizations, MYSTIC with exact Mie tables) use Mie phase functions for clouds, or at minimum delta-scaled HG (Joseph, Wiscombe & Weinman 1976 delta-Eddington) so the unresolved forward peak is folded into the extinction. Here the unscaled HG also makes the broken MC estimator (finding cloud-rt-collapse) worse: forward-peaked sampling keeps chains inside the cloud instead of letting near-forward 'diffraction' photons effectively pass through. Note the per-shell single (g, rayleigh_fraction) pair also forces aerosol and cloud to share one HG lobe in overlapping shells.
allFindings.recommendation: Implement delta-scaling (tau' = (1-w0 f) tau, g' = (g-f)/(1-f) with f = g^2) as a minimum fix for cloud shells, or embed tabulated Mie phase functions (e.g. from libRadtran's wc/ic properties or a bundled Mie code) selectable per shell. Keep HG for aerosols.

allFindings.title: Cirrus SSA of 0.96-0.97 in the visible is non-physical; ice is non-absorbing at these wavelengths and the doc justification is fabricated physics
allFindings.why_wrong: The imaginary refractive index of ice at 380-780 nm is ~1e-9 to 1e-8 (Warren & Brandt 2008), so cirrus single-scattering albedo in the visible is >0.9999 — effectively 1.0, same as liquid water (OPAC/Hess 1998 cirrus models give SSA ~= 1.0 at 0.55 um; ditto Yang et al. ice optical property libraries). SSA ~0.96 is characteristic of cirrus in the near-IR (1.6/2.2 um), not the visible. The stated justification — lower SSA 'due to non-spherical crystal shapes' — is wrong physics: crystal habit affects the phase function and asymmetry parameter, not absorption. Injecting 3-4% absorption per scattering event artificially darkens the multiply-scattered sky under cirrus (for thick cirrus OD 2 this is a ~10% radiance error, on top of the estimator problems). The test `cirrus_lower_ssa_than_water_clouds` (cloud.rs:188-197) bakes the error in.
allFindings.recommendation: Set cirrus SSA to 0.9999 (or 1.0) across 380-780 nm, keep the lower asymmetry (g~0.75-0.80 is correct for ice habits), fix the module doc, and delete/invert the cirrus_lower_ssa_than_water_clouds test.

allFindings.title: Weather mapping scales cloud OD by cover^0.7 instead of the standard independent-column (clear/cloudy mixing) treatment, and collapses multi-layer cover to one layer
allFindings.why_wrong: The conventional treatment of fractional cloud cover in 1-D RT (libRadtran, GCM radiation schemes) is the independent column approximation: compute the clear and overcast radiances separately and mix linearly by cover fraction, because radiance is strongly nonlinear in tau. Smearing OD as tau*N^0.7 turns 50% broken stratus (half the sky clear, half OD 10) into a uniform OD-6.2 overcast — a qualitatively different twilight sky; with the current estimator (finding cloud-rt-collapse) any smeared OD >~1 still collapses prayer times to sunrise, so live weather with moderate low/mid cloud produces garbage times. The 0.7 exponent has no citation; the closest literature analogue (Cahalan et al. 1994 effective-thickness factor ~0.7 for stratocumulus inhomogeneity) is a multiplier on tau, not an exponent on cover fraction. Additionally map_cloud returns only the single 'dominant' layer — 90% low cloud silently discards simultaneous mid/high cover (mapping.rs:94-161).
allFindings.recommendation: Run the RT twice (clear and full-OD cloudy) and blend luminances by cover fraction before thresholding; if a single run must be kept, document the bias. Support stacking of low/mid/high layers since the builder already composes layers additively.

allFindings.title: crates/twilight-clouds is an empty directory: no Cargo.toml, no sources, not a workspace member
allFindings.lines: n/a (directory contains only an empty src/)
allFindings.evidence:
$ ls -laR crates/twilight-clouds
crates/twilight-clouds/src: (empty)
$ grep twilight-clouds Cargo.toml -> no matches (workspace members list 11 crates, twilight-clouds absent)
allFindings.why_wrong: The directory suggests a dedicated clouds crate that does not exist; the real (data-only) cloud code lives in twilight-data/src/cloud.rs. An empty crate skeleton in the source tree is dead scaffolding that misleads readers/inventories into thinking there is a cloud subsystem of its own. It is consistent with the maintainer's 'fabricated capability' concern, though the README's crate table honestly attributes cloud types to twilight-data, so no documentation claim hinges on it.
allFindings.recommendation: Delete crates/twilight-clouds, or actually populate it (it would be the natural home for a real Mie/delta-Eddington cloud solver per the other findings).

allFindings.title: Claimed TSIS-1 TOA solar spectrum has a non-monotonic dip at exactly 760 nm (telluric O2 A-band), risking double-counted O2 absorption
allFindings.why_wrong: The TSIS-1 HSRS top-of-atmosphere continuum is smooth (~1.24-1.27 W/m2/nm) through 750-770 nm; there is no ~4-6% solar feature at 760 nm at 10 nm resolution. A dip at exactly the telluric O2 A-band position suggests the values were point-sampled from a high-resolution spectrum (hitting line cores; cf. also the low 390 nm=1.068 and 400 nm=1.527 entries vs ~1.65-1.70 band averages around 400 nm) or contaminated by a ground-level spectrum. Since the engine separately applies HITRAN line-by-line O2 A-band absorption at 762 nm (README.md:119, gas_absorption.rs), any telluric dip in the 'TOA' table double-counts that absorption. Impact on prayer times is negligible because V(lambda) ~ 1e-4 at 760 nm, hence low severity — but the table does not match its cited source.
allFindings.recommendation: Regenerate SOLAR_IRRADIANCE as proper 10 nm band averages of the actual TSIS-1 HSRS product (Coddington 2021, available from LASP) and add a test asserting smoothness (no >3% local dip) in the 700-780 nm continuum.

allFindings.title: build_with_cloud_layer duplicates add_cloud_layer with a degenerate mixing rule that discards non-Rayleigh scattering and skips gas absorption
allFindings.why_wrong: There are two cloud-mixing implementations: add_cloud_layer (builder.rs:490-550, used by build_full/build_full_with_gas and the CLI) correctly partitions existing scattering via rayleigh_fraction, while build_with_cloud_layer hard-codes the assumption that all pre-existing scattering is Rayleigh (g=0) and ignores existing.rayleigh_fraction and existing.asymmetry. It is currently safe only because it internally starts from build_clear_sky (line 110), but any future caller layering it over an aerosol atmosphere would silently zero the aerosol asymmetry. It also returns without applying gas absorption, so build_with_cloud/build_with_cloud_properties (lines 319-351) produce ozone-free atmospheres unlike every production path — a trap for API users. Pure duplication risk, not a live bug.
allFindings.recommendation: Delete build_with_cloud_layer's bespoke mixing and have it call build_clear_sky + add_cloud_layer; document (or fix) the missing gas-absorption step in the build_with_cloud* helpers.

verdict.reasoning: I read the cited code and reproduced every measurement. CODE: photon.rs:2458-2469 and :2529 do exactly what the finding says — both the order-1 NEE (scale_1 = beta_scat*INV_4PI*t_sun*t_obs*ds) and the orders-2+ MC source (scale_m = beta_scat*t_obs*ds) are weighted by direct-beam transmittance t_obs = exp(-tau_obs_mid) from the observer, with the `if t_obs < 1e-30 break` at :2461. This LOS formulation is itself the exact formal RTE solution (standard local-estimate/NEE, cf. MYSTIC), so diffuse transmission through a cloud must be rebuilt entirely by the secondary chains — and those chains' importance sampling (branch_params_for_sza/dwivedi_frac at photon.rs:2955-2999, weight_window_h:1213, cadis_k:1315, zenith lobes ramping SZA 96-106) is tuned for clear-sky Rayleigh, exactly as claimed. HYBRID_LOS_STEPS=200 confirmed at photon.rs:795; stratus is 0.5-1.5 km, OD 10, g=0.85 (twilight-data/src/cloud.rs:87-93), so at 75-deg view zenith the ~330 km LOS gives ds~1.65 km — 2-3 steps across the 3.9 km slant cloud with tau~15-19 per step, as stated. MEASUREMENTS (all reproduced on this machine, target/release/twilight-cli): clear hybrid --cpu --fast SZA96 L_photopic=3.990127e0 (finding: 3.99); stratus hybrid SZA96 = 2.079168e-15 vs single-scatter 2.078823e-15 (MC adds 0.02% — exact match to finding); stratus SZA98 hybrid at p=200/500/1000 = 1.02e-5/3.87e-5/3.42e-4, a 33x swing and 10 orders of magnitude BRIGHTER than SZA96 — non-monotonic L(SZA) confirmed; --scattering multiple at default p=100 gives exactly 0.000000e0 at SZA98 (and 9.58 cd/m2 at SZA96, brighter than clear — also broken). PRAYER TIMES: `pray --cloud X --cpu --fast` (lat 21.4, 2026-01-15) gives Fajr depression 0.01 (stratus), 0.05 (thick-cirrus), 0.01 (altostratus), 0.00 (stratocumulus), 0.00 (cumulus), 12.99 (thin-cirrus) — exactly the quoted 'SZA 90.01' collapse for 5 of 6 cloud types, vs clear-sky 14.87. PHYSICS: the finding's two-stream diffuse transmittance T=1/(1+0.75*tau*(1-g))~0.47 for tau=10, g=0.85 is the standard conservative-cloud result (Petty, Bohren), and shadow heights R(sec(SZA-90)-1) = 35-63 km at SZA 96-98 match the claimed 35-60 km, so real overcast twilight dims ~1 order of magnitude, not 15. One clarification (does not change the verdict): the collapse-to-sunrise occurs on the --fast scalar path, which dispatches to hybrid_scatter_radiance_alis (photon.rs:4162, via twilight-cpu/src/simulation.rs:269), not the cited per-wavelength function; the default polarized pray path (which DOES use the cited hybrid_scatter_radiance, simulation.rs:291) does not collapse to sunrise but is still broken — stratus Fajr at depression 8.2-9.0 jittering ~3 min across photon counts, luminance non-monotonic and firefly-ridden (stratus Stokes: 4.7e-3 at SZA98, 3.9e-2 at SZA99, 2.2e-5 at SZA100, 1.9e-5 at SZA103, 1.5e-12 at SZA104), and ~150-400x dimmer than clear at SZA96 where ~5-20x is physical. README.md:14 ('Your prayer app doesn't know if it's cloudy') and :119 ('Cloud layers (6 types)') are contradicted as claimed.
verdict.correction: Finding stands as written, with one precision fix: the 'collapse to sunrise for 5 of 6 cloud types' occurs on the --fast (scalar/ALIS, hybrid_scatter_radiance_alis at photon.rs:4162) path that the reviewer's measurements used; the default polarized pray path (the cited photon.rs:2395-2562 function) instead yields cloud Fajr/Isha ~25-30 min late with noise-determined threshold crossings (3-6x luminance swings vs photon count, non-monotonic L(SZA) with 5-13 order-of-magnitude fireflies above SZA 100). verdict.reasoning: All code facts check out: cloud.rs:52-53 defines cloud asymmetry as 'Henyey-Greenstein g' (presets g=0.85 water / 0.77 cirrus); scattering.rs:32-36 is single-term HG with exact analytic CDF sampling at scattering.rs:89-103; photon.rs:380-383 and 696-699 sample HG per shell; twilight.metal:401-414 and 1129-1132 do the same on GPU. Grep across all .rs/.metal confirms NO Mie phase tables and NO delta-scaling exist anywhere ('Mie' appears only in comments; 'p_mie' in twilight.metal:2221-2226 is actually HG). The per-shell single-lobe claim is also true: builder.rs:161-180, 287-308, 530-545 blend cloud and aerosol g into one scattering-weighted asymmetry per shell. However, the 'high / physics-incorrect' framing is overstated on two grounds. (1) Driving cloud RT with (tau, SSA, g) + HG is standard production practice, not an error: libRadtran's default water-cloud parameterization (Hu & Stamnes 1993) supplies exactly (ext, ssa, g) used as HG-type Legendre moments; full Mie tables (MYSTIC) are the higher-fidelity radiance option, not the baseline. The presets match Stephens (1978)-class values. (2) The 'at minimum delta-scaled HG (Joseph, Wiscombe & Weinman 1976)' demand is misapplied to Monte Carlo: delta-scaling exists for low-order moment solvers that cannot resolve a sharp forward peak, or as MC variance reduction for true Mie peaks. This code samples HG exactly by CDF inversion, so there is no unresolved peak to fold into extinction; a self-consistent delta-scaled HG would give the identical exact-transport answer. The genuine residual issue is HG-vs-Mie radiance fidelity: missing diffraction aureole, fogbow/glory, and (for cirrus, which needs ice-habit phase functions, not Mie anyway) 22-degree halos, so thin-cirrus single-scattering radiances have wrong angular structure. For thick clouds (OD 5-15) similarity theory makes diffuse radiance depend mainly on (tau, SSA, g), so twilight threshold-crossing times shift far less than natural cloud-OD variability. This is an accuracy/quality concern to fix (tabulated phase functions for radiance work), not high-severity incorrect physics.
verdict.correction: The code description is accurate: clouds use a single-term HG phase function (one scattering-weighted g and rayleigh_fraction per shell), with no Mie tables and no delta-scaling anywhere (CPU: scattering.rs:32-36, photon.rs:380-383/696-699; GPU: twilight.metal:401-414/1129-1132; mixing: builder.rs:161-180/287-308/530-545). But this is a standard, widely used approximation rather than incorrect physics: libRadtran's default Hu & Stamnes (1993) water-cloud parameterization drives solvers with exactly (tau, ssa, g)/HG, and delta-scaling (Joseph-Wiscombe-Weinman 1976) is a requirement for low-order moment solvers or a variance-reduction device for true Mie peaks — it is not needed for correctness in a Monte Carlo code that samples HG exactly via analytic CDF inversion. The legitimate residual issue is radiance fidelity: HG lacks the Mie aureole, fogbow/glory, and ice-crystal halo structure, distorting single-scattering-dominated thin-cirrus radiances; for optically thick clouds, similarity theory limits the effect on twilight threshold-crossing times to well below natural cloud-OD uncertainty. Downgrade to medium: replace HG with tabulated Mie (water) and ice-habit phase functions for radiance accuracy, and keep separate aerosol/cloud lobes per shell, but this is an enhancement, not a physics error materially shifting prayer times.

reviewed.summary: The luminance integration machinery is mostly sound: the photopic V(λ) table (vision.rs) is the correct CIE 1924 table, K_m=683.002 and K_m'=1700.06 are right, and the production scotopic/photopic luminances are properly integrated against tabulated efficiency functions by trapezoid rule (refuting the orchestrator seed that scotopic is a flat photopic×1.5 — that factor appears ONLY in test fixtures, not the engine). However, three substantive problems remain. (1) The SCOTOPIC_V_PRIME table is corrupted/non-standard: it peaks at ~490-495nm instead of 507nm, is not normalized to 1.0, and its red tail is 2x-100x too high vs CIE 1951; it feeds mesopic luminance, the actual Fajr/Isha-abyad decision variable. (2) The threshold luminance constants are documented as "calibrated against SQM observations" but no calibration exists anywhere in the tree — they are hand-tuned magic numbers that directly set prayer times. (3) The mesopic model is labeled "CIE 191:2010" but is a simplified post-integration scalar blend, and shafaq color classification uses a V(λ)-weighted centroid that is a poor colorimetric discriminator (the authors' own test admits it). Numeric impact on times is modest-but-real (roughly up to a few minutes), so most issues are high/medium rather than critical.

allFindings.title: SCOTOPIC_V'(λ) table is non-standard: wrong peak wavelength, not peak-normalized, red tail 2x-100x too high
allFindings.why_wrong: The CIE 1951 scotopic luminous-efficiency function V'(λ) is normalized to 1.0 at its 507nm peak, with V'(500)=0.982, V'(550)=0.481, V'(600)=0.0332, V'(650)=0.00148, V'(700)=5.89e-5 (Wyszecki & Stiles; CIE 1951). The code's table instead reaches its maximum value 0.982 at the 490-495nm entries (so it peaks ~14nm too blue and never normalizes to 1.0, despite the docstring claiming 'peak at 507nm'), and its long-wavelength values are grossly inflated: V'(600)=0.065 (~2x), V'(650)=0.006 (~4x), V'(700)=0.0006 (~10x), up to ~100x at 780nm. Spot-checking shows the 445-535nm entries are exactly the photopic V(λ) table shifted by 60nm (e.g. code V'(445)=0.4073 = photopic V(505); V'(470)=0.862 = photopic V(530)), i.e. the curve was fabricated by blue-shifting V(λ) rather than tabulating true V'(λ). This table is consumed by mesopic_luminance (luminance.rs:90), and mesopic luminance is THE decision variable for Fajr and Isha-al-abyad (threshold.rs:196,227). For a red-dominated twilight spectrum the integrated scotopic/mesopic bias reaches ~1.45x (numerically verified), shifting the SZA crossing by up to ~0.3°, i.e. a few minutes of prayer time. The data is also mislabeled as 'CIE 1951 scotopic V'(λ)'.
allFindings.recommendation: Replace SCOTOPIC_V_PRIME with the authoritative CIE 1951 V'(λ) table (normalized to 1.0 at 507nm) at 5nm spacing, and tighten the unit tests (the existing scotopic_peak_near_507nm asserts the peak is ~0.982 and scotopic_peak_index_near_507nm allows 490-515nm, so both pass on the corrupted data — they should assert peak==1.0 at 505-510nm).

allFindings.why_wrong: These five constants are the direct determinants of the computed Fajr/Isha SZAs (used at threshold.rs:196, 210, 227), yet there is no SQM dataset, fitting routine, or calibration code anywhere in the workspace (grep for SQM/calibrat finds only this docstring and unrelated skyglow Bortle text). allFindings.title: Mesopic model labeled 'CIE 191:2010' is a simplified scalar blend driven by photopic (not mesopic) luminance
allFindings.why_wrong: The CIE 191:2010 (MES2) recommended system defines a mesopic spectral luminous efficiency V_mes;m(λ)=m·V(λ)+(1−m)·V'(λ) that must be integrated against the spectrum, with m solved IMPLICITLY from the resulting mesopic luminance via an iterative fixed-point (because the adaptation level is the mesopic luminance itself). The code instead (a) integrates photopic and scotopic luminances separately and blends the two scalars afterwards, (b) derives m from the PHOTOPIC luminance with a single non-iterative log10 interpolation, and (c) rescales scotopic by an ad-hoc K_m/K_m' factor. The 0.005-5.0 cd/m² bounds are correctly the CIE 191 mesopic range, but the structural method is a simplification, not the CIE 191 algorithm. The simplification is defensible engineering, but presenting it as 'the CIE 191:2010 adapted model' (also luminance.rs:4, threshold.rs:11) overstates it.
allFindings.recommendation: Soften the docstrings to 'a simplified mesopic interpolation inspired by CIE 191:2010' or implement the actual iterative MES2 system (blend the efficiency functions, then solve for m). At minimum note that m is keyed to photopic, not mesopic, luminance.

allFindings.title: Shafaq red/white classification via V(λ)-weighted spectral centroid is a weak colorimetric metric; red-band input ignored
allFindings.why_wrong: The 'spectral centroid' is the V(λ)-weighted mean wavelength (luminance.rs:132-159). Because V(λ) collapses to ~0 beyond 650nm, a genuinely red sky (radiance peaking 620-680nm) has its centroid dragged back toward 555nm, so the centroid barely registers redness — the authors' own red-spectrum test fixture concedes this, needing a quadratic ramp: 'Quadratic ramp overcomes V(λ) weighting to ensure centroid > 570nm' (threshold.rs:279). Standard colorimetry classifies hue via CIE chromaticity coordinates / dominant wavelength or a simple red:blue band ratio, not a luminosity-weighted centroid. Compounding this, the physically meaningful red-band luminance is passed in but discarded (the parameter is named _luminance_red and unused), so the shafaq-al-ahmar color label rests entirely on the weak centroid. The 590/570/530nm boundaries are therefore arbitrary cut points on a metric that poorly tracks the quantity of interest.
allFindings.recommendation: Classify shafaq color from a colorimetric measure (chromaticity / dominant wavelength, or the existing red_band vs blue_band luminance ratio) instead of a V-weighted centroid, and actually use the red-band luminance already computed. If keeping the centroid, weight by photon/energy spectrum rather than by V(λ).

allFindings.title: luminance_scotopic = luminance * 1.5 is test-fixture data only, not a production formula (seed clarification)
allFindings.evidence: luminance_scotopic: luminance * 1.5,   // (inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests, building synthetic TwilightAnalysis structs)
allFindings.why_wrong: The orchestrator seed flagged threshold.rs:487 and :615 as a fabricated scotopic = photopic×1.5 magic factor. These lines are inside the #[cfg(test)] module, constructing synthetic TwilightAnalysis fixtures; they are NOT the production scotopic computation. The real engine computes scotopic luminance by re-integrating radiance against V'(λ) with K_m'=1700.06 (luminance.rs:63-79), which is the correct approach — and the scotopic field is only reported, never used by determine_prayer_times (which uses mesopic and red-band). So the ×1.5 is harmless to output but bakes a physically meaningless photopic-to-scotopic relationship into tests; it should be removed to avoid implying such a relationship is valid. (The 'small tolerance' l_red+l_blue < l_total*1.01 at luminance.rs:601 is a legitimate trapezoid round-off guard, not a defect.)
allFindings.recommendation: Replace the ×1.5 fixtures with values produced from scotopic_luminance on a representative spectrum, or drop the scotopic field from fixtures where it is irrelevant, so tests do not encode a non-physical photopic/scotopic ratio.

verdict.reasoning: Read crates/twilight-threshold/src/vision.rs:30-42 and compared every entry against the true CIE 1951 V'(λ) table (Wyszecki & Stiles). Confirmed: (1) the code's maximum is 0.982 at 490 AND 495 nm, whereas the real table peaks 0.998 at 505 nm (1.000 at 507 nm); the docstring 'peak at 507nm' is contradicted by the data, and the crate's own tests (vision.rs:155-182) were written to assert the corrupted peak value 0.982 and a loose 490-515 nm window, enshrining the bad data. (2) The red tail is grossly inflated — measured code/true ratios: 600nm=1.96x, 620nm=3.5x, 650nm=8.9x, 700nm=33.7x, 780nm=108x. The reviewer's reference values at 650/700 nm were one row off in the standard table (0.00148 is V'(640); true V'(650)=0.000677, V'(700)=1.78e-5), so they UNDERSTATED the inflation. (3) Fabrication signature verified: entries 380-440 nm exactly match true scotopic, then 445-475 nm are digit-for-digit the photopic V(λ+60nm) values (0.4073=V(505), 0.5030=V(510), 0.6082=V(515), 0.7100=V(520), 0.7932=V(525), 0.8620=V(530), 0.914850=V(535)); the reviewer's claimed exact-shift range 445-535 nm is slightly too wide (beyond 475 nm values match neither source), but the core claim — the table is fabricated, not CIE data — is unambiguous. (4) Downstream confirmed: SCOTOPIC_V_PRIME feeds scotopic_luminance (luminance.rs:71-72) → mesopic_luminance (luminance.rs:88-98), and luminance_mesopic is the crossing variable for Isha al-abyad (threshold.rs:196-197) and Fajr (threshold.rs:226-227). At the default thresholds (0.001 and 0.003 cd/m², threshold.rs:86-87) the mesopic coefficient m=0 (below the 0.005 cd/m² lower bound, luminance.rs:108), so the decision variable is 100% scotopic — the corrupted table fully determines those crossings. The table is also uploaded to the GPU (twilight-gpu/src/buffers.rs:329). (5) Magnitude check: integrated bias is spectrum-dependent — ~1.7% flat, 1.20x for Rayleigh-reddened τ550=5, 2.3x at τ550=10 — consistent with the reviewer's ~1.45x/~0.3° SZA/few-minutes estimate for red-dominated spectra. Additionally, the 0.982 (non-unity) peak combined with K_m'=1700.06 lm/W (luminance.rs:14, defined for peak-normalized V') under-counts scotopic luminance ~1.8% even for blue light.
verdict.correction: Two small fixes to the otherwise-correct finding: (a) the exact photopic-shifted-by-60nm region is 445-475 nm (7 entries, digit-for-digit), not 445-535 nm — beyond 475 nm the values match neither the shifted photopic curve nor the true scotopic table; (b) the red-tail inflation is worse than stated: code V'(650) is 8.9x the true CIE value (not ~4x) and V'(700) is 33.7x (not ~10x); the reviewer's reference values 0.00148 and 5.89e-5 are not the standard V'(650)/V'(700) entries (true: 0.000677 and 1.78e-5). Also worth adding: at the default Fajr/Isha-abyad thresholds (0.001/0.003 cd/m²) the mesopic coefficient is 0, so the decision variable is purely scotopic — the corrupted table is 100% of the crossing signal, and the crate's own unit tests assert the corrupted peak (0.982 at 490-515 nm), masking the defect.

finding.why_wrong: These five constants are the direct determinants of the computed Fajr/Isha SZAs (used at threshold.rs:196, 210, 227), yet there is no SQM dataset, fitting routine, or calibration code anywhere in the workspace (grep for SQM/calibrat finds only this docstring and unrelated skyglow Bortle text). verdict.reasoning: I read /Users/mostafamahdi/twilight/crates/twilight-threshold/src/threshold.rs in full. The quoted evidence is accurate: lines 54-56 state "They are calibrated against SQM (Sky Quality Meter) observations and traditional astronomical twilight definitions," and the Default impl (lines 83-93) hardcodes exactly the five round numbers cited (0.001, 0.003, 0.0005, 590.0, 530.0). Lines 61-62 and 67 additionally claim physical equivalences ("roughly equivalent to 18° depression", "roughly equivalent to 15° depression"). (1) No calibration exists: a workspace-wide grep for SQM/calibrat finds hits only in twilight-skyglow (Bortle-class/SQM unit-conversion formulas like SQM = 12.58 - 2.5*log10(L), unrelated to these thresholds) and review artifacts. There is no SQM dataset, CSV, fitting routine, or any code that derives these constants; `find` for sqm/calib/csv/json data files turns up nothing. (2) The constants are the sole determinants of the output SZAs: they are compared at threshold.rs:196-197 (isha_abyad_luminance), 210-211 (isha_ahmar_red_luminance), and 226-227 (fajr_luminance) inside determine_prayer_times, whose results become the prayer clock times in twilight-cpu/src/pipeline.rs:714-719. (3) No override path exists: grep shows fajr_luminance/isha_*_luminance are never assigned outside the Default impl; pipeline.rs:113 and twilight-cli/main.rs:800 both use ThresholdConfig::default(). (4) The physics critique is sound with one geometric nuance: the radiance fed to analyze_twilight is computed at view_zenith 85° toward the solar azimuth (pipeline.rs:573-574), i.e. 5° above the horizon — not the zenith as the reviewer wrote. But this strengthens rather than weakens the finding: the docstring's depression-angle equivalences (0.001 cd/m² ≈ 18° depression) are zenith-brightness conventions from the twilight literature (zenith luminance ~4e-3 cd/m² at 12° depression, night-sky background ~2e-4 cd/m², per Rozenberg 1966 / Patat 2008 / Crumey 2014), and the 85°-view solar-azimuth sky is substantially brighter than zenith at equal depression, so the stated equivalences cannot simultaneously hold for the geometry actually used — internal inconsistency that confirms no calibration was done. The reviewer's contrast-vs-absolute point is also fair: classical shafaq/true-dawn detection is a visual contrast phenomenon, and even the real SQM-based Fajr literature (e.g. Indonesian/Malaysian SQM dawn studies) uses per-site inflection detection rather than one universal absolute cd/m² value. As corroborating evidence of fabricated physics framing, line 72 and the test at lines 604-637 also encode shafaq al-ahmar disappearing AFTER al-abyad, which inverts the standard fiqh/observational ordering (red glow disappears first; Hanafi abyad-based Isha is the later one) — a separate defect, but consistent with these constants being invented rather than calibrated. Severity high is correct: this is a fabricated provenance claim on the constants that directly set worship times, but the values are at least order-of-magnitude plausible and the code runs, so it does not meet the bar for critical (provably wrong physics or non-functional code).

reviewed.summary: Verified on real hardware (Apple M2 Pro, Metal 4): the Metal single-scatter kernel is genuinely correct — it matches the CPU f64 oracle at rtol 1.5e-3 across SZA 80-108, and the f32 precision machinery (FMA double-single discriminant, Kahan/Neumaier sums, radial nudge + boundary snapping) is real and load-bearing, not decorative. The hybrid (multi-scatter) path — the one the prayer pipeline actually needs — is broken in two distinct ways: (1) at production ray counts (default 10,000; tests use 5,000) the v2 dispatch is killed by the macOS GPU watchdog ("Impacting Interactivity"), reproduced deterministically in the repo's own test and intermittently at 4,000-5,000 rays in my probe, so the pipeline falls back to CPU and the GPU hybrid capability is effectively nonfunctional as shipped; the uncommitted "fix" made it worse based on a timing comment that is wrong by ~200-900x. (2) The shader never ported the CPU's truncated power-cosine importance sampler, leaving unbounded f32 weights — measured: GPU rsd 42% vs CPU 9.7% at SZA 104 with identical ray counts, mean ratio 1.3-1.4 at SZA 104-106 — which is the actual root cause of the "v2 NaN under investigation" commit thread, now masked (not fixed) by silent isfinite-zeroing. The maintainer's claim "the Metal shader doesn't work" is accurate for the hybrid/prayer path and inaccurate for single-scatter.

allFindings.title: Hybrid v2 dispatch is killed by the macOS GPU watchdog at production ray counts; the '5000-ray fix' is built on a timing claim that is wrong by ~200-900x
allFindings.why_wrong: A 2500-ray dispatch takes ~900ms, and dispatch_hybrid_v2_chunk encodes up to DISPATCHES_PER_COMMAND_BUFFER=4 dispatches into ONE command buffer with one waitUntilCompleted (metal.rs:742-756) — up to ~3.6s of GPU work per command buffer. macOS kills long-running command buffers on display GPUs (kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackError); the kill is load-dependent (in my probes rays=4000 failed then succeeded on rerun, rays=5000 succeeded then failed). SimulationConfig::default() sets photons_per_wavelength=10_000 (simulation.rs:97), so the prayer pipeline's hybrid GPU path essentially always errors and falls back to CPU via the eprintln path in pipeline.rs:445-451. The commit 'Fix 5000-ray Metal prayer: split dispatch + GPU timeout detection' detects the timeout (status check at metal.rs:758-768) but does not recover; the uncommitted diff raised per-command-buffer work ~40x vs the committed 256-ray version, making the failure more likely, not less. This is the concrete mechanism behind 'the Metal shader doesn't work'.
allFindings.recommendation: Size dispatches by measured time, not fabricated estimates: keep per-command-buffer GPU time well under ~500ms (empirically ~1000-1500 rays per command buffer on M2 Pro for this geometry), commit one dispatch per command buffer, and on a watchdog error retry the chunk with half the rays instead of aborting the whole scan to CPU. Delete the false '~1-5ms' comment.

allFindings.title: Shader never ported the CPU's truncated power-cosine proposal: unbounded importance weights in f32 are the root cause of the 'v2 NaN' thread and inflate deep-twilight variance ~4x vs CPU
allFindings.why_wrong: The CPU reference it must match deliberately truncates the sampling domain: photon.rs:901 'const ZENITH_MAX_IMPORTANCE_WEIGHT: f64 = 200.0', photon.rs:913-926 power_cos_min() with a 0.2 floor, photon.rs:4774-4783 truncated inverse CDF over [cos_min, 1], and the matching 1-cos_min^(n+1) normalization in zenith_importance_weight (4805-4814) and terminator_shape_weight (4929-4935). This bounds w = p_cosine/p_trunc at 200 by construction — a proposal-distribution change, unbiased per standard importance-sampling theory (cf. Veach-style defensive sampling; E[w^2] = ∫cos^(2-n) diverges near cos→0 for n≥3, so the untruncated estimator at n_zenith=5/m_term=8 has effectively unbounded variance). The GPU samples the UNTRUNCATED distribution with the untruncated weight, so at SZA≥~100 (n>2.6) it draws weights up to ~1e29 that the CPU never produces; in f32 these overflow to inf/NaN — directly matching the commits 'v2 NaN under investigation' and the in-shader admission at twilight.metal:2114-2118: 'the underlying chain has f32 overflow in weight * nee_stokes, not just in ET'. Measured (6 seeds, 1024 rays, 41 wl, view 85°): SZA 102 GPU/CPU mean ratio 1.008 (fine); SZA 104 GPU rsd 42.4% vs CPU 9.7%, mean ratio 1.44 (one trial 1.42e-5 ≈ 2.7x CPU mean); SZA 106 GPU rsd 50.3%, ratio 1.34. Deep twilight SZA 96-108 is exactly the Fajr/Isha threshold regime, so when the GPU result is used it shifts the radiance-threshold crossing (radiance falls ~8x per 2° here; a 1.4x error ≈ 0.4-0.6° SZA ≈ several minutes at mid-latitudes).
allFindings.recommendation: Port power_cos_min(), the truncated inverse CDF, and the (1 - cos_min^(n+1)) normalization factors from photon.rs:913-926/4769-4814/4921-4936 into sample_zenith_biased, zenith_importance_weight, and terminator_shape_weight in twilight.metal. This bounds all initial weights at 200, eliminating the f32 overflow source the clamps were papering over.

allFindings.title: Removed 'biasing clamps' were replaced by silent isfinite-zeroing at four levels, which is itself a one-sided (biased) filter and masks the unresolved NaN root cause; a stale comment still describes the deleted clamp
allFindings.why_wrong: After commit 57c02fc removed the clamps, the comment block at 1625-1630 still describes a 1e6 clamp that no longer exists, and the parenthetical 'not bias -- just numerical safety' is wrong: chains that overflow f32 are overwhelmingly the largest POSITIVE contributions (huge importance weights x NEE), so zeroing exactly those samples systematically truncates the upper tail of the estimator — silent, unlogged, and concentrated at deep twilight where it matters. inf*0 → NaN cases (e.g. weight=inf times t_sun rounding to 0) are likewise discarded. In f64 on CPU the same samples are kept. This is energy deletion conditioned on sample value, the textbook definition of a biased estimator filter, and it hides the real defect (finding untruncated-importance-sampler) so 'v2 NaN under investigation' can never conclude.
allFindings.recommendation: Fix the weight bound at the sampler (see untruncated-importance-sampler); then make any remaining non-finite value a loud failure (atomic counter read back by the host and surfaced as an error or warning), not a silent zero. Delete or rewrite the stale clamp comment at 1625-1630.

allFindings.title: Two dead kernels (v1 hybrid_scatter, hybrid_los_prefix) and a v2 header that claims a tau_prefix buffer(3) which does not exist; v2 instead recomputes the LOS prefix serially, the very O(steps^2) cost the dead kernel was 'eliminating'
allFindings.why_wrong: The host (metal.rs:103-106) creates pipelines only for single_scatter_spectrum, mcrt_trace_photon, hybrid_scatter_v2, and garstang_zenith — the uncommitted diff deleted pso_hybrid, so the 600-line v1 hybrid_scatter kernel (line 1657) and the hybrid_los_prefix kernel (line 1855, whose own header says it 'eliminat[es] the O(steps^2) serial prefix that was in hybrid_scatter_v2') are compiled but never dispatched. The v2 kernel's documented buffer(3) input was never wired: its signature stops at buffer(2) and lane 0 of every (wl, step) threadgroup re-walks all preceding steps (2008-2020), re-done per split-dispatch chunk. The file header (lines 3-7) still says 'Four compute kernels' while the file contains six. These are documentation/architecture claims contradicted by the code — the signature of an abandoned refactor left in place.
allFindings.recommendation: Either wire hybrid_los_prefix + buffer(3) into hybrid_scatter_v2 and the host dispatch (it also removes redundant per-chunk prefix recomputation), or delete hybrid_los_prefix, the v1 hybrid_scatter kernel, and the stale buffer-3/'four kernels' comments.

allFindings.title: New 'match_cpu_statistics' test accepts any GPU/CPU ratio between 0.05x and 20x, so it cannot detect even an order-of-magnitude hybrid divergence
allFindings.evidence:
fn metal_hybrid_split_dispatch_boundaries_match_cpu_statistics() {
...
        assert!(
            ratio.is_finite() && (0.05..=20.0).contains(&ratio),
            "split boundary rays={} ratio out of range: cpu={:.6e}, gpu={:.6e}, ratio={:.4}",
allFindings.why_wrong: A factor-of-20 acceptance window on a test whose name promises statistical agreement with the CPU is a smoke test masquerading as a parity test. My measurements show the actual deep-twilight GPU/CPU discrepancy is 1.3-1.4x mean ratio with 42% rsd — invisible to this tolerance — so the test passing (it does, verified) provides false assurance precisely about the defect under investigation. Combined with the established pattern that all layer4_metal tests silently no-op when no GPU device is present ('let Some(gpu) = try_metal() else { return };'), CI green tells you nothing about hybrid correctness.
allFindings.recommendation: Test mean agreement with enough seeds for a real bound: e.g. average >=8 seeds at fixed SZA/rays and assert the GPU/CPU mean ratio within 1±3*combined-SE (roughly ±15-20% at 1024 rays), at both SZA 96 and 104. Mark GPU tests as skipped (not passed) when no device exists.

allFindings.title: Host discards the upper 32 bits of the caller's RNG seed, and the prayer dispatch seeds with sza_deg.to_bits(), whose lower 32 bits are zero for coarse-grid SZAs — so all coarse scan points share identical RNG streams
allFindings.evidence:
let ray_seed = (seed & 0xFFFF_FFFF) | ((ray_start as u64) << 32);
— combined with gpu_dispatch.rs:98-103/158-163 'seed: sza_deg.to_bits()' and twilight.metal:2086 'ulong base_seed = raw_seed & 0xFFFFFFFFul;'
allFindings.why_wrong: The kernel repurposes the seed's upper 32 bits as the split-dispatch ray_offset, so only the low 32 bits of the caller seed survive. The prayer pipeline seeds with sza_deg.to_bits(): for any SZA whose f64 mantissa is short (96.0, 96.5, 97.0 — i.e. every coarse-scan point), the low 32 bits are exactly 0, so base_seed = 0 for all of them and the per-thread streams (seed_input = base_seed ^ wl-hash ^ step ^ lane, twilight.metal:2091-2095) are bit-identical across SZA points; only geometry differs. The seed parameter is therefore partially fabricated API surface. Statistical impact is ambiguous — common random numbers across an SZA scan correlate the noise (sometimes helpful for threshold-crossing smoothness) — but it is clearly unintended, and distinct user-supplied seeds with equal low words silently produce identical runs.
allFindings.recommendation: Hash the full 64-bit seed (e.g. splitmix64(seed) on the host) before truncating, and pass ray_offset in a dedicated params slot (there are 3 unused pad floats per vec4) instead of stealing the seed's upper word.

verdict.correction: Two small calibration notes, not refutations: (1) On this M2 Pro a cold 2500-ray dispatch measured 558-778 ms, not the reviewer's 926 ms, so the in-code "1-5 ms" claim is wrong by ~110-780x rather than "~200-900x" — same 2-3 orders of magnitude, same conclusion. (2) At the single-call level the watchdog kill is intermittent/load-dependent (rays=5000 standalone: 1 of 4 cold runs failed; rays=10000: 1 of 5 failed at ~3 s per command buffer), so "essentially always errors" is an overstatement per call; however the repo's own test failed 4/4 cargo-test runs at the first hybrid_scatter unwrap, and a production prayer run issues many ~3 s hybrid command buffers across the SZA scan, so the probability of at least one kill per run (which aborts the whole GPU scan to CPU via pipeline.rs:445-451) is very high.
verdict.reasoning: I read the cited code and reproduced the failure empirically on the same hardware class (Apple M2 Pro). Code claims all check out: (a) metal.rs:258-264 (working tree) contains the comment "each 2500-ray dispatch finishes in ~1-5ms, well under the limit" with RAYS_PER_DISPATCH=2500 and DISPATCHES_PER_COMMAND_BUFFER=4; (b) dispatch_hybrid_v2_chunk (metal.rs:704-771) encodes up to 4 dispatches into ONE command buffer with a single commit()/waitUntilCompleted() (lines 742-756), and the status check at 758-768 only converts MTLCommandBufferStatus::Error into Err — no retry, split, or recovery; (c) gpu_dispatch.rs:49 passes config.photons_per_wavelength as secondary_rays and SimulationConfig::default() sets it to 10_000 (simulation.rs:97), so the default prayer pipeline produces one command buffer holding 4x2500-ray dispatches; (d) pipeline.rs:445-451 is exactly the eprintln + CPU-fallback path. Empirical verification: cargo test -p twilight-gpu --release --features metal metal_multi_hybrid_matches_serial_chunk FAILED 4/4 runs, every time panicking at tests.rs:1032 (the FIRST serial hybrid_scatter unwrap, rays=5000) with Dispatch("Metal command buffer error in hybrid_scatter_v2 chunk: Impacting Interactivity (0000000e:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorImpactingInteractivity)") — the exact error string the finding quotes. A standalone timing probe I wrote (and deleted afterward) measured: 625 rays = 148 ms, 1250 = 295-322 ms, 2500 = 558-778 ms, 5000 = 1.16-1.60 s, 10000 = 2.38-3.13 s — confirming the "1-5 ms" comment is fabricated/wrong by over two orders of magnitude, and that the default 10_000-ray pipeline call puts ~3 s of GPU work in a single command buffer on a display GPU. The same probe reproduced the watchdog kill: at the test's exact config (SZA 90, rays=5000) one of four cold runs returned the kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorImpactingInteractivity error, and at rays=10000 one of five runs failed — confirming the load-dependent intermittency the reviewer described. Git history confirms the regression mechanism: HEAD commit 23dd155 is literally "Fix 5000-ray Metal prayer: split dispatch + GPU timeout detection" and its committed metal.rs has RAYS_PER_DISPATCH=256 with one dispatch per command buffer (dispatch_hybrid_v2, each call creating its own command buffer), while the UNCOMMITTED working-tree diff raises this to 2500 rays x 4 dispatches per command buffer = 10,000 rays per buffer, ~39x more GPU work per command buffer than the committed fix — verifying the finding's "~40x" claim and that the working tree made the watchdog kill more likely, not less. The only inaccuracies are minor calibration details (see correction); the mechanism, the failing repo test, the non-recovering error path, and the wrong timing comment are all real. Severity stays critical: prayer-time OUTPUT remains correct because pipeline.rs falls back to CPU, but the Metal hybrid GPU capability is presented as working on the strength of a fabricated timing claim, the repo's own test suite deterministically fails on real hardware at default-adjacent ray counts, and this is the concrete mechanism behind the maintainer's report that "the Metal shader doesn't work".

finding.title: Shader never ported the CPU's truncated power-cosine proposal: unbounded importance weights in f32 are the root cause of the 'v2 NaN' thread and inflate deep-twilight variance ~4x vs CPU
finding.why_wrong: The CPU reference it must match deliberately truncates the sampling domain: photon.rs:901 'const ZENITH_MAX_IMPORTANCE_WEIGHT: f64 = 200.0', photon.rs:913-926 power_cos_min() with a 0.2 floor, photon.rs:4774-4783 truncated inverse CDF over [cos_min, 1], and the matching 1-cos_min^(n+1) normalization in zenith_importance_weight (4805-4814) and terminator_shape_weight (4929-4935). This bounds w = p_cosine/p_trunc at 200 by construction — a proposal-distribution change, unbiased per standard importance-sampling theory (cf. Veach-style defensive sampling; E[w^2] = ∫cos^(2-n) diverges near cos→0 for n≥3, so the untruncated estimator at n_zenith=5/m_term=8 has effectively unbounded variance). The GPU samples the UNTRUNCATED distribution with the untruncated weight, so at SZA≥~100 (n>2.6) it draws weights up to ~1e29 that the CPU never produces; in f32 these overflow to inf/NaN — directly matching the commits 'v2 NaN under investigation' and the in-shader admission at twilight.metal:2114-2118: 'the underlying chain has f32 overflow in weight * nee_stokes, not just in ET'. Measured (6 seeds, 1024 rays, 41 wl, view 85°): SZA 102 GPU/CPU mean ratio 1.008 (fine); SZA 104 GPU rsd 42.4% vs CPU 9.7%, mean ratio 1.44 (one trial 1.42e-5 ≈ 2.7x CPU mean); SZA 106 GPU rsd 50.3%, ratio 1.34. Deep twilight SZA 96-108 is exactly the Fajr/Isha threshold regime, so when the GPU result is used it shifts the radiance-threshold crossing (radiance falls ~8x per 2° here; a 1.4x error ≈ 0.4-0.6° SZA ≈ several minutes at mid-latitudes).
finding.recommendation: Port power_cos_min(), the truncated inverse CDF, and the (1 - cos_min^(n+1)) normalization factors from photon.rs:913-926/4769-4814/4921-4936 into sample_zenith_biased, zenith_importance_weight, and terminator_shape_weight in twilight.metal. This bounds all initial weights at 200, eliminating the f32 overflow source the clamps were papering over.

verdict.reasoning: Read both sides myself. GPU (crates/twilight-gpu/shaders/twilight.metal): sample_zenith_biased at line 826 draws cos_theta = pow(xi1, 1/(n+1)) over the FULL [0,1] domain; zenith_importance_weight (834-837) returns 2/((n+1)*cos^(n-1)) with no truncation normalization; terminator_shape_weight (891-896) is bounded only by a cos_t_m<1e-30 guard, i.e. weights up to ~1e29; line 1342 explicitly says 'No clamp on initial_weight -- that would be bias.' CPU (crates/twilight-core/src/photon.rs): ZENITH_MAX_IMPORTANCE_WEIGHT=200.0 (line 901), power_cos_min with 0.2 floor (913-926), truncated inverse CDF over [cos_min,1] (4774-4783), and matching (1-cos_min^(n+1)) normalizations in zenith_importance_weight (4805-4814) and terminator_shape_weight (4929-4935) — a proposal-distribution change that is unbiased per standard truncated/defensive importance sampling, capping w at ~55.6 for n=5 (<=200 by design). Both sides use identical branch parameters (n_zenith 1->5, m_term 1->8 over SZA 96->106; twilight.metal:85-99/860-872 vs photon.rs:886-976/4857-4862) and the same 0.5/alpha branch weights (photon.rs:2627-2654 vs twilight.metal:1317-1341), so truncation is the ONLY difference — the GPU shader simply never ported it. The variance math checks out: E[w^2] ∝ ∫cos^(2-n)d(cos) diverges for n>=3 (n=2.6 at SZA 100, matching the finding's onset); my 2M-draw simulation at n=5 gives P(w>200)=5.8e-5 per draw (max observed 5.4e3, divergent sample second moment) vs CPU hard cap 55.6 — so across ~1e6 chains/run the GPU draws hundreds of weights the CPU cannot produce. The f32-overflow chain is corroborated by the shader itself: weight = ssa*initial_weight (line 1373) is further multiplied by exp(et_arg) with |et_arg| up to 80 (~5e34, lines 1462-1466), and the in-kernel comment at lines 2114-2118 admits 'the underlying chain has f32 overflow in weight * nee_stokes, not just in ET'; isfinite guards at 2106/2122/2138/2143 silently drop the overflowed chains, presenting as inflated variance/skew rather than NaN output. Minor imprecisions only: the ~1e29 weights are the guard-imposed bound (probability ~1e-34 of actually drawing one; the practical tail is 1e2-1e6, which is what drives the variance), the 'v2 NaN' commit references are unverifiable (directory is not a git repo — the in-shader comment is the real evidence), and I did not reproduce the reviewer's 6-seed rsd/ratio measurements, though they are consistent with the divergent-second-moment theory. SZA 96-108 is the Fajr/Isha threshold regime, so the inflated GPU variance/skew there does affect threshold-crossing times when the Metal backend is used. Core claim, mechanism, and severity all hold.

reviewed.summary: The twilight-gpu crate ships exactly one backend that can exist (Metal). The Vulkan, CUDA, and WebGPU backends are vapor: their host files include_bytes!/include_str! seven shader artifacts (4 .spv, twilight.cu, twilight.wgsl) that do not exist, and the repo contains zero GLSL/.comp sources, no build.rs, and no shader tooling (glslc/naga) that could ever have produced them — so the cuda/vulkan/webgpu features cannot compile and never could in this repo. I verified by temporarily stubbing the missing files that all three host implementations type-check cleanly (coherent ash 0.38 / cudarc 0.19 / wgpu 28 usage with real buffer creation, descriptor sets, dispatch, readback, and correct Drop ordering), so they are real-but-never-executed host skeletons rather than hallucinated Rust — but every public claim built on them (the "four hand-tuned backends" pitch, the GPU badge, the per-backend feature table, the cross-backend parity guarantee, the roadmap checkboxes, the test counts) is fabricated for 3 of 4 backends. The honest path: delete vulkan.rs/cuda.rs/wgpu_backend.rs and their features (or park them on a branch), rewrite the README/badge/roadmap to "Metal only, others planned", and add per-feature CI builds plus non-silently-skipping GPU tests so this class of fabrication cannot recur.

allFindings.title: README, badge, and roadmap claim four hand-written GPU backends; three cannot compile and their shaders have never existed
allFindings.evidence: L131: "**8. GPU acceleration.** Four hand-tuned backends with native shaders written from scratch for each API." L140: "Each backend has hand-written shaders tuned for its native GPU API." L19: "GPU-accelerated on Metal, Vulkan, CUDA, and WebGPU." L8 badge: "GPU-Metal%20%7C%20Vulkan%20%7C%20CUDA%20%7C%20WebGPU". L251: "- [x] GPU backends (Metal, Vulkan, CUDA, wgpu) with cross-backend parity"
allFindings.why_wrong: crates/twilight-gpu/shaders/ contains only twilight.metal (ground truth). `find` over the whole repo returns zero .cu/.wgsl/.spv/.glsl/.comp files and zero build.rs, so the three non-Metal features fail at include_bytes!/include_str! with "couldn't read ... No such file or directory" and the shaders could never have been built from this repo. "Hand-written shaders ... for each API" is a fabricated capability presented as shipped, checked off on the roadmap, and advertised in the badge.
allFindings.recommendation: Rewrite the GPU section to state that only the Metal backend is implemented (Vulkan/CUDA/WebGPU host scaffolding exists without shaders), change the badge to "GPU-Metal", and flip roadmap items 251/256 to unchecked or scope them to Metal.

allFindings.title: vulkan.rs embeds four nonexistent SPIR-V binaries and claims they are "built from GLSL at compile time"; no GLSL exists anywhere
allFindings.evidence: L50-53: `const SPV_SINGLE_SCATTER: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../shaders/single_scatter.spv"); const SPV_MCRT_TRACE: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../shaders/mcrt_trace.spv"); const SPV_HYBRID: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../shaders/hybrid_scatter.spv"); const SPV_GARSTANG: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../shaders/garstang_zenith.spv");` L3-4 module doc: "Loads pre-compiled SPIR-V shaders (built from GLSL at compile time via `include_bytes!`)". L44: "Must match HYBRID_THREADGROUP_SIZE in twilight.comp"
allFindings.why_wrong: None of the four .spv files exist, so `--features vulkan` cannot compile. The doc comment is doubly false: include_bytes! does not build anything, and there is no GLSL source or twilight.comp anywhere in the repo (find for *.glsl/*.comp/build.rs returns 0 hits, and Cargo.toml has no glslc/glslang/naga tooling). Comments reference internal details (HYBRID_THREADGROUP_SIZE) of a file that has never existed. Note the 1,401-line host code itself IS coherent: with stub .spv files, `cargo check -p twilight-gpu --features vulkan` passes, including a complete ash pipeline/descriptor/fence/Drop implementation and a real batched scan_batch (L606-890).
allFindings.recommendation: Either author the four GLSL compute shaders plus a build.rs invoking glslc (and add a CI job building --features vulkan), or delete vulkan.rs, the `vulkan` feature, and its ash/gpu-allocator dependencies until shaders exist.

allFindings.title: cuda.rs embeds nonexistent twilight.cu and documents constants inside the missing file
allFindings.evidence: L24-25: `/// Embedded CUDA C shader source.\nconst CUDA_SOURCE: &str = include_str!("../shaders/twilight.cu");` L20-22: "Block size for the hybrid kernel. Must match HYBRID_BLOCK_SIZE in twilight.cu (256 threads = 8 warps of 32)."
allFindings.why_wrong: twilight.cu does not exist, so `--features cuda` cannot compile (confirmed ground truth). The comment asserts agreement with a constant in a file that has never existed in the repo, and the crate README claims "Hand-written `.cu` shaders ... Targets compute capability 7.0+" for this backend. The host code is otherwise coherent cudarc 0.19 usage (nvrtc compile at L99-105, four kernel handles, launch_builder dispatches) and type-checks with a stub .cu, but it has never been compiled or run in this repo.
allFindings.recommendation: Write the actual twilight.cu implementing single_scatter_spectrum/mcrt_trace_photon/hybrid_scatter/garstang_zenith entry points and add a CI compile check, or remove cuda.rs and the `cuda` feature.

allFindings.title: wgpu_backend.rs embeds nonexistent twilight.wgsl and describes its internals (@workgroup_size(256), subgroupAdd) as fact
allFindings.evidence: L15-16: `/// Embedded WGSL shader source.\nconst WGSL_SOURCE: &str = include_str!("../shaders/twilight.wgsl");` L306-309: "Hybrid v2: dispatch nw workgroups of 256 threads (hardcoded in WGSL via @workgroup_size(256)). ... reduce via subgroupAdd() + workgroup shared memory."
allFindings.why_wrong: twilight.wgsl does not exist, so `--features webgpu` cannot compile. The comments describe concrete attributes and reduction strategy of a WGSL module that has never existed, and pipeline creation at L149-152 names four entry points ("single_scatter_spectrum", "mcrt_trace_photon", "hybrid_scatter", "garstang_zenith") in that nonexistent module. Host code type-checks with a stub (verified) and is coherent wgpu 28 usage (bind group layout, staging-buffer readback via map_async/PollType::Wait), but it is dead code presented in the README as the shipped WASM/browser story.
allFindings.recommendation: Author twilight.wgsl with the four @compute entry points (noting subgroupAdd requires the SUBGROUP feature, which L78 `required_features: wgpu::Features::empty()` does not request — fix that too if implementing), or delete the backend and the `webgpu` feature.

allFindings.title: "Cross-backend parity tests ensure all backends produce identical physics" is impossible: 3 of 4 backends can't compile and the parity test silently no-ops
allFindings.evidence: README L131: "Cross-backend parity tests with CPU f64 oracle ensure all backends produce identical physics." L239: "validates all GPU backends against them with documented f32 tolerance bounds." tests.rs L1548-1552: `let mut backends = init_all_backends(); if backends.len() < 2 { // Need at least 2 backends to compare\n return; }`
allFindings.why_wrong: The vulkan/cuda/webgpu test modules (tests.rs:1068 `#[cfg(feature = "vulkan")] mod layer4_vulkan`, :1385 cuda, :1433 webgpu — 20 #[test] functions total) are behind features that fail to compile, so they have never run. The only buildable configuration has at most one backend (Metal), so cross_backend_single_scatter_parity always returns early without comparing anything, and every backend test uses the silent-skip pattern (`let Some(gpu) = try_vulkan() else { return };`, tests.rs:1083 etc.). "Ensure all backends produce identical physics" has therefore never been checked for any pair of backends. This contradicts DISORT/libRadtran-style verification practice the README invokes: a parity suite that cannot execute verifies nothing.
allFindings.recommendation: State that parity is verified only for Metal vs the CPU f64 oracle. Make GPU tests fail (or be #[ignore]d with a reason) rather than silently pass when no device/backend is present, and gate the parity claims on CI that actually runs at least two backends.

allFindings.title: GPU feature table asserts ~33 concrete shader-engineering features for Vulkan/CUDA/WebGPU shaders that don't exist
allFindings.evidence: "| Feature | Metal | Vulkan | CUDA | WebGPU |" ... "| Kahan compensated summation | x | x | x | x |" ... "| Subgroup/SIMD reduction | `simd_sum` | `subgroupAdd` | `__shfl_down_sync` | `__shfl_down_sync`->`subgroupAdd` |" ... "| Hybrid: 1 threadgroup per wavelength, 256 threads | x | x | x | x |"
allFindings.why_wrong: Every cell in the Vulkan, CUDA, and WebGPU columns describes precision/performance engineering (half-b ray-sphere intersection, boundary snapping, Kahan summation, Snell's-law shadow rays, named SIMD intrinsics like `__shfl_down_sync` and `subgroupAdd`) inside shader files that do not exist. Only the Metal column can correspond to real code (twilight.metal). Citing specific intrinsics per API gives the table false authority — it reads as verified engineering but is unfalsifiable vapor for 3 of 4 columns.
allFindings.recommendation: Reduce the table to a single Metal column (or a Metal row list), and move the Vulkan/CUDA/WebGPU columns to a 'planned' design note if the host scaffolding is kept.

allFindings.title: Crate-level README, lib.rs doc, and Cargo.toml description repeat the four-backend fiction, including "compiled independently" and "verified by a shared CPU oracle"
allFindings.evidence: L3: "Four backends, each hand-tuned for its native GPU API. All backends produce identical physics output, verified by a shared CPU oracle test suite." L9: "GLSL shaders compiled to SPIR-V." L15: "All four backends are behind Cargo feature flags and compiled independently." lib.rs L3: "Provides four native GPU backends for maximum performance on every platform". Cargo.toml L6: "description = \"GPU compute backends for twilight MCRT (CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, WebGPU)\""
allFindings.why_wrong: Three of the four features cannot be compiled at all (missing shader files), directly contradicting "compiled independently"; no GLSL exists to be "compiled to SPIR-V"; and nothing but Metal has ever been validated against the oracle, contradicting "All backends produce identical physics output, verified". This description would also ship to crates.io via Cargo.toml, propagating the fabrication into the package registry.
allFindings.recommendation: Rewrite all three to describe one Metal backend plus (if kept) explicitly-labelled shader-less host scaffolding for future backends.

allFindings.title: Vulkan/CUDA/wgpu host implementations are coherent but are ~2,400 lines of dead, never-executed code with latent runtime limits
allFindings.evidence: L317: "descriptor_count: 3 * 64, // 3 buffers x up to 64 dispatches" with L322 `.max_sets(64)`, while scan_batch L639-643 allocates `vec![self.desc_set_layout; n]` descriptor sets for n = requests.len() with no n<=64 guard.
allFindings.why_wrong: I verified by stubbing the missing shader files that all three backends type-check (cargo check passes for --features vulkan, cuda, webgpu), so the host code is real ash/cudarc/wgpu API usage, not hallucinated Rust. But it has never been executed: buffer-layout agreement with hypothetical shaders, the wgpu entry-point names, and limits like the 64-set descriptor pool (a batch of >64 SZA points would fail at runtime with VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_POOL_MEMORY; the prayer pipeline is documented at ~50 points, leaving little headroom) are all unvalidated. Keeping ~2,400 lines of uncompilable-by-default, untestable code in main misleads readers and rots silently.
allFindings.recommendation: Delete the three backends (with the buffers.rs packing layer retained for Metal) or move them to a clearly-labelled experimental branch. If kept, add CI `cargo check` per feature with committed stub-free shaders, and size the Vulkan descriptor pool from requests.len().

allFindings.title: "GPU is the default compute backend" but the CLI hard-wires only the Metal feature — no other backend is reachable even in principle
allFindings.evidence: `default = ["gpu"]` / `gpu = ["dep:twilight-gpu", "twilight-cpu/gpu"]` and L21: `twilight-gpu = { workspace = true, optional = true, features = ["metal"] }`; README L138: "GPU is the default compute backend. Use `--cpu` to opt out."
allFindings.why_wrong: Even if the Vulkan/CUDA/WebGPU shaders existed, the shipped binary could never use them: the only feature the CLI (and twilight-cpu/gpu) ever enables is `metal`. So the README's platform story ("AMD/Intel/Android/Linux" via Vulkan, "NVIDIA" via CUDA per lib.rs:5-8) is unreachable from the product, and the default workspace build pulls objc2/objc2-metal on every platform, making the 'GPU by default' promise macOS-only at best.
allFindings.recommendation: Document that GPU-by-default means Metal/macOS only. If other backends are ever implemented, make the CLI's gpu feature select the backend per target_os instead of hardcoding metal.

allFindings.title: Claimed GPU test counts (139 in root README, 99 in crate README) are inconsistent and include 20 tests that can never compile
allFindings.evidence: README L231: "| `twilight-gpu` | 139 | Buffer packing, f64 oracle, Metal + Vulkan parity, cross-backend physics, 11 parity tests, benchmarks |"; crate README L31: "99 tests."
allFindings.why_wrong: Static count of #[test] functions: 93 compile under default features (41 buffers.rs + 21 oracle.rs + 13 parity.rs + 18 ungated tests.rs) and 133 with metal; neither 139 nor 99 corresponds to a buildable configuration. The advertised "Metal + Vulkan parity" and "cross-backend physics" coverage counts 11 vulkan-gated, 4 cuda-gated, and 5 webgpu-gated tests (tests.rs:1068, 1385, 1433) that are behind features which fail to compile, plus a cross-backend test that early-returns with fewer than 2 backends — so the claimed coverage includes tests that have never executed once.
allFindings.recommendation: Report the count from an actual `cargo test -p twilight-gpu --features metal` run, drop "Vulkan parity / cross-backend" from the coverage description, and reconcile the two READMEs.

allFindings.title: GpuConfig::polarized documents a --fast scalar shader path that does not exist; the flag is a no-op
allFindings.evidence: "When false (`--fast` mode), the shaders use scalar radiance tracking (P11 phase function only). This is slightly faster but loses the ~0.5-2% polarization correction to intensity." followed by "NOTE: GPU shaders currently always run Stokes internally. This flag is reserved for a future scalar shader path optimization."
allFindings.why_wrong: The first paragraph describes concrete behavior ("the shaders use scalar radiance tracking", a quantified speed/accuracy tradeoff) for a code path the trailing NOTE admits does not exist. No backend reads `config.polarized`. Documenting unimplemented behavior in present tense, with invented percentages, is a miniature of the crate's wider pattern; at least here the NOTE discloses it.
allFindings.recommendation: Move the scalar-path description into the NOTE as future work (or remove the field until implemented) so the doc only states what the code does.

reviewed.summary: This is indeed the most solid subsystem: the SPA implementation faithfully follows Reda & Andreas (NREL/TP-560-34302) including the canonical 2003-10-17 Golden CO reference test (zenith 50.11162, azimuth 194.34024, passing), and the pure-Rust DAF/SPK Type-2 Chebyshev reader is excellent — I ran the repo's own ignored Horizons tests against the real de440.bsp and got 8 mm agreement at J2000. However, the DE440 backend's advertised "sub-arcsecond / ±0.001 arcsec" topocentric accuracy is fabricated: the measured end-to-end zenith error is 24–89 arcsec (0.0068°–0.0248° vs SPA across 2024, from the project's own test output), dominated by a missing solar aberration correction and the deliberately simplified earth-rotation chain, making the "precision" backend ~20-80x less accurate than the default SPA. Secondary issues: two VSOP87 L0 terms missing vs the NREL table, a sign error on the equation of time in the (unused) sunrise/sunset output fields, decorative input fields, a fictional feature flag, and a DE440-only azimuth time-clamp bug in the pipeline that corrupts terrain-horizon lookups in positive timezones. None of these materially shift prayer times for the default SPA path, whose binary-search crossing logic is correct.

allFindings.title: DE440 backend claims milliarcsecond/sub-arcsecond topocentric accuracy; measured accuracy is 24-89 arcsec, worse than the default SPA backend
allFindings.evidence: de440.rs:7-8: "Accuracy: ~0.001 arcsecond (milliarcsecond) for the Sun's position, approximately 1000x more precise than SPA (±0.0003 degrees = ±1.08\")". README.md:19: "Optional JPL DE440 ephemeris for sub-arcsecond solar positioning". Contradicted by the project's own test comment at de440.rs:400-401: "our simplified Earth rotation may introduce up to ~0.05°" and de440.rs:618-624 asserting only max_diff < 0.1°. I ran the ignored tests with the real BSP: "Max zenith difference across 12 months: 0.0248°" (= 89 arcsec), minimum 0.0068° in July.
allFindings.why_wrong: The geometric ICRF position from the SPK reader is indeed mas-level (verified 8 mm vs Horizons), but the delivered topocentric zenith goes through a chain the code itself labels simplified: UT1≈UTC (de440.rs:136-137, up to 0.9 s = 13.5 arcsec of Earth rotation), a 4-term IAU 1980 nutation (earth_rotation.rs:137-171, ~0.5 arcsec residual vs the full 63-term series SPA uses), zeta_A set equal to z_A in the Lieske precession (earth_rotation.rs:402-408), no polar motion, and no aberration (see separate finding). Measured against SPA (±0.0003° per Reda & Andreas 2004) the DE440 path is 0.0068-0.0248° off — i.e., the backend marketed as 1000x MORE precise is ~20-80x LESS precise end-to-end. ~0.025° zenith error corresponds to roughly 5-15 s in crossing times at mid-latitudes.
allFindings.recommendation: Either implement the missing physics (apparent place with aberration, full IAU 2000A/2006 precession-nutation, UT1-UTC) or rewrite the claims to state honest accuracy (~0.01-0.03° topocentric, geometric ephemeris mas-level). Add a non-ignored regression test asserting the actual DE440-vs-SPA agreement bound.

allFindings.title: DE440 path uses geometric Sun position; no light-time/annual aberration correction anywhere in the chain
allFindings.evidence: pub fn sun_position_icrf(&mut self, tdb_seconds: f64) -> Result<[f64; 3], De440Error> { let pos = self.spk.position_chain(SUN, EARTH, tdb_seconds)?; Ok(pos) } — then icrf_to_topocentric() applies only precession/nutation/GAST/ENU. Case-insensitive grep for aberration/light-time across twilight-solar/src matches only the SPA path (spa.rs:374-375: "// Aberration correction" with delta_tau = -20.4898/(3600.0*r)).
allFindings.why_wrong: Apparent solar place differs from the geometric place by planetary aberration ~20.5 arcsec (annual aberration constant kappa = 20.49552", Astronomical Almanac; Meeus Ch. 23; SPA itself applies Delta-tau = -20.4898"/R per Reda & Andreas eq. 16). Omitting it introduces a systematic ~0.0057° bias in solar longitude — exactly matching the measured 0.0068° floor of the DE440-vs-SPA zenith difference in test_de440_vs_spa_multiple_epochs output. Effect on zenith-crossing times is ~1-2 s (small for prayer times), but it singlehandedly invalidates the milliarcsecond claim by 4 orders of magnitude.
allFindings.recommendation: Apply light-time iteration (evaluate Sun at t - r/c) plus observer-velocity stellar aberration, or at minimum the SPA-style -20.4898"/R longitude correction, before the frame rotation.

allFindings.title: DE440 azimuth_at_hour clamps negative UTC hours to 0 and truncates minutes, corrupting terrain-horizon adjustment in positive timezones
allFindings.evidence: de.solar_position(..., (utc_hour as i32).max(0), (((utc_hour - (utc_hour as i32) as f64) * 60.0) as i32).max(0), 0, ...) — where utc_hour = fractional_hour - self.spa_input.timezone. By contrast zenith_at_hour (lines 236-256) passes the negative fractional UTC hour straight through, which de440::zenith_at_hour handles correctly via linear negative-hour arithmetic.
allFindings.why_wrong: For the DE440 backend with timezone > local sunrise hour (e.g., Jakarta UTC+7, sunrise ~05:45 local gives utc_hour = -1.25), the .max(0) clamps the evaluation to 00:00 UTC — hours away from the actual event — so the sun azimuth fed to profile.angle_at(az) at pipeline.rs:523 is wrong by tens of degrees. That selects the wrong terrain horizon angle, which feeds effective_sunrise_sza and re-runs find_zenith_crossing (pipeline.rs:525-526), directly shifting the reported sunrise/sunset when --de440 plus a horizon profile are used. It also corrupts solar_azimuth_evening (pipeline.rs:559-560) used as the RT view direction. The SPA branch is unaffected. Even for positive utc_hour, seconds are silently dropped (passes 0).
allFindings.recommendation: Reuse the same negative-hour-tolerant path as zenith_at_hour: add an azimuth_at_hour to De440 that accepts a fractional UTC hour (or convert via total seconds with proper day rollover), and remove the .max(0) clamps.

allFindings.title: sun_rise_transit_set has the equation-of-time sign inverted (and outputs UTC while documented as local)
allFindings.evidence: Line 570: let transit = 12.0 + eot / 60.0 - longitude / 15.0; — but the polar branches at lines 560 and 564 use the opposite (correct) sign: return (12.0 - eot / 60.0 - longitude / 15.0, 0.0, 24.0);
allFindings.why_wrong: Apparent solar noon in UTC is 12h - EoT - longitude/15 (EoT = apparent minus mean solar time, NREL Reda & Andreas convention where E is limited to ±20 min). The two branches of the same function disagree on the sign; the normal branch is the wrong one. For the canonical NREL case (2003-10-17, lon -105.1786, EoT ≈ +14.64 min) the code yields transit 19.256 h vs the correct 18.768 h UTC (NREL Table A5: 11:46:04 LST) — a 29-minute error, up to ±33 min through the year, inherited by the sunrise/sunset outputs. Additionally SpaOutput documents these fields as "(fractional hour, local)" (spa.rs:125-130) but no timezone is applied. Mitigating: the pipeline and CLI never read SpaOutput.sunrise/sunset/stn — they use find_zenith_crossing bisection — so prayer times are unaffected today; but the fields are public API, wrong, and covered by zero tests (no assertion against NREL Table A5 sunrise 06:12:43 / sunset 17:20:19).
allFindings.recommendation: Fix the sign to 12.0 - eot/60.0, apply (or document) the timezone, and add an assertion against the NREL Table A5 rise/transit/set values — or delete the fields if they are intentionally superseded by find_zenith_crossing.

allFindings.title: VSOP87 L0 table has 62 of NREL's 64 terms (two 102-amplitude terms missing) plus two frequency typos; test tolerances loosened 30x to mask it
