allFindings.evidence: L0_TERMS contains 62 entries (counted programmatically; NREL spa.c / Table A4.2 has 64). The sequence jumps from (103.0, 0.636, 4694.003) directly to (99.0, 6.21, 2146.17) at spa_tables.rs:50-51, omitting NREL's {102, 0.976, 15720.839} and {102, 4.267, 7.114}. Also (3418.0, 2.8289, 3.5232) should be 3.5231 and (492.0, 4.205, 775.522) should be 775.523. The reference test admits it: spa.rs:820 "// Earth heliocentric longitude (allow wider tolerance due to table truncation)" with assert tolerance 0.01°.
allFindings.why_wrong: Reda & Andreas 2004 (NREL/TP-560-34302) Table A4.2 and the reference spa.c use 64 L0 terms; the ±0.0003° accuracy claim (lib.rs:6, README) presumes the complete subset. Each missing term contributes up to 102e-8 rad ≈ 0.21 arcsec, combined worst case ~0.42" = 1.2e-4° — comparable to the entire advertised error budget. The NREL reference test asserts zenith only to 0.01° (spa.rs:840), 33x looser than the claimed ±0.0003°, so the claim is not actually verified by any test. Prayer-time impact is negligible (<0.1 s), but a claimed-faithful reference implementation silently deviates from its reference.
allFindings.recommendation: Add the two missing L0 terms and fix the two frequency typos from NREL Table A4.2, then tighten the reference-case assertions (L to ~1e-5°, zenith/azimuth to ~0.001°) so the ±0.0003° claim is enforced.

allFindings.title: README 'validated to 8 meters vs JPL Horizons' matches no assertion: tests are #[ignore]d, silently skip without the BSP, and assert <1 km (actual measured agreement is 8 mm)
allFindings.evidence: README.md:117: "DE440 validated to 8 meters vs JPL Horizons." The test asserts: assert!(dr < 1.0, "position error {} km exceeds 1 km tolerance", dr); (de440.rs:457) and is #[test] #[ignore] with a silent early-return when the file is absent: let path = match get_de440_path() { Some(p) => p, None => return }; (de440.rs:424-427). Running with the real BSP: "Total position error: 0.000008 km" (8 mm) at J2000 and 25 mm at 2024-03-18.
allFindings.why_wrong: The headline validation number appears in no test: the in-repo assertion is 1 km (125,000x looser than 8 m), the tests never run in default CI (all 10 DE440/Horizons tests are ignored — the advertised '73 tests' = 63 run + 10 ignored), and they pass as no-ops when data/de440.bsp is missing. Ironically the real agreement is 8 millimeters, so the README figure looks like a garbled transcription of the true number — conservative, but unsupported by any executable check.
allFindings.recommendation: Tighten the Horizons assertions to the demonstrated level (e.g., dr < 0.001 km), make the tests fail loudly (or skip with explicit notice) when the BSP is absent, and correct the README figure to the measured value.

allFindings.title: SpaInput fields slope, azm_rotation, and atmos_refract are accepted but never used; refraction constants hardcoded
allFindings.evidence: Struct documents "Surface slope (degrees from horizontal...)", "Surface azimuth rotation...", "Atmospheric refraction at sunset/sunrise (degrees, default 0.5667)" — but grep shows slope/azm_rotation/atmos_refract are only ever assigned in struct literals, never read. The refraction acceptance threshold hardcodes the value instead of using the field: let delta_e = if e0 >= -(0.26667 + 0.5667) { ... (spa.rs:491), and sunrise target hardcodes sun_rise_transit_set(..., -0.8333) (spa.rs:654). The NREL reference test even sets slope: 30.0, azm_rotation: -10.0 (spa.rs:798-799) as if surface-incidence output existed.
allFindings.why_wrong: NREL SPA uses slope/azm_rotation to compute the surface incidence angle (Reda & Andreas section A.4.4) and uses atmos_refract in the refraction acceptance condition. Here the incidence-angle step is unimplemented and the configurable refraction is fictional — the API advertises configurability that has no effect, which can silently mislead a caller who changes atmos_refract expecting different sunrise behavior. Also dead-code in the same vein: earth_rotation::refraction_correction (earth_rotation.rs:475-488) is called only by its own unit test, so the DE440 path never applies refraction (harmless for twilight depressions, but it also misapplies Bennett's apparent-to-true formula to a true elevation input — Saemundsson 1986 is the correct inverse, as SPA uses).
allFindings.recommendation: Either wire atmos_refract into the two hardcoded sites and implement the incidence angle, or remove the three fields (and the unused refraction_correction) so the API matches reality.

allFindings.title: lib.rs claims the DE440 backend is gated behind a 'de440' feature flag that does not exist
allFindings.evidence: "The SPA backend is always available and serves as the default. The DE440 backend requires the `de440` feature flag and a path to the BSP file." — but crates/twilight-solar/Cargo.toml contains no [features] section at all ([dependencies] libm only), and de440/spk/earth_rotation are unconditionally `pub mod` (lib.rs:18-20).
allFindings.why_wrong: The documented build configuration is fictitious: there is no cargo feature named de440 anywhere in the workspace. Harmless in effect (the backend is always compiled and only activates when a path is supplied), but it is a fabricated capability description of the kind the maintainer is auditing for, and anyone trying `--features de440` will get an 'unknown feature' style mismatch with the docs.
allFindings.recommendation: Delete the feature-flag sentence (the path-based opt-in is the real gate), or actually add the feature if binary-size gating is desired.

allFindings.title: Persistent-twilight detection hardcodes SZA < 106.0 deg, untied to the actual Fajr/Isha thresholds in use
allFindings.evidence: let max_sza_deg = engine.compute_max_sza(); let persistent_twilight = max_sza_deg.map(|sza| sza < 106.0).unwrap_or(false);
allFindings.why_wrong: 106.0° (16° depression) is a magic constant. The engine's actual Fajr/Isha thresholds come from the RT+vision model and commonly correspond to ~13-18° depression (SZA 103-108°). On a date where max SZA = 107°, an 18°-based threshold search returns None (no Fajr) yet persistent_twilight = false, so the CLI's high-latitude messaging (main.rs:1223-1224 "N/A (persistent twilight — sky never fully dark)") can mislabel why a time is missing; conversely 16°-based methods get flagged persistent while their crossing still exists at SZA 105. Conventionally astronomical (persistent) twilight is defined at 18° depression (SZA 108), so even as a fixed convention the constant is nonstandard. The 0.5 h sampling in compute_max_sza is fine since the SZA extremum is flat.
allFindings.recommendation: Compare max SZA against the actual threshold SZA being searched for each prayer time (per-output persistent flags), or at minimum use the conventional 108° and document the choice.

finding.title: DE440 backend claims milliarcsecond/sub-arcsecond topocentric accuracy; measured accuracy is 24-89 arcsec, worse than the default SPA backend
finding.evidence: de440.rs:7-8: "Accuracy: ~0.001 arcsecond (milliarcsecond) for the Sun's position, approximately 1000x more precise than SPA (±0.0003 degrees = ±1.08\")". README.md:19: "Optional JPL DE440 ephemeris for sub-arcsecond solar positioning". Contradicted by the project's own test comment at de440.rs:400-401: "our simplified Earth rotation may introduce up to ~0.05°" and de440.rs:618-624 asserting only max_diff < 0.1°. I ran the ignored tests with the real BSP: "Max zenith difference across 12 months: 0.0248°" (= 89 arcsec), minimum 0.0068° in July.
finding.why_wrong: The geometric ICRF position from the SPK reader is indeed mas-level (verified 8 mm vs Horizons), but the delivered topocentric zenith goes through a chain the code itself labels simplified: UT1≈UTC (de440.rs:136-137, up to 0.9 s = 13.5 arcsec of Earth rotation), a 4-term IAU 1980 nutation (earth_rotation.rs:137-171, ~0.5 arcsec residual vs the full 63-term series SPA uses), zeta_A set equal to z_A in the Lieske precession (earth_rotation.rs:402-408), no polar motion, and no aberration (see separate finding). Measured against SPA (±0.0003° per Reda & Andreas 2004) the DE440 path is 0.0068-0.0248° off — i.e., the backend marketed as 1000x MORE precise is ~20-80x LESS precise end-to-end. ~0.025° zenith error corresponds to roughly 5-15 s in crossing times at mid-latitudes.
finding.recommendation: Either implement the missing physics (apparent place with aberration, full IAU 2000A/2006 precession-nutation, UT1-UTC) or rewrite the claims to state honest accuracy (~0.01-0.03° topocentric, geometric ephemeris mas-level). Add a non-ignored regression test asserting the actual DE440-vs-SPA agreement bound.

verdict.reasoning: Core claim verified by direct reproduction. de440.rs:7-8 states "Accuracy: ~0.001 arcsecond (milliarcsecond) for the Sun's position, approximately 1000x more precise than SPA"; repeated at lib.rs:8-9 and README.md:19,209. I ran the ignored tests with the real BSP (data/de440.bsp exists): the geometric ICRF vector is genuinely mas-level (8e-6 km vs Horizons), but the delivered topocentric zenith differs from SPA by 0.0066-0.0248 deg across 2024 (reproduced the reviewer's numbers exactly, max in December). All cited simplifications are real: UT1=UTC at de440.rs:136-137; 4-term IAU1980 nutation at earth_rotation.rs:160-164; zeta_A=z_A at earth_rotation.rs:402-408; no polar motion; no aberration anywhere in the DE440 path (grep: aberration appears only in spa.rs:374-375, the -20.4898/R term per Reda & Andreas 2004). HOWEVER, the reviewer misattributed their own headline number: SPA's zenith output includes the Meeus refraction correction when e0 > -0.83 deg (spa.rs:491-499), while the DE440 path never applies refraction (earth_rotation.rs:475 refraction_correction is dead code, called only by its own unit test). At the test's daytime elevations (30-53 deg) refraction is 0.012-0.028 deg, which dominates the December 0.0248 deg figure; the reviewer's stated error chain (aberration 20.5" + UT1 + nutation 0.5" + polar motion 0.3") cannot sum to 89" in 2024 when UT1-UTC ~ 0. I wrote a temporary test comparing both backends at Fajr depth (z=108 deg, where SPA's refraction term is zero, i.e., the regime that actually sets prayer times): the genuine astronomical error of the DE440 path is 14-21 arcsec (matching the missing annual aberration almost exactly), and the measured Fajr-18deg crossing shift at Mecca is +1.5 to +2.5 s, not the claimed 5-15 s (also note de440.rs:163-166 truncates time to integer seconds, quantizing crossings to ~1 s). So the thesis stands at the ~15-20x-worse-than-SPA level (20" vs 1.08"), not 20-80x, and the prayer-time impact is roughly 2-5 s at mid-latitudes. The pipeline does swap DE440 in as the primary engine when a BSP path is given (twilight-cpu/src/pipeline.rs:224-227), and the refraction inconsistency between supposedly interchangeable backends (de440.rs:178 "Mirrors spa::find_zenith_crossing() for API compatibility") would additionally corrupt sunrise/sunset (z=90.833) by ~0.5 deg / ~2 min — a distinct bug the reviewer did not flag.
verdict.correction: The accuracy claim is genuinely fabricated relative to the delivered output: the mas-level figure applies only to the geometric ICRF vector (verified 8 mm vs Horizons), while the delivered topocentric zenith carries ~14-21 arcsec of astronomical error, dominated by the complete absence of the ~20.5" annual aberration correction (present in SPA at spa.rs:374-375, absent everywhere in the DE440 path), plus smaller UT1/nutation/precession simplifications — i.e., the backend marketed as 1000x more precise than SPA is ~15-20x LESS precise. The reviewer's 24-89 arcsec daytime measurement is real but conflates this with a separate inconsistency: SPA's zenith is refraction-corrected above the horizon (spa.rs:491-499) while DE440's never is (refraction_correction at earth_rotation.rs:475 is dead code), and that refraction mismatch (0.012-0.028 deg) dominates the December 89" figure. At twilight depths where Fajr/Isha are computed, SPA applies no refraction either, and the measured Fajr-18deg crossing shift is +1.5 to +2.5 s at Mecca (roughly 2-5 s at mid-latitudes), not 5-15 s. Severity remains high: overstated-by-~20,000x precision claim on an optional backend that is actually worse than the default, plus inconsistent refraction semantics that would shift DE440-backed sunrise/sunset by ~2 minutes.

reviewed.summary: The skyglow subsystem is a façade: a Garstang-style single-scatter integrator exists (garstang.rs) and its geometry is actually correct, but it is dead code — nothing in the pipeline or CLI ever calls it, and it contains two compounding magnitude errors (~70x underestimate) duplicated in the Metal kernel. The path actually wired into prayer times (quick_estimate -> pipeline.rs radiance injection) commits a category error: it injects the VIIRS ground-level upward radiance directly as observer sky radiance, ~60-300x brighter than the crate's own calibrated zenith-luminance mapping. Empirically verified: enabling --skyglow at Bortle 1 (pristine sky) deletes Fajr, and Bortle >=2 deletes all prayer times (N/A), while the CLI prints a fabricated "~N min shift" from an uncited heuristic that has no connection to the actual computation. Documented capabilities (MCRT ground-source tracer, embedded VIIRS lookup, World Bank S3 tiles, 5000K LED spectrum, compute_skyglow) do not exist.

allFindings.title: Pipeline injects VIIRS ground-emission radiance as sky radiance, deleting Fajr/Isha at even pristine Bortle settings
allFindings.evidence: lib.rs: `let zenith_lum = bortle::radiance_to_zenith_luminance(radiance_nw); ... let (spectral, num_wl) = spectrum::mixed_spectrum(radiance_nw, led_fraction);` where spectrum.rs does `let total_si = total_radiance_nw * 1e-5;` (the FULL VIIRS radiance becomes band-integrated sky radiance in W/m^2/sr). pipeline.rs: `sr.radiance[i] += sg.spectral_radiance[i];`. Empirical: `twilight-cli pray --skyglow --bortle 1` -> 'Fajr (true dawn): N/A (threshold not crossed)'; `--bortle 2`..`5` -> ALL of Fajr/Isha-abyad/Isha-ahmar = 'N/A (threshold not crossed in scan range)' while printing 'Light pollution: Bortle 5 (~7 min shift)'. Baseline without --skyglow: Fajr 02:30:19.
allFindings.why_wrong: VIIRS DNB measures the upward radiance of city lights as seen looking DOWN from orbit; the artificial radiance an observer sees looking UP at the sky is the small scattered fraction, ~2-3 orders of magnitude lower (this conversion is exactly what Garstang 1986/Falchi 2016 modeling exists to do). The injected spectrum integrates to R*1e-5 W/m^2/sr (x6.26 angular factor at 10 deg from quick_estimate_at_angle), i.e. photopic ~0.13 cd/m^2 for Bortle 5 (R=6) — 43x above the 0.003 cd/m^2 Isha threshold and ~60x brighter than the crate's OWN calibrated artificial zenith luminance (0.092*6^0.72 = 0.33 mcd/m^2 = 3.3e-4 cd/m^2). At R=100 the discrepancy is ~135x (measured: 341 mcd injected vs 2.5 mcd calibrated). Consequence: the sky never crosses the threshold, so the feature outputs no prayer times at all for any realistic setting — for software intended for the ummah this silently destroys the result it advertises to refine.
allFindings.recommendation: Convert VIIRS radiance to artificial sky radiance BEFORE injection: either run the garstang.rs integration (after fixing its own bugs) or scale the lamp spectrum so its photopic luminance equals the calibrated zenith luminance from bortle::radiance_to_zenith_luminance (mcd/m^2 -> cd/m^2 -> spectral via the lamp SPD shape). Add a regression test asserting that quick_estimate's spectral_radiance, pushed through twilight_threshold::photopic_luminance, agrees with its own zenith_luminance field.

allFindings.title: Advertised 'Garstang RT skyglow model', MCRT ground-source tracer, and VIIRS data sources are never used or do not exist
allFindings.evidence: lib.rs docs: '2. **MCRT ground-source tracer** (nearby sources, <30km): Full photon tracing from ground-level light sources... Captures cloud reflection, terrain blocking', '- **Embedded lookup** (~10km resolution, always available offline) - **World Bank S3** (~750m COG tiles, free, no auth)', and 'For the full spatially-resolved computation, use [`garstang::compute_skyglow`]'. README.md:125: 'Garstang RT skyglow model... Estimates zenith brightness added to the twilight signal'. grep confirms: `garstang::compute_skyglow` does not exist; no MCRT ground-source tracer exists anywhere in the workspace; the only RadianceSource impl is ConstantRadiance; and garstang::{zenith_brightness, bin_sources, directional_brightness, viirs_to_flux} have ZERO callers outside crates/twilight-skyglow itself — the pipeline/CLI use only quick_estimate_at_angle (bortle power-law + lamp spectrum).
allFindings.why_wrong: These are fabricated capabilities presented as real. The quantity 'added to the twilight signal' is not the Garstang RT zenith brightness — it is raw VIIRS radiance spread over a lamp SPD. The `mcrt_radius_km` field in SkyglowConfig (lib.rs:52-53) is decorative; SkyglowConfig itself is never constructed by any consumer. The doc-link to a nonexistent function would also fail rustdoc link checking.
allFindings.recommendation: Either wire garstang::zenith_brightness/bin_sources into the pipeline (with real or constant radiance data) or delete the claims. Remove the MCRT-ground-tracer and data-source bullets from docs until implemented; fix README.md:125 to describe what is actually computed.

allFindings.title: Garstang single-scatter estimator divides by an extra 4*pi with already-normalized phase functions (12.6x underestimate), duplicated in Metal kernel
allFindings.evidence: garstang.rs:261: `let di = source_intensity / (4.0 * PI * r2) * sigma_total * p_average * extinction * dh;` while rayleigh_phase (line 273) is `3.0 / (16.0 * PI) * (1.0 + theta.cos().powi(2))` and HG (line 285) is `(1.0 - g * g) / (4.0 * PI * denom)` — both normalized so the integral over 4*pi sr equals 1. Metal twilight.metal:2253 has the identical `source_intensity / (4.0f * PI * r2) * sigma_total * p_avg * extinction * dh`.
allFindings.why_wrong: The standard single-scatter source term (cf. Garstang 1986 PASP 98:364; Chandrasekhar; libRadtran/MYSTIC convention) for a point source of intensity I [W/sr] is dL = (I/r^2) * sigma_s * P(theta) * exp(-tau_in - tau_out) * ds, where P is normalized to unit integral over the sphere — exactly the normalization these phase functions use (Rayleigh 3/(16*pi)(1+cos^2) integrates to 1). Dividing again by 4*pi double-counts the solid-angle normalization, making the result 4*pi ~ 12.57x too small. (Only with the alternative convention P_iso = 1, i.e. ∫P dΩ = 4π — as Garstang's own f(theta) — would a /4π be correct.) None of the 13 unit tests in garstang.rs checks absolute magnitude, so this is invisible to the test suite.
allFindings.recommendation: Remove the 4*pi from the denominator (keep unit-normalized phase functions), and add a test comparing zenith_brightness for a known source against a hand-computed analytic value or a published Garstang benchmark (e.g. Garstang 1989 Mt. Palomar/Boulder cases).

allFindings.title: Uplight/reflectance fraction re-applied to flux that is already satellite-measured upward flux; Garstang emission function omitted
allFindings.evidence: LightSource doc (lines 49-51): 'Total upward flux of this bin (W/sr). Derived from VIIRS radiance * pixel area'. Then lines 178-182: 'Simplified: effective_up ≈ uplight_fraction + ground_reflectance * 0.5' / `let effective_up = config.uplight_fraction + config.ground_reflectance * 0.5; let source_intensity = source.upward_flux * effective_up;` (default 0.10 + 0.15*0.5 = 0.175). Same in twilight.metal:2198-2199.
allFindings.why_wrong: In Garstang (1986) the uplight fraction F and ground reflectance G partition the TOTAL lamp output via his emission function psi(z) = (1/2pi)(2G(1-F)cos z + 0.554 F z^4). VIIRS-derived upward flux ALREADY IS the light that escaped upward (direct uplight + reflections), so multiplying by 0.175 again double-counts the shielding/reflection losses, suppressing the result ~5.7x (combined with the spurious 4*pi: ~72x total underestimate). Additionally, the source is treated as isotropic (constant W/sr in all directions) — Garstang's characteristic angular emission function, the defining feature of his model, is entirely absent, which mis-weights near-horizontal emission that dominates skyglow from distant cities. The 'effective_up = uplight + reflectance*0.5' partition itself is an invented formula appearing in no published Garstang variant.
allFindings.recommendation: If sources are VIIRS-derived, drop effective_up entirely (or use it only to back out total lamp output and then apply Garstang's psi(z) for the direction-dependent intensity toward each scattering point). Cite and implement the actual Garstang 1986 emission function if the model is to keep his name.

allFindings.title: Reported 'prayer shift minutes' is an invented formula with fabricated citations, disconnected from (and contradicted by) the actual computed shift
allFindings.evidence: bortle.rs: 'each doubling of sky brightness shifts twilight threshold by approximately 2-3 minutes (Garstang 1989, cross-checked with observations in Cinzano 2000)' ... `let natural_threshold = 0.05; ... 2.5 * (1.0 + ratio).log2()`. pipeline.rs computes skyglow_shift_minutes from this heuristic, NOT from the actual threshold-crossing difference. Empirical: with --skyglow --bortle 5 the CLI prints 'Light pollution: Bortle 5 (~7 min shift)' on the same screen where Fajr/Isha are 'N/A (threshold not crossed in scan range)'.
allFindings.why_wrong: Garstang 1989 (PASP 101:306) is about night-sky brightness predictions at observatory sites and Cinzano 2000 about DMSP satellite mapping — neither derives a minutes-per-doubling twilight-threshold shift; the 2.5*log2(1+L/0.05) form and the 0.05 mcd/m^2 'natural threshold' are unsourced. The formula also ignores latitude/season: the solar depression rate (deg/min) varies by more than 2x between the equator and 55 deg latitude, so a fixed minutes-per-doubling constant cannot be correct. Worst, the engine already computes the real shift implicitly (via the injected radiance moving the threshold crossing) — yet reports this unrelated heuristic, so the displayed number actively contradicts the displayed times.
allFindings.recommendation: Compute the shift as (threshold-crossing time with skyglow) minus (without skyglow) from the actual pipeline, or remove the field. Delete the false citations.

allFindings.title: VIIRS->zenith-luminance power law 'L = 0.092*R^0.72' attributed to Falchi et al. (2016) appears invented and contradicts the crate's own Bortle tables
allFindings.evidence: 'Uses the empirical relationship from Falchi et al. (2016): L_artificial = a * R^b where a=0.092 and b=0.72 are fit parameters derived from SQM-calibrated Garstang model inversions' / `0.092 * radiance_nw.powf(0.72)`. Self-inconsistency: BORTLE_VIIRS_RADIANCE[8]=100.0 with BORTLE_LUMINANCE_MCD[8]=7.0, but the formula gives 0.092*100^0.72 = 2.53 mcd/m^2 (2.8x off); for Bortle 9 (R=300, table 20.0 mcd) the formula gives 5.6 mcd (3.6x off). Consequently radiance_to_bortle(100.0) classifies a 'Bortle 8' radiance as class 7 — the test radiance_to_bortle_city (line 348-352) papers over this by accepting 7..=9.
allFindings.why_wrong: Falchi et al. 2016 (Science Advances, 'The new world atlas of artificial night sky brightness') contains no local pointwise VIIRS-radiance-to-zenith-luminance power law; their zenith brightness is a Garstang-type PSF integration of all VIIRS pixels within ~195 km, which cannot be reduced to a function of the local pixel alone. The constants 0.092/0.72 are presented with false provenance, and the two 'calibrations' in the same file disagree by up to 3.6x at the bright end, so at most one can be right.
allFindings.recommendation: Replace with a single internally consistent calibration (e.g. fit a*R^b through the BORTLE_VIIRS_RADIANCE/BORTLE_LUMINANCE_MCD pairs, or better, integrate radiance over a neighborhood per Falchi's method) and attribute it honestly as an in-house fit.

allFindings.title: SkyglowResult.zenith_luminance documented as cd/m^2 but holds mcd/m^2 (1000x label error)
allFindings.evidence: Field doc: '/// Artificial sky brightness at zenith (cd/m^2). pub zenith_luminance: f64,' but it is populated by `let zenith_lum = bortle::radiance_to_zenith_luminance(radiance_nw);` whose contract (bortle.rs:109) is '...to artificial zenith luminance (mcd/m^2)'. The lib.rs test quick_estimate_city asserts `result.zenith_luminance > 1.0` for R=100, which only makes sense in mcd (2.53); 2.53 cd/m^2 would be an absurd artificial zenith brightness (brighter than full-moon sky by ~1000x).
allFindings.why_wrong: cd/m^2 vs mcd/m^2 is a factor-1000 unit mismatch between doc contract and value. The threshold crate works in cd/m^2 (ThresholdConfig defaults 0.001-0.003 cd/m^2), so any future consumer trusting the field doc and comparing zenith_luminance against thresholds inherits a 1000x error.
allFindings.recommendation: Change the doc to mcd/m^2 (and the directional_luminance doc on line 83 likewise), or convert the stored value to cd/m^2. Add a unit suffix to the field name (zenith_luminance_mcd) as pipeline.rs already does for its output field.

allFindings.title: Earth-curvature correction is claimed in comments and a constant is declared for it, but no correction exists; integration extends to 200 km
allFindings.evidence: Line 39-40: '/// Mean Earth radius (m) for curvature correction. const EARTH_RADIUS: f64 = 6_371_000.0;' Line 195-197: 'With Earth curvature, this is slightly more complex, but for typical distances (<200km) and altitudes (<30km), the flat-Earth approximation with a curvature correction is adequate.' Yet the geometry uses pure flat-Earth `(d * d + h * h).sqrt()` and no curvature term appears anywhere in the optical-depth or scattering-angle code; EARTH_RADIUS is only used in offset_latlon for lat/lon binning. bin_sources default extends to radius_km=200 (config) with bins to `(50.0, radius_km, 20.0)`.
allFindings.why_wrong: Garstang (1989) explicitly added Earth-curvature terms because they matter for sources beyond roughly 50 km: at d=200 km the surface drops ~3.1 km below the observer's tangent plane, comparable to the 1.5 km aerosol scale height, so flat-Earth slant optical depths and source-to-scatter distances are substantially wrong for the outer bins. The comment asserts a correction that the code does not contain.
allFindings.recommendation: Either implement the Garstang 1989 curvature terms (or cap the integration radius near 50 km) or correct the comments and remove the misleading EARTH_RADIUS doc string.

allFindings.title: Angular model constants hand-tuned away from the cited Duriscoe fit; azimuthal city-direction model is invented and dead code despite docs tying it to Fajr/Isha viewing geometry
allFindings.evidence: 'Duriscoe found A ≈ 10, B ≈ 2.5 from all-sky photometry... We use A=8.0, B=2.2 which better matches Garstang' (no Garstang comparison exists anywhere in the repo). azimuthal_enhancement hard-codes `sigma_deg = (10.0 / source_distance_km).atan()` ('typical city with 10km radius') and `peak = (50.0 / d).powf(0.5).min(3.0)` with no citation. grep confirms azimuthal_enhancement, angular::directional_brightness, and twilight_observation_factor have no callers outside angular.rs, even though the module doc (lines 7-9) says 'the relevant viewing direction is toward the horizon at the azimuth of sunset (Isha) or sunrise (Fajr)' — the pipeline applies only the elevation factor at a fixed 10 deg via the CLI, and LightSource.azimuth_deg is stored but never read.
allFindings.why_wrong: The deviation from the cited published constants is justified by a comparison that was never performed in this codebase, and the azimuthal 'light dome' model (Gaussian with invented width/peak laws) is unreachable, so the documented direction-dependence of skyglow toward the sunset/sunrise azimuth never affects any output. This is decorative code with unverifiable constants.
allFindings.recommendation: Either wire the azimuthal model into directional skyglow at the actual Fajr/Isha azimuth (using the stored azimuth_deg) and document where A=8.0/B=2.2 come from, or delete the dead functions and use the published Duriscoe constants.

allFindings.title: Crate README claims 5000K LED spectra, a blue-light-fraction result field, and 'negligible' dark-site shifts — all contradicted by the code
allFindings.evidence: 'LED emission at 3000K, 4000K, and 5000K color temperatures' — spectrum.rs contains only LED_3000K_SPECTRUM and LED_4000K_SPECTRUM, no 5000K. 'returns a SkyglowResult with spectral radiance, Bortle class, zenith brightness, and blue-light fraction' — SkyglowResult (lib.rs:79-97) has no blue-light-fraction field. 'Estimates the prayer time shift... negligible at dark sites (Bortle 1-3)' — verified CLI behavior is that Bortle 1 eliminates Fajr and Bortle 2-3 eliminate all prayer times (finding skyglow-injects-ground-radiance).
allFindings.why_wrong: Three checkable claims in the crate's own README are false against the source: one nonexistent dataset (5000K SPD), one nonexistent API field, and one behavioral claim directly refuted by running the binary. Pattern is consistent with generated documentation never validated against the code.
allFindings.recommendation: Regenerate the README from the actual API surface; add a doc test or integration test that exercises the documented entry point and asserts dark-site behavior (Bortle 1-3 must still yield Fajr/Isha times).

allFindings.title: Test suite checks only signs/monotonicity, never absolute magnitudes or cross-module consistency, masking every magnitude bug above
allFindings.evidence: All 13 garstang.rs behavioral tests assert only positivity/ordering (e.g. `assert!(b > 0.0, "Should have positive brightness")`, `assert!(b_near > b_far)`); none pins zenith_brightness to a physical magnitude, so the 4*pi and effective_up factors (combined ~70x) are untestable. spectrum.rs mixed_spectrum_interpolates computes `let _expected = (all_hps[i] + all_led[i]) / 2.0;` then discards it and asserts only `half[i] > 0.0` — the test name promises an interpolation check it does not perform. No test anywhere compares quick_estimate's spectral_radiance-derived luminance to its own zenith_luminance field, the exact inconsistency behind the critical finding.
allFindings.why_wrong: The README advertises '69 tests' as evidence of soundness, but sign/monotonicity tests cannot catch wrong normalization constants, double-counted fractions, or 100x unit-scale errors — precisely the defect classes present. A single magnitude assertion (e.g. Bortle-5 injected luminance < 1 mcd/m^2) would have failed loudly.
allFindings.recommendation: Add magnitude-anchored tests: (a) zenith_brightness vs an analytic single-scatter reference; (b) photopic luminance of quick_estimate spectral output equals zenith_luminance within tolerance; (c) end-to-end pipeline test that Bortle 1-3 still produces Fajr/Isha times.

finding.title: Pipeline injects VIIRS ground-emission radiance as sky radiance, deleting Fajr/Isha at even pristine Bortle settings
finding.evidence: lib.rs: `let zenith_lum = bortle::radiance_to_zenith_luminance(radiance_nw); ... let (spectral, num_wl) = spectrum::mixed_spectrum(radiance_nw, led_fraction);` where spectrum.rs does `let total_si = total_radiance_nw * 1e-5;` (the FULL VIIRS radiance becomes band-integrated sky radiance in W/m^2/sr). pipeline.rs: `sr.radiance[i] += sg.spectral_radiance[i];`. Empirical: `twilight-cli pray --skyglow --bortle 1` -> 'Fajr (true dawn): N/A (threshold not crossed)'; `--bortle 2`..`5` -> ALL of Fajr/Isha-abyad/Isha-ahmar = 'N/A (threshold not crossed in scan range)' while printing 'Light pollution: Bortle 5 (~7 min shift)'. Baseline without --skyglow: Fajr 02:30:19.
finding.why_wrong: VIIRS DNB measures the upward radiance of city lights as seen looking DOWN from orbit; the artificial radiance an observer sees looking UP at the sky is the small scattered fraction, ~2-3 orders of magnitude lower (this conversion is exactly what Garstang 1986/Falchi 2016 modeling exists to do). The injected spectrum integrates to R*1e-5 W/m^2/sr (x6.26 angular factor at 10 deg from quick_estimate_at_angle), i.e. photopic ~0.13 cd/m^2 for Bortle 5 (R=6) — 43x above the 0.003 cd/m^2 Isha threshold and ~60x brighter than the crate's OWN calibrated artificial zenith luminance (0.092*6^0.72 = 0.33 mcd/m^2 = 3.3e-4 cd/m^2). At R=100 the discrepancy is ~135x (measured: 341 mcd injected vs 2.5 mcd calibrated). Consequence: the sky never crosses the threshold, so the feature outputs no prayer times at all for any realistic setting — for software intended for the ummah this silently destroys the result it advertises to refine.
finding.recommendation: Convert VIIRS radiance to artificial sky radiance BEFORE injection: either run the garstang.rs integration (after fixing its own bugs) or scale the lamp spectrum so its photopic luminance equals the calibrated zenith luminance from bortle::radiance_to_zenith_luminance (mcd/m^2 -> cd/m^2 -> spectral via the lamp SPD shape). Add a regression test asserting that quick_estimate's spectral_radiance, pushed through twilight_threshold::photopic_luminance, agrees with its own zenith_luminance field.

verdict.reasoning: I read all cited code and reproduced both the math and the empirical behavior. (1) Code: spectrum.rs:203 converts the full VIIRS radiance only in units (`total_si = total_radiance_nw * 1e-5`, nW/cm²/sr → W/m²/sr) and normalize_factor (spectrum.rs:334-341) makes the band integral of the injected spectrum equal that full value — no ground-emission-to-skyglow scattering conversion is applied. lib.rs:143 computes the correct calibrated luminance via the crate's own Falchi-2016 fit (bortle.rs:126, L=0.092·R^0.72 mcd/m²) but uses it only for display/Bortle class; lib.rs:147 builds the injected spectrum from the raw radiance. twilight-cli main.rs:1028 applies quick_estimate_at_angle(..., 10.0), multiplying the spectrum by the 6.26x Duriscoe factor (angular.rs:82-86), and pipeline.rs:696 adds it directly to MCRT radiance. (2) Physics: VIIRS DNB is upward TOA radiance of ground emission; observed skyglow is the scattered fraction (Garstang 1986, Cinzano 2001, Falchi 2016) — exactly the conversion the crate's own bortle.rs encodes but the spectral path skips. My independent CIE-V(λ) computation reproduces the reviewer's numbers: Bortle 5 injects 0.126 cd/m² photopic at 10° (42x the 0.003 cd/m² isha_abyad threshold in threshold.rs:87, 60x the crate's own calibrated directional luminance); R=100 → 132x; even Bortle 1 injects 2.1e-3 cd/m², above the 0.001 cd/m² Fajr threshold. (3) Empirical: I ran target/release/twilight-cli pray (single-scatter, CPU). Baseline finds all times; --skyglow --bortle 1 → Fajr N/A; --bortle 2 and --bortle 5 → ALL of Fajr/Isha-abyad/Isha-ahmar 'N/A (threshold not crossed in scan range)' while simultaneously printing the calibrated '~7 min shift' estimate. The feature silently deletes prayer times at even physically negligible light-pollution settings (Bortle 2 = 0.04 mcd/m² artificial, ~75x below the Isha threshold). Only quibble: the reviewer's general '~2-3 orders of magnitude' framing slightly overstates the measured 1.3-2.1 orders (19x-132x), but every concrete number they cite is accurate and reproduced, so this does not change the verdict.

finding.title: Advertised 'Garstang RT skyglow model', MCRT ground-source tracer, and VIIRS data sources are never used or do not exist
finding.evidence: lib.rs docs: '2. **MCRT ground-source tracer** (nearby sources, <30km): Full photon tracing from ground-level light sources... Captures cloud reflection, terrain blocking', '- **Embedded lookup** (~10km resolution, always available offline) - **World Bank S3** (~750m COG tiles, free, no auth)', and 'For the full spatially-resolved computation, use [`garstang::compute_skyglow`]'. README.md:125: 'Garstang RT skyglow model... Estimates zenith brightness added to the twilight signal'. grep confirms: `garstang::compute_skyglow` does not exist; no MCRT ground-source tracer exists anywhere in the workspace; the only RadianceSource impl is ConstantRadiance; and garstang::{zenith_brightness, bin_sources, directional_brightness, viirs_to_flux} have ZERO callers outside crates/twilight-skyglow itself — the pipeline/CLI use only quick_estimate_at_angle (bortle power-law + lamp spectrum).
finding.why_wrong: These are fabricated capabilities presented as real. The quantity 'added to the twilight signal' is not the Garstang RT zenith brightness — it is raw VIIRS radiance spread over a lamp SPD. The `mcrt_radius_km` field in SkyglowConfig (lib.rs:52-53) is decorative; SkyglowConfig itself is never constructed by any consumer. The doc-link to a nonexistent function would also fail rustdoc link checking.
finding.recommendation: Either wire garstang::zenith_brightness/bin_sources into the pipeline (with real or constant radiance data) or delete the claims. Remove the MCRT-ground-tracer and data-source bullets from docs until implemented; fix README.md:125 to describe what is actually computed.

verdict.reasoning: Every grep claim checks out. (1) lib.rs:18-20 advertises an 'MCRT ground-source tracer ... Full photon tracing from ground-level light sources'; no such code exists anywhere in the workspace (searched all crates for skyglow/ground-source tracing). (2) lib.rs:24-27 advertises VIIRS data sources 'Embedded lookup (~10km ...)' and 'World Bank S3 (~750m COG tiles)'; neither exists — the only S3 client in the repo is the Copernicus DEM downloader in twilight-terrain/src/copernicus.rs, and the only RadianceSource impl is ConstantRadiance (lib.rs:123). (3) lib.rs:141 doc-links [`garstang::compute_skyglow`], which does not exist; I ran `cargo doc -p twilight-skyglow` and rustdoc reports "no item named `compute_skyglow` in module `garstang`" (warn-by-default rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links — a warning, not a hard doc failure, the finding's only slight overstatement). (4) garstang.rs does contain a genuine Garstang-style single-scatter integration (zenith_brightness, bin_sources, viirs_to_flux, directional_brightness) with internal tests, but ZERO callers outside the crate — it is dead code, exactly as the finding distinguishes ('never used or do not exist'). The fabrication actually extends further than reported: twilight-gpu ships a garstang_zenith kernel (shaders/twilight.metal:2163, trait method lib.rs:276, pipeline setup in metal.rs:106/cuda.rs:120/vulkan.rs:339) that also has zero callers anywhere, including tests. (5) The only production path is twilight-cli/src/main.rs:1028 quick_estimate_at_angle(radiance, led_fraction, 10.0); its spectral_radiance comes from spectrum::mixed_spectrum (spectrum.rs:244), which converts the raw VIIRS nW/cm^2/sr value to W/m^2/sr (×1e-5) and spreads it over a unit-integral lamp SPD, then pipeline.rs:692-699 adds it directly to the MCRT natural radiance. So the quantity 'added to the twilight signal' (README.md:125 'Garstang RT skyglow model ... Estimates zenith brightness added to the twilight signal') is indeed upward VIIRS-equivalent radiance reinterpreted as observer sky radiance, not the Garstang RT zenith brightness — the displayed zenith luminance is a separate bortle.rs power-law fit. (6) SkyglowConfig (incl. mcrt_radius_km, lib.rs:52-53) is never constructed by any consumer; the only in-crate reference is the default_config_values test, so the field is decorative as claimed. Severity 'high' is appropriate rather than 'critical': the skyglow subsystem is opt-in (--skyglow/--bortle/--radiance), the default prayer-time path is unaffected, and the Garstang code itself genuinely exists (unwired) rather than being wholly fake — but documentation and README present capabilities (MCRT tracer, VIIRS data sources, spatially-resolved Garstang computation) that do not exist or are never invoked.
verdict.correction: Core finding stands as written. One detail: the broken intra-doc link [`garstang::compute_skyglow`] produces a rustdoc warning (warn-by-default rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links lint), not a hard documentation build failure — verified by running cargo doc. Additionally, the fabrication is broader than reported: twilight-gpu also exposes an uncalled garstang_zenith kernel (twilight.metal:2163, GpuBackend trait at twilight-gpu/src/lib.rs:276) with zero callers anywhere in the workspace.

finding.title: Garstang single-scatter estimator divides by an extra 4*pi with already-normalized phase functions (12.6x underestimate), duplicated in Metal kernel
finding.evidence: garstang.rs:261: `let di = source_intensity / (4.0 * PI * r2) * sigma_total * p_average * extinction * dh;` while rayleigh_phase (line 273) is `3.0 / (16.0 * PI) * (1.0 + theta.cos().powi(2))` and HG (line 285) is `(1.0 - g * g) / (4.0 * PI * denom)` — both normalized so the integral over 4*pi sr equals 1. Metal twilight.metal:2253 has the identical `source_intensity / (4.0f * PI * r2) * sigma_total * p_avg * extinction * dh`.
finding.why_wrong: The standard single-scatter source term (cf. Garstang 1986 PASP 98:364; Chandrasekhar; libRadtran/MYSTIC convention) for a point source of intensity I [W/sr] is dL = (I/r^2) * sigma_s * P(theta) * exp(-tau_in - tau_out) * ds, where P is normalized to unit integral over the sphere — exactly the normalization these phase functions use (Rayleigh 3/(16*pi)(1+cos^2) integrates to 1). Dividing again by 4*pi double-counts the solid-angle normalization, making the result 4*pi ~ 12.57x too small. (Only with the alternative convention P_iso = 1, i.e. ∫P dΩ = 4π — as Garstang's own f(theta) — would a /4π be correct.) None of the 13 unit tests in garstang.rs checks absolute magnitude, so this is invisible to the test suite.
finding.recommendation: Remove the 4*pi from the denominator (keep unit-normalized phase functions), and add a test comparing zenith_brightness for a known source against a hand-computed analytic value or a published Garstang benchmark (e.g. Garstang 1989 Mt. Palomar/Boulder cases).

verdict.reasoning: The code does exactly what the finding says and the physics reasoning is sound. garstang.rs:261 computes `di = source_intensity / (4.0 * PI * r2) * sigma_total * p_average * extinction * dh`, while rayleigh_phase (line 273, `3/(16π)(1+cos²θ)`) and henyey_greenstein_phase (line 285, `(1−g²)/(4π·denom^{3/2})`) are both normalized to unit integral over 4π sr — I verified numerically that each integrates to exactly 1.0 over the sphere. The source quantity is an intensity in W/sr (LightSource.upward_flux documented W/sr at garstang.rs:49-51; viirs_to_flux at lines 354-370 explicitly builds I = L·A in W/sr), so I/r² is already the irradiance at the scattering point and the standard single-scatter term (Garstang 1986 PASP 98:364; Chandrasekhar convention with ∫P dΩ = 1) is (I/r²)·σ_s·P(θ)·e^{−τin−τout}·ds with no further 4π. The extra /(4π) double-counts the solid-angle normalization, so the returned 'W/m²/sr' brightness is 4π ≈ 12.57x too small. The identical line exists in twilight.metal (~line 2253): `float di = source_intensity / (4.0f * PI * r2) * sigma_total * p_avg * extinction * dh;` with the same unit-normalized phase functions inline. The test-blindness claim also holds: garstang.rs has 22 tests (finding said 13 — minor miscount), all positivity/monotonicity/additivity/relative checks, none pinning absolute magnitude, so the uniform factor passes the suite. One mitigating fact the finding omitted: this Garstang path is currently dead in production — the CLI/pipeline skyglow injection (twilight-cli/src/main.rs:1028 → quick_estimate_at_angle → bortle::radiance_to_zenith_luminance + spectrum::mixed_spectrum) never calls garstang::zenith_brightness, and the GPU garstang_zenith trait method has zero callers in twilight-cpu, twilight-cli, or the GPU crate's tests/parity/oracle. So it cannot shift prayer times today, which is why this is high rather than critical; it remains a genuine 12.6x error in a public, documented radiometric API duplicated across CPU and all GPU backends, and lib.rs:141 steers users to the garstang module (referencing a nonexistent `garstang::compute_skyglow`) for the 'full' computation.
verdict.correction: Finding is accurate as stated, with two refinements: (1) garstang.rs contains 22 unit tests, not 13 (none checks absolute magnitude, so the substantive point stands); (2) the buggy Garstang integration is not currently wired into the production prayer-time path — the pipeline's skyglow injection uses the empirical Bortle quick_estimate calibration, and the GPU garstang_zenith kernel has no callers — so the 12.57x underestimate affects the public API and any future/external use, but does not presently shift computed prayer times.

finding.title: Uplight/reflectance fraction re-applied to flux that is already satellite-measured upward flux; Garstang emission function omitted
finding.evidence: LightSource doc (lines 49-51): 'Total upward flux of this bin (W/sr). Derived from VIIRS radiance * pixel area'. Then lines 178-182: 'Simplified: effective_up ≈ uplight_fraction + ground_reflectance * 0.5' / `let effective_up = config.uplight_fraction + config.ground_reflectance * 0.5; let source_intensity = source.upward_flux * effective_up;` (default 0.10 + 0.15*0.5 = 0.175). Same in twilight.metal:2198-2199.
finding.why_wrong: In Garstang (1986) the uplight fraction F and ground reflectance G partition the TOTAL lamp output via his emission function psi(z) = (1/2pi)(2G(1-F)cos z + 0.554 F z^4). VIIRS-derived upward flux ALREADY IS the light that escaped upward (direct uplight + reflections), so multiplying by 0.175 again double-counts the shielding/reflection losses, suppressing the result ~5.7x (combined with the spurious 4*pi: ~72x total underestimate). Additionally, the source is treated as isotropic (constant W/sr in all directions) — Garstang's characteristic angular emission function, the defining feature of his model, is entirely absent, which mis-weights near-horizontal emission that dominates skyglow from distant cities. The 'effective_up = uplight + reflectance*0.5' partition itself is an invented formula appearing in no published Garstang variant.
finding.recommendation: If sources are VIIRS-derived, drop effective_up entirely (or use it only to back out total lamp output and then apply Garstang's psi(z) for the direction-dependent intensity toward each scattering point). Cite and implement the actual Garstang 1986 emission function if the model is to keep his name.

verdict.reasoning: Read garstang.rs in full and the Metal kernel. The quoted code is verbatim accurate: garstang.rs:179-182 computes effective_up = uplight_fraction + ground_reflectance*0.5 (defaults 0.10 + 0.15*0.5 = 0.175) and multiplies it into source.upward_flux; twilight.metal:2198-2199 is identical. The double-count is proven by the code's own docs: viirs_to_flux (garstang.rs:354-370), the sole producer of upward_flux (via bin_sources line 436), states 'VIIRS already measures this quantity... I = L_viirs * A' — i.e. the input is already the upward-escaped intensity, so re-applying the Garstang F/G partition (which in Garstang 1986 applies to TOTAL lamp output via psi(z) = (1/2pi)[2G(1-F)cos z + 0.554 F z^4]) suppresses the result by 1/0.175 ≈ 5.7x. The 'effective_up' partition is demonstrably invented: the comment at line 177 literally contains the placeholder 'some_factor'. The missing emission function is also confirmed: source intensity is isotropic, and garstang.rs:201 computes the source-to-scatter elevation angle as `let _sin_chi = ...` then never uses it (underscore prefix), so Garstang's near-horizontal z^4 lobe that dominates distant-city skyglow is absent from both CPU and GPU paths. Refutation attempts failed: no call path supplies total lamp output as upward_flux; 0.175 cannot be an angular nadir correction (it is angle-independent and documented as the uplight/reflection split). The finding's arithmetic checks out (1/0.175=5.71; combined with the separate spurious /(4pi) at line 261 over already-normalized phase functions, 5.71*12.57≈72x). Note zenith_brightness/bin_sources have zero call sites outside the crate's own tests, so present-day impact on prayer-time output is via a currently-unwired subsystem — consistent with 'high' rather than 'critical'.

finding.title: Reported 'prayer shift minutes' is an invented formula with fabricated citations, disconnected from (and contradicted by) the actual computed shift
finding.evidence: bortle.rs: 'each doubling of sky brightness shifts twilight threshold by approximately 2-3 minutes (Garstang 1989, cross-checked with observations in Cinzano 2000)' ... `let natural_threshold = 0.05; ... 2.5 * (1.0 + ratio).log2()`. pipeline.rs computes skyglow_shift_minutes from this heuristic, NOT from the actual threshold-crossing difference. Empirical: with --skyglow --bortle 5 the CLI prints 'Light pollution: Bortle 5 (~7 min shift)' on the same screen where Fajr/Isha are 'N/A (threshold not crossed in scan range)'.
finding.why_wrong: Garstang 1989 (PASP 101:306) is about night-sky brightness predictions at observatory sites and Cinzano 2000 about DMSP satellite mapping — neither derives a minutes-per-doubling twilight-threshold shift; the 2.5*log2(1+L/0.05) form and the 0.05 mcd/m^2 'natural threshold' are unsourced. The formula also ignores latitude/season: the solar depression rate (deg/min) varies by more than 2x between the equator and 55 deg latitude, so a fixed minutes-per-doubling constant cannot be correct. Worst, the engine already computes the real shift implicitly (via the injected radiance moving the threshold crossing) — yet reports this unrelated heuristic, so the displayed number actively contradicts the displayed times.
finding.recommendation: Compute the shift as (threshold-crossing time with skyglow) minus (without skyglow) from the actual pipeline, or remove the field. Delete the false citations.

verdict.reasoning: Read all cited code and reproduced the behavior empirically. (1) /Users/mostafamahdi/twilight/crates/twilight-skyglow/src/bortle.rs:218-238 contains exactly the quoted formula `2.5 * (1.0 + ratio).log2()` with `natural_threshold = 0.05` mcd/m^2, and lines 222-224 attribute the "2-3 minutes per doubling" claim to "(Garstang 1989, cross-checked with observations in Cinzano 2000)". Garstang 1989 (PASP 101:306) models artificial night-sky brightness at observatory sites and Cinzano et al. 2000 (MNRAS 318:641) maps DMSP satellite night-sky brightness — neither contains any twilight-threshold timing result, so the citation is fabricated support. The 0.05 mcd/m^2 constant is additionally contradicted by the same file's NATURAL_SKY_LUMINANCE_MCD = 0.17 (line 47): twilight luminance cannot be below the natural night-sky floor, so a 'natural twilight luminance at Isha threshold' of 0.05 is below the module's own stated physical minimum. The fixed minutes-per-doubling constant also ignores latitude/season, while the solar depression rate varies by >2x with latitude, as the finding says. (2) /Users/mostafamahdi/twilight/crates/twilight-cpu/src/pipeline.rs lines 689-699 inject the skyglow spectral radiance into the spectral results BEFORE threshold analysis, so the real shift is embodied in the computed times; yet lines 761-765 fill skyglow_shift_minutes solely from the bortle.rs heuristic — structurally disconnected from the actual crossing difference. (3) I ran the CLI myself: `pray --lat 55.7 --lon 12.6 --date 2026-01-15 --tz 1 --scattering single --skyglow --bortle 5 --cpu` prints 'Light pollution: Bortle 5 (~7 min shift)' (main.rs:1187-1196, fed by pipeline.rs:761-765) directly above 'Fajr (true dawn): N/A (threshold not crossed in scan range)' (main.rs:1226) — reproducing the finding's empirical claim verbatim. Even with --bortle 3 (rural, 0.078 mcd/m^2), the baseline times (Fajr 06:38:47, Isha 17:55:50) all become N/A while the display claims '~3 min shift' — the actual computed effect is 'threshold never crossed' while the heuristic reports 3 minutes, an active contradiction. Mitigating nuance: bortle.rs:209-211 does label the function 'a rough empirical estimate ... Use the full pipeline for accurate results', but the pipeline then reports this heuristic as its own output field and the CLI prints it unqualified next to the real results, so the disclaimer does not rescue it, and the fabricated citation stands regardless. Severity stays high (not critical) because the heuristic number does not feed into the computed prayer times themselves; it is a fabricated-citation, misleading displayed diagnostic.

reviewed.summary: The terrain subsystem is substantially real, not slop: I downloaded the actual Copernicus GLO-30 N21/E039 COG and the crate's own ignored integration tests pass (tiled-DEFLATE decode via tiff 0.11.3 works, Kaaba elevation 296.2 m, eastern horizon 13.0 deg — consistent with Mecca's topography), the point-registration GeoTransform matches GLO-30 convention, Vincenty/UTM round-trips are correct, and the sunrise/sunset adjustment has the right sign and azimuth convention (SPA azimuth clockwise-from-north matches HorizonProfile indexing). However: the Danish LiDAR backend is a fabricated capability (the code itself admits the WCS endpoint is an untested guess, the user is told to register at the wrong service, and the 0.4 m design would need tens of GB of RAM); the README's claim that terrain "adjusts the effective solar zenith angle at each azimuth" and "shifts prayer times" is overstated — the profile is consulted at exactly two azimuths and Fajr/Isha are never touched by terrain; and the effective-SZA constant double-counts refraction against the default SPA engine, biasing terrain-adjusted sunrise/sunset (Maghrib) by ~1-2.5 minutes.

allFindings.title: Danish LiDAR backend is an untested guessed endpoint that cannot work as shipped
allFindings.why_wrong: Three independent problems: (1) The code's own comment admits the WCS endpoint/parameters are a guess that was never tested against the real service, yet README.md ticks '[x] Terrain masking (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, Danish LiDAR)' and the crate description advertises 'national LiDAR'. (2) lib.rs:100-102 tells the user to 'Register free at https://datafordeler.dk' while the code calls api.dataforsyningen.dk — two different Danish data platforms with non-interchangeable tokens, so the suggested key cannot authorize the request. (3) Even if the endpoint worked, the design is infeasible: resolution_m()=0.4 means a 10x10 km tile decodes to 25000x25000 f32 = 2.5 GB in RAM (geotiff.rs loads the full image via read_image into a Vec<f32>), the default 30 km horizon radius prepares ~28+ tiles (~70+ GB), each downloaded as a multi-GB single HTTP GET read fully into memory (cache.rs:88-93), and compute_horizon would issue 360 x 75,000 = 27 million Vincenty solves at 0.4 m steps. resolve_source (lib.rs:96-98) automatically selects this backend for any Danish coordinate when a key is set.
allFindings.recommendation: Either remove the Danish backend and the README checkbox until it is tested end-to-end, or make it honest: verify the real Dataforsyningen/Datafordeler WCS endpoint, request downsampled coverage (e.g., SCALESIZE to 2-5 m), stream downloads to disk, and decode windows rather than whole tiles. At minimum, mark it experimental in README and resolve_source.

allFindings.title: README claims terrain 'adjusts the effective SZA at each azimuth' and 'shifts prayer times'; code consults 2 azimuths and never touches Fajr/Isha
allFindings.evidence: README.md:123: "Computes a 360-point horizon profile and adjusts the effective solar zenith angle at each azimuth. Mountains and buildings that block the horizon shift prayer times." — but pipeline.rs only does: `let az = engine.azimuth_at_hour(sr_h).unwrap_or(90.0); let hz = profile.angle_at(az); if hz > 0.01 { let eff_sza = horizon::effective_sunrise_sza(hz); ... }` for sunrise and sunset only.
allFindings.why_wrong: Grepping the workspace shows HorizonProfile::angle_at is called exactly twice (pipeline.rs:523, 537) — once at the sunrise azimuth and once at the sunset azimuth. The 360-point profile feeds nothing else: the MCRT twilight scan (Step 7 onward) and the threshold analysis that produce fajr_time/isha_abyad_time/isha_ahmar_time are completely independent of input.horizon_profile, and the field's own doc (pipeline.rs:77-78) honestly says only 'sunrise/sunset SZA is adjusted'. So the headline claim of per-azimuth SZA adjustment is false as stated, and the project's core outputs (Fajr/Isha, the twilight prayers this engine exists for) are never shifted by terrain. Note: NOT applying observer-horizon masking to astronomical-twilight thresholds is physically defensible (the sun is 10-18 deg below the horizon at Fajr/Isha; a ridge does not occult it, and its effect on diffuse sky radiance is second order) — the error is the README selling a capability the pipeline does not have. Only sunset (Maghrib) and sunrise are actually adjusted.
allFindings.recommendation: Rewrite README.md:123 to say terrain adjusts sunrise/sunset (Maghrib) times via the horizon angle at the sun's rise/set azimuth, and explicitly state Fajr/Isha are unaffected by design. Alternatively, if per-azimuth sky masking of the twilight radiance is intended, implement it in the RT view-geometry — but that is a research-level change.

allFindings.title: effective_sunrise_sza applies the fixed 0.8333 deg horizon offset to elevated horizons, double-counting refraction against the default SPA engine; its own comment contradicts the formula
allFindings.why_wrong: Three layered problems. (1) Comment vs code: SZA = 90.8333 - h puts the sun's center at altitude h MINUS 0.8333 deg, not 'h + 0.8333' as the comment claims. (2) Engine convention: the pipeline finds crossings of this SZA using SolarEngine zenith values. The SPA path (the default; spa.rs:491-499) returns a REFRACTION-CORRECTED zenith (`let e = e0 + delta_e; let zenith = 90.0 - e;`), so the 0.5667 deg refraction baked into 0.8333 is counted twice: the sun is declared clear of an h-degree ridge while its apparent center is still 0.5667 deg below the ridge (upper limb still ~0.30 deg below). The DE440 path returns a geometric zenith (earth_rotation.rs:369, 'uncorrected for refraction'), so the two engines disagree by ~0.5 deg on the same threshold. (3) Even on the geometric path, refraction at apparent altitude h should be R(h) (Bennett 1982: ~34' at 0 deg, ~10' at 5 deg, ~4' at 13 deg), not the fixed 34' horizon value. Net effect for Mecca's measured 13 deg eastern horizon: terrain-adjusted sunrise declared ~2-2.5 min early; terrain-adjusted sunset (= Maghrib, a prayer time) ~2-2.5 min late under SPA. Sign and azimuth-matching of the adjustment are otherwise CORRECT (smaller SZA -> later sunrise / earlier sunset; SPA azimuth clockwise-from-north matches HorizonProfile indexing).
allFindings.recommendation: Define effective SZA per the engine's zenith convention: for the SPA (apparent) path use 90 + 0.2667 - h (semidiameter only); for a geometric path use 90 + 0.2667 + R(h) - h with Bennett refraction evaluated at h. Fix the contradictory comment, and unify the SPA/DE440 zenith conventions behind SolarEngine.

allFindings.title: CLI prepare() bounding box lacks 1/cos(lat) on longitude, and elevation_at cannot lazy-load, so east/west terrain within the scan radius is silently dropped at mid/high latitudes
allFindings.why_wrong: One degree of longitude spans 111*cos(lat) km, so the longitude half-width must be radius/(111*cos(lat)). At 55 N a 30 km scan reaches +/-0.47 deg of longitude but only +/-0.27 deg is prepared; compute_horizon's Vincenty march then queries coordinates whose 1-degree tile was never loaded, CopernicusDem30::elevation_at returns None (it explicitly cannot lazy-load), and horizon.rs:57 silently skips the sample as if no terrain existed. The result is an underestimated horizon specifically in the east/west sectors — exactly the sunrise/sunset azimuths the adjustment depends on — whenever the observer sits within the un-prepared margin of a tile boundary at |lat| greater than about 33 deg. No warning is emitted.
allFindings.recommendation: Use radius_deg_lon = horizon_radius / (111.0 * lat.to_radians().cos().max(0.01)) for the longitude span (keep /111.0 for latitude), or compute the bbox from vincenty_forward at azimuths 0/90/180/270. Better: have compute_horizon assert/report when samples fall outside prepared coverage.

allFindings.title: Download/parse failures silently degrade to 'no terrain': prepare() error vec is provably dead, and a missing observer pixel makes all angles relative to elevation 0
allFindings.why_wrong: prepare() always returns Ok: a total network failure (or a misparsed tile) yields tiles full of None, the CLI then prints 'Terrain: ... (radius 30 km)' as success and computes an all-zero horizon profile — terrain masking is reported active while doing nothing. Worse, if only the observer's own tile fails but neighbor tiles load, unwrap_or(0.0) computes every elevation angle against observer height 0 instead of the true ground height (e.g., 296 m at Mecca), inflating horizon angles by atan(296/d) — at 10 km that is +1.7 deg of spurious obstruction, which directly shifts the reported sunrise/sunset. For a tool whose stated purpose is religious timing, hard failures should not be converted into silently wrong profiles.
allFindings.recommendation: Make load_tile/download_and_parse propagate errors into prepare()'s result (the plumbing half-exists); in compute_horizon, return an error or refuse to build a profile when the observer pixel has no data instead of unwrap_or(0.0).

allFindings.title: GeoTIFF geo-tag extraction is a stub: module doc claims tag parsing, but read_geo_transform always errors, so the public ElevationTile::from_file can never succeed
allFindings.evidence:
Module doc: "Extracts geographic metadata (pixel scale, tiepoint, CRS) from TIFF tags." — but read_geo_transform ends with: // For now, return a placeholder that will be filled by the backend-specific code.
Err("GeoTransform must be provided by the backend (use from_file_with_geo)".to_string())
allFindings.why_wrong: ModelPixelScaleTag (33550) / ModelTiepointTag (33922) are never read; the function ignores its decoder argument entirely. Consequently the public API from_file (geotiff.rs:57) unconditionally fails at runtime for every input. The shipped code paths avoid it (copernicus.rs and denmark.rs construct the GeoTransform from known tile layout and call from_file_with_geo, which I verified works on a real Copernicus COG), so results are not corrupted — but the doc claim is false and from_file is a dead-on-arrival public function. Mitigating fact: the hard-coded Copernicus registration (top-left pixel center at (lon_floor, lat_floor+1), pixel = 1/width deg) exactly matches GLO-30's point registration, confirmed by the passing real-tile Kaaba test (296.2 m).
allFindings.recommendation: Either implement real tag parsing (the tiff crate exposes Tag::Unknown via decoder.get_tag / find_tag for 33550/33922) or delete from_file and the stub, and fix the module doc to say transforms are supplied by backends.

allFindings.title: horizon_time_shift is dead code with an arbitrary polar fallback; the CLI instead prints a misleading 'min shift' from max_angle x 4
allFindings.why_wrong: horizon_time_shift is never called outside its own unit tests (workspace grep) — the pipeline correctly derives the actual shift by re-solving the zenith crossing instead. Meanwhile the CLI banner computes 'min shift' as max_angle * 4.0: it uses the maximum horizon over ALL 360 azimuths (not the sun's rise/set azimuth) and the equator-equinox rate (4 min/deg), so for Mecca it would print '52 min shift' (13 deg x 4) when the real sunrise azimuth may see a much smaller angle and the obliquity factor differs with latitude/season. The dead function's polar fallback '1 hour per degree' is a magic constant with no derivation. Neither corrupts computed times; both mislead users and reviewers about what the code does.
allFindings.recommendation: Delete horizon_time_shift or wire the actual pipeline-computed shift into the CLI message; label the banner number as a rough upper bound based on the worst azimuth, or print the horizon angle at the actual sunrise/sunset azimuths.

allFindings.title: Curvature drop omits terrestrial refraction and the comment misattributes it to the solar engine
allFindings.why_wrong: The solar engine refracts the SUN's apparent position; it cannot account for refraction of the sightline from observer to TERRAIN, which is a separate effect. Standard surveying/viewshed practice (Bomford, Geodesy; the common k≈0.13 refraction coefficient, i.e., effective Earth radius R/(1-k) ≈ 7/6 R) reduces the curvature drop to d^2(1-k)/(2R). Omitting it systematically underestimates horizon angles of distant terrain — by only ~0.018 deg at the 30 km default radius, so the practical impact on times is well under a minute. This is at the edge of acceptable-approximation territory; it is flagged mainly because the in-code justification is factually wrong rather than because the magnitude matters.
allFindings.recommendation: Use curvature_drop = dist*dist*(1.0-0.13)/(2.0*EARTH_RADIUS_M) (or effective radius 7/6 R) and correct the comment to say terrestrial refraction is approximated, not delegated to the solar engine.

finding.title: Danish LiDAR backend is an untested guessed endpoint that cannot work as shipped
finding.why_wrong: Three independent problems: (1) The code's own comment admits the WCS endpoint/parameters are a guess that was never tested against the real service, yet README.md ticks '[x] Terrain masking (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, Danish LiDAR)' and the crate description advertises 'national LiDAR'. (2) lib.rs:100-102 tells the user to 'Register free at https://datafordeler.dk' while the code calls api.dataforsyningen.dk — two different Danish data platforms with non-interchangeable tokens, so the suggested key cannot authorize the request. (3) Even if the endpoint worked, the design is infeasible: resolution_m()=0.4 means a 10x10 km tile decodes to 25000x25000 f32 = 2.5 GB in RAM (geotiff.rs loads the full image via read_image into a Vec<f32>), the default 30 km horizon radius prepares ~28+ tiles (~70+ GB), each downloaded as a multi-GB single HTTP GET read fully into memory (cache.rs:88-93), and compute_horizon would issue 360 x 75,000 = 27 million Vincenty solves at 0.4 m steps. resolve_source (lib.rs:96-98) automatically selects this backend for any Danish coordinate when a key is set.
finding.recommendation: Either remove the Danish backend and the README checkbox until it is tested end-to-end, or make it honest: verify the real Dataforsyningen/Datafordeler WCS endpoint, request downsampled coverage (e.g., SCALESIZE to 2-5 m), stream downloads to disk, and decode windows rather than whole tiles. At minimum, mark it experimental in README and resolve_source.

verdict.reasoning: Read denmark.rs in full plus lib.rs, cache.rs, geotiff.rs, horizon.rs, projection.rs, twilight-cli/src/main.rs, and README.md. All three legs hold. (1) denmark.rs:101-104 literally states the WCS endpoint "will be finalized once the user provides their API key and we can test against the real service" — the code self-documents as untested — while README.md:249 ticks "[x] Terrain masking (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, Danish LiDAR)" and README.md:123/213 advertise the "Danish SDFI backend" as shipped. (2) lib.rs:100-102 and the CLI help (main.rs:177-178) direct users to register at https://datafordeler.dk, but the code calls api.dataforsyningen.dk with token= auth (denmark.rs:117-125); Dataforsyningen (token query param) and Datafordeleren (service-user credentials) are distinct Danish platforms with non-interchangeable credentials, so the suggested key cannot authorize the request. (3) Resource math verified: resolution_m()=0.4 (denmark.rs:184-186), the crate's own test states a 10 km tile is 25000x25000 px (denmark.rs:276-277), geotiff.rs:219-231 decodes the full image into Vec<f32> = 2.5 GB/tile, default 30 km radius (main.rs:175-176) gives a ±30 km bbox (main.rs:977-983) = 36-49 tiles (the finding's "~28+" is conservative), all retained simultaneously in a never-evicted HashMap (denmark.rs:47) and necessarily resident because elevation_at takes &self (denmark.rs:168-182); cache.rs:88-93 reads each HTTP body fully into RAM; horizon.rs:45-77 with 0.4 m steps over 30 km yields exactly 360x75,000 = 27M vincenty_forward calls (true iterative geodesic, projection.rs:167-249). Aggravating detail the finding missed: prepare() returns Ok(()) unconditionally (denmark.rs:229) after swallowing download failures, so the CLI prints "Terrain: Danish DHM LiDAR (0.4m)" and produces an all-zero horizon profile labeled as LiDAR even when nothing downloaded. Only minor caveat: 27M Vincenty solves is slow but CPU-feasible; the true infeasibility is the ~90-120 GB RAM requirement, which the finding correctly treats as primary. Severity critical is justified under the rubric's "fabricated capability presented as real": the backend is auto-selected for any Danish coordinate when a key is set (lib.rs:96-99), cannot authenticate, was never tested, could not fit in memory if it did work, and silently degrades to a fake flat-horizon result labeled as 0.4 m LiDAR.

finding.title: README claims terrain 'adjusts the effective SZA at each azimuth' and 'shifts prayer times'; code consults 2 azimuths and never touches Fajr/Isha
finding.evidence: README.md:123: "Computes a 360-point horizon profile and adjusts the effective solar zenith angle at each azimuth. Mountains and buildings that block the horizon shift prayer times." — but pipeline.rs only does: `let az = engine.azimuth_at_hour(sr_h).unwrap_or(90.0); let hz = profile.angle_at(az); if hz > 0.01 { let eff_sza = horizon::effective_sunrise_sza(hz); ... }` for sunrise and sunset only.
finding.why_wrong: Grepping the workspace shows HorizonProfile::angle_at is called exactly twice (pipeline.rs:523, 537) — once at the sunrise azimuth and once at the sunset azimuth. The 360-point profile feeds nothing else: the MCRT twilight scan (Step 7 onward) and the threshold analysis that produce fajr_time/isha_abyad_time/isha_ahmar_time are completely independent of input.horizon_profile, and the field's own doc (pipeline.rs:77-78) honestly says only 'sunrise/sunset SZA is adjusted'. So the headline claim of per-azimuth SZA adjustment is false as stated, and the project's core outputs (Fajr/Isha, the twilight prayers this engine exists for) are never shifted by terrain. Note: NOT applying observer-horizon masking to astronomical-twilight thresholds is physically defensible (the sun is 10-18 deg below the horizon at Fajr/Isha; a ridge does not occult it, and its effect on diffuse sky radiance is second order) — the error is the README selling a capability the pipeline does not have. Only sunset (Maghrib) and sunrise are actually adjusted.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite README.md:123 to say terrain adjusts sunrise/sunset (Maghrib) times via the horizon angle at the sun's rise/set azimuth, and explicitly state Fajr/Isha are unaffected by design. Alternatively, if per-azimuth sky masking of the twilight radiance is intended, implement it in the RT view-geometry — but that is a research-level change.

verdict.reasoning: I independently verified every claim. (1) README.md:123 says verbatim: "Computes a 360-point horizon profile and adjusts the effective solar zenith angle at each azimuth. Mountains and buildings that block the horizon shift prayer times," and README.md:19 lists terrain masking inside the sentence describing how Fajr/Isha are computed. (2) A workspace grep confirms HorizonProfile::angle_at is called in non-test code exactly twice — crates/twilight-cpu/src/pipeline.rs:523 (sunrise azimuth) and :537 (sunset azimuth); the only other pipeline use of input.horizon_profile (lines 753-756) just copies source_name into output metadata. (3) The MCRT scan config (pipeline.rs:569-579), threshold analysis (701-714), and the fajr_time/isha_abyad_time/isha_ahmar_time computations (717-727, via find_zenith_crossing on prayer_result SZAs) contain no terrain term — Fajr/Isha are provably independent of the horizon profile. (4) The code's own docs contradict the README: pipeline.rs:77-78 says "sunrise/sunset SZA is adjusted," and horizon.rs:5-6 says the 360-element array is "used to shift sunrise/sunset times." (5) The finding's physics caveat is sound: at Fajr/Isha the sun is ~13-18 deg below the geometric horizon (README's own examples show 13-15 deg depressions), so a few-degree ridge from a 30 km scan cannot occult it; standard astronomical-twilight convention uses the geometric horizon and applies horizon occultation only to direct-beam sunrise/sunset. So not applying terrain to twilight thresholds is defensible — the error is the README selling per-azimuth SZA adjustment and terrain-shifted prayer times that the pipeline does not implement for its flagship outputs. Minor nuance (already conceded in the finding): sunset is Maghrib, so terrain does shift one prayer time, which keeps this at high rather than critical.

reviewed.summary: The Open-Meteo client itself is sound: I verified live that both endpoints accept the exact variable names in api.rs and return the assumed units, the NO2 µg/m³→molecules/m³ conversion constant is exact, the Dobson Unit constant (2.6868e20 m⁻²) is correct, and the Angstrom extrapolation follows the standard convention with OPAC-plausible parameters. The integration into the builder/pipeline is real, not fabricated. However, both surface→column gas mappings are physically unjustified: the O3 column is guessed from surface O3 via an invented 0.5 DU/(µg/m³) correlation whose 300 DU baseline conflicts with both the documented (~347 DU) and actual (~546 DU) standard-profile column, so enabling --weather silently changes O3 absorption by ~45% independent of weather; and the NO2 surface reading is propagated through a 2.4 km-effective-thickness profile, yielding tropospheric columns 4-25x above anything observed by OMI/TROPOMI. A literal abandoned LLM derivation ("...wait]") with a dimensionally wrong formula is shipped in the doc comments, confirming the maintainer's AI-slop suspicion for this module, even though the executable code beneath it is mostly correct.

allFindings.title: O3 column in DU is fabricated from surface O3 via an invented, uncited correlation
allFindings.why_wrong: Total column O3 is ~90% stratospheric, controlled by Brewer-Dobson transport and synoptic dynamics (WMO Ozone Assessments; Fishman et al. 1990 show the tropospheric residual is ~10% of the column). Boundary-layer surface O3 (photochemistry, titration, deposition) carries essentially no predictive information about the column, yet a precise '0.5 DU per ug/m3' constant is shipped with no literature source — the comment itself admits 'weak correlation'. CAMS produces actual total-column ozone, but Open-Meteo's air-quality API only exposes surface ozone, so the code invents a column instead. README.md:43 ('the engine accounts for today's actual O3 column') overstates this: no column observation is ever fetched. Also doc/code mismatch: the comment (lines 184-185) says 'a floor of 250 DU', the code clamps to 220.0.
allFindings.recommendation: Do not derive column O3 from surface O3. Either fetch a real total-column product (CAMS TCO3 via the ADS API, or a TOMS/OMI climatology by latitude/month) or keep the climatological default and document that surface O3 is unusable for this. Fix the README claim and the 250-vs-220 doc mismatch.

allFindings.title: Documented default O3 column (~347 DU) contradicts the actual ~546 DU standard profile, so enabling --weather silently cuts O3 absorption ~45%
allFindings.why_wrong: Trapezoid integration of STD_O3_DENSITY over STD_ALT_KM (gas_absorption_data.rs:26876-26902, surface 5.4e17 m^-3, peak 5.4e18 m^-3 at 30 km) gives 1.467e23 m^-2 = 546 DU, not 347 DU (US Standard 1976 is ~345 DU; the table is too fat at 25-40 km). The '~347 DU' figure in this crate (repeated at builder.rs:421) appears never to have been computed — the only test (gas_absorption.rs:1450-1454) asserts the absurdly wide bracket 100-600 DU. Consequence for the weather path: with weather OFF the model runs at ~546 DU; with weather ON, estimate_o3_column_du snaps the column to ~300 DU (clamped 220-450). That ~45% O3 reduction changes Chappuis-band (500-700 nm) absorption along the long twilight path (ozone airmass ~30-50 at Fajr/Isha depressions; Hulburt 1953 shows Chappuis absorption dominates zenith twilight radiance), shifting band radiance by a factor of several — plausibly minutes of prayer-time shift between --weather and non-weather runs for identical real atmospheres.
allFindings.recommendation: Recompute and fix the standard O3 table so the default column is ~345 DU (gas-absorption fix), then make the weather baseline consistent with the actual default. Add a test asserting the standard column within +-10% of 345 DU, not 100-600.

allFindings.title: NO2 surface reading scaled through the whole standard profile yields columns 4-25x above any observed urban NO2 VCD
allFindings.why_wrong: The standard NO2 profile (gas_absorption_data.rs:26904-26930) has surface density 4.0e15 m^-3 (~0.3 ug/m3) and column 9.7e14 cm^-2, i.e. an effective thickness of column/surface = 2.4 km. Pinning the surface to a CAMS reading scales the column linearly: 40 ug/m3 ('moderate urban' per mapping.rs:213) gives factor 131x and a column of 1.27e17 cm^-2 — 4-6x above the most extreme TROPOMI/OMI megacity tropospheric VCDs (~2-3e16 cm^-2) and ~10-25x typical urban values (~5e15-1e16 cm^-2). Even a clean-suburban 10 ug/m3 produces 3.2e16 cm^-2, already extreme-megacity level. The hidden profile assumption (surface concentration extended over 2.4 km effective depth, on top of an unrealistically clean 0.3 ug/m3 baseline that inflates the multiplicative factor) is exactly the surface-to-column fallacy: a point measurement cannot give a column without a boundary-layer-height assumption, and real urban NO2 is confined to ~0.5-1 km. At sigma_NO2(435nm) ~ 6e-19 cm^2 (Vandaele et al. 1998) the spurious column adds vertical tau ~0.08 in blue, systematically dimming modeled blue twilight radiance in any city.
allFindings.recommendation: Replace whole-profile scaling with an explicit boundary-layer model: add the observed surface density over an assumed mixing height (~800 m, documented), leave the free-troposphere/background profile untouched, and raise the standard surface baseline to a realistic ~1-2 ug/m3 background. Cap the implied tropospheric VCD at ~3e16 cm^-2.

allFindings.title: Abandoned LLM chain-of-thought ('...wait]') and a dimensionally wrong 'Actually:' formula shipped in NO2 conversion docs
allFindings.why_wrong: This is literal AI-generated reasoning residue: a derivation abandoned mid-token ('... wait]') followed by an 'Actually:' formula that is wrong — dividing by 22.4 L/mol (molar volume) belongs to ppb-to-mass conversions, and the units (g/mol x kg/g x L/m3 x L/mol) do not cancel to molecules/m3. The third docstring formula (lines 207-211) and the implemented code (line 215, C*1e-6*N_A/M = 1.309e16 per ug/m3, verified: 40 ug/m3 -> 5.24e17 m^-3) are correct, so the function works, but two of the three documented derivations contradict it and would mislead any maintainer auditing the units.
