allFindings.recommendation: Delete lines 199-204 entirely, keeping only the correct derivation at lines 205-213.

allFindings.title: Cloud cover % mapped to optical depth via uncited f^0.7 homogenization instead of standard partial-cloud treatment
allFindings.why_wrong: tau_eff = tau * f^0.7 has no literature basis. The standard treatments are (a) the independent column approximation — radiance = f*cloudy + (1-f)*clear, as used in libRadtran/MYSTIC and GCM radiation schemes (Barker 1996) — or (b) Cahalan et al. (1994)'s effective-thickness approximation, which is a constant reduction factor chi~0.7 multiplying tau to correct plane-parallel albedo bias, NOT an exponent on the cover fraction. The chosen form looks like a garbled conflation of the two. Materially: 50% cover of OD-10 stratus becomes a uniform OD-6.2 overcast (diffuse transmittance ~e^-4), whereas under ICA half the sky is clear and the clear fraction dominates whether twilight is observable at all — the qualitatively decisive regime for prayer-time observation under broken cloud. The 'cloud edges / horizontal transport' justification is hand-waving with no source.
allFindings.recommendation: Either run two columns (cloudy/clear) and blend radiances by cover fraction (ICA), or at minimum use tau_eff = f * chi * tau with chi=0.7 citing Cahalan et al. 1994, and document the regime where homogenization fails.

allFindings.title: 10% scattered low cloud completely masks 90% high cloud due to early-return priority
allFindings.why_wrong: Only one layer is ever emitted, and the priority is a hard threshold (10%), not dominance: with cloud_cover_low=15% and cloud_cover_high=90%, the function returns scattered Cumulus at OD 5*0.15^0.7 ~ 1.3 and discards a near-overcast cirrus deck (ThickCirrus OD ~2 at 8-11 km) that actually controls twilight transmission, since twilight light enters through the high atmosphere. The live API response I fetched during review (low:0, mid:73, high:88) shows mixed multi-layer skies are the common case, not an edge case. The doc comment's rationale ('low clouds have the largest radiative impact') only holds when the low layer is substantial, which the 10% threshold does not ensure.
allFindings.recommendation: Select the layer with the largest cover*default_OD product, or better, emit up to three layers (the builder's add_cloud_layer already distributes any layer across shells, so multiple calls would work).

allFindings.title: Maritime aerosol types exist in the model but are unreachable from the weather mapping
allFindings.why_wrong: AerosolType::MaritimeClean and MaritimePolluted (aerosol.rs:110-128, Angstrom 0.5/0.8 per OPAC sea-salt) can never be selected by --weather, even for coastal/oceanic locations common across the Muslim world. Clean marine air at AOD 0.10 is classified ContinentalAverage (alpha=1.3 instead of ~0.5), and the Angstrom extrapolation then overestimates blue AOD by (550/410)^(1.3-0.5) ~ 1.27, i.e. ~27% at 410 nm, skewing the modeled twilight color. Half of the OPAC types the data crate implements are dead weight in weather mode.
allFindings.recommendation: Use a coastal/ocean heuristic (e.g. sea_salt_aerosol is not exposed by Open-Meteo, but PM10-PM2.5 coarse fraction with low dust, or a land-sea mask from the existing DEM crate) to select maritime types near coasts.

allFindings.title: Relative humidity is fetched but never used, despite OPAC aerosol properties being strongly RH-dependent
allFindings.evidence:
/// Relative humidity at 2m (%)
pub relative_humidity: f64,
allFindings.why_wrong: relative_humidity_2m is requested from the API (api.rs:67) and stored, but grep confirms it is never read by map_aerosol/map_cloud/map_gas_composition (its only appearance in mapping.rs is a test fixture at line 357). aerosol.rs:70-71 admits the defaults are pinned at 'moderate relative humidity (~50-70%)', yet OPAC (Hess et al. 1998) tabulates properties at 8 RH grid points precisely because hygroscopic growth changes scattering by f(RH)~2-3x between RH 50% and 90% for sulfate/sea-salt. Fetching the field and ignoring it is a half-built capability; humid-evening conditions (typical at Isha in the tropics) will underestimate aerosol scattering.
allFindings.recommendation: Apply a Hanel-type f(RH) growth factor to AOD/SSA for the hygroscopic types (not Desert), or remove the field and document the fixed-RH assumption.

Boundary-layer surface O3 (photochemistry, titration, deposition) carries essentially no predictive information about the column, yet a precise '0.5 DU per ug/m3' constant is shipped with no literature source — the comment itself admits 'weak correlation'. CAMS produces actual total-column ozone, but Open-Meteo's air-quality API only exposes surface ozone, so the code invents a column instead. README.md:43 ('the engine accounts for today's actual O3 column') overstates this: no column observation is ever fetched. Also doc/code mismatch: the comment (lines 184-185) says 'a floor of 250 DU', the code clamps to 220.0.

verdict.reasoning: Read mapping.rs myself: estimate_o3_column_du (lines 186-197) is exactly as quoted — baseline 300 DU at 60 ug/m3 surface O3, invented sensitivity 0.5 DU per ug/m3 with no citation, clamp(220.0, 450.0); the doc comment at line 184 says 'floor of 250 DU' while the code clamps at 220, confirming the doc/code mismatch. Verified in api.rs:72 that only surface ozone is fetched from Open-Meteo's air-quality endpoint (current=...,ozone,...) and lib.rs:37-39 documents it as 'Surface ozone concentration (ug/m3)' — no total-column observation exists anywhere in the crate, yet README.md:43 claims 'the engine accounts for today's actual O3 column'. The synthesized DU value is consumed as a real column target by twilight-data/src/builder.rs:464 (scales the O3 profile to target_du), so it directly modulates Chappuis-band absorption in the RT model. The physics critique is correct per standard literature: total column O3 is ~90% stratospheric (Fishman et al. 1990; WMO Ozone Assessments), controlled by Brewer-Dobson/synoptic dynamics, while surface O3 is boundary-layer photochemistry/titration/deposition; no published surface-to-column linear sensitivity exists, the code's own comment admits 'weak correlation', and the mapping can even be anti-correlated seasonally (mid-latitude column peaks in spring, surface O3 episodes peak in summer), injecting up to ±45 DU of spurious variation. A citable standard alternative (Van Heuklon 1979 latitude/season climatology, or a fixed default) exists and was not used. Adjacent code (lines 201-203) contains an abandoned LLM artifact '1e6 [cm3/m3... wait]', corroborating the fabrication pattern. Severity high (not critical) is right: the 220-450 DU clamp bounds the damage and README.md:109 describes the surface-to-column mapping more honestly, so prayer-time impact is real but bounded (likely sub-minute to ~1 min via Chappuis OD changes of ~10-20%).

finding.title: Documented default O3 column (~347 DU) contradicts the actual ~546 DU standard profile, so enabling --weather silently cuts O3 absorption ~45%
finding.why_wrong: Trapezoid integration of STD_O3_DENSITY over STD_ALT_KM (gas_absorption_data.rs:26876-26902, surface 5.4e17 m^-3, peak 5.4e18 m^-3 at 30 km) gives 1.467e23 m^-2 = 546 DU, not 347 DU (US Standard 1976 is ~345 DU; the table is too fat at 25-40 km). The '~347 DU' figure in this crate (repeated at builder.rs:421) appears never to have been computed — the only test (gas_absorption.rs:1450-1454) asserts the absurdly wide bracket 100-600 DU. Consequence for the weather path: with weather OFF the model runs at ~546 DU; with weather ON, estimate_o3_column_du snaps the column to ~300 DU (clamped 220-450). That ~45% O3 reduction changes Chappuis-band (500-700 nm) absorption along the long twilight path (ozone airmass ~30-50 at Fajr/Isha depressions; Hulburt 1953 shows Chappuis absorption dominates zenith twilight radiance), shifting band radiance by a factor of several — plausibly minutes of prayer-time shift between --weather and non-weather runs for identical real atmospheres.
finding.recommendation: Recompute and fix the standard O3 table so the default column is ~345 DU (gas-absorption fix), then make the weather baseline consistent with the actual default. Add a test asserting the standard column within +-10% of 345 DU, not 100-600.

verdict.reasoning: Every checkable claim held up under independent verification. (1) The "~347 DU for US Standard 1976" doc text exists verbatim at crates/twilight-weather/src/lib.rs:73-75 and is repeated at crates/twilight-data/src/builder.rs:420-421. (2) I independently trapezoid-integrated STD_O3_DENSITY over STD_ALT_KM (gas_absorption_data.rs:26831-26902) and got 1.4668e23 m^-2 = 545.9 DU — matching the reviewer's 546 DU and contradicting both the doc (~347) and the true US Standard 1976 / AFGL afglus value (~345 DU). The table peaks at 30 km (5.4e18 m^-3) instead of ~22 km and is ~2-4x too dense at 30-40 km; no AFGL climatology exceeds ~486 DU, so 546 DU matches nothing physical. (3) standard_gas_profile (gas_absorption.rs:696-723) linearly interpolates this table, so the simulation really carries ~540+ DU; the only column test (gas_absorption.rs:1450-1455) asserts the bracket 100 < du < 600 while its own failure message says "expected ~200-400 DU" — the actual value would fail that stated expectation, confirming the bracket was never reconciled with the data. (4) The weather discrepancy is real: CLI main.rs:668-684 uses build_full (no scaling, native ~546 DU) without --weather, but with --weather, estimate_o3_column_du (mapping.rs:186-197) returns 300 + 0.5*(surface_o3-60) clamped to 220-450 DU and scale_o3_column (gas_absorption.rs:737-755) correctly rescales from the actual integrated column — so weather ON cuts the O3 column ~45% for the same real atmosphere. (5) Physics consequence is sound: Chappuis-band O3 absorption dominates zenith twilight radiance (Hulburt 1953), ozone slant airmass at Fajr/Isha depressions is tens, so a 246 DU column change (Δτ_vert ≈ 0.034 at 600 nm) gives Δτ_slant of order 1, a factor ~2-4+ in band radiance — plausibly minutes at the threshold crossing. Only nuance: the erroneous side is the DEFAULT (non-weather) path, since 546 DU is non-physical and the weather path's ~300 DU is closer to reality; the reviewer's text already notes the table is "too fat at 25-40 km", so this is a framing refinement, not an error in the finding.

finding.title: NO2 surface reading scaled through the whole standard profile yields columns 4-25x above any observed urban NO2 VCD
finding.why_wrong: The standard NO2 profile (gas_absorption_data.rs:26904-26930) has surface density 4.0e15 m^-3 (~0.3 ug/m3) and column 9.7e14 cm^-2, i.e. an effective thickness of column/surface = 2.4 km. Pinning the surface to a CAMS reading scales the column linearly: 40 ug/m3 ('moderate urban' per mapping.rs:213) gives factor 131x and a column of 1.27e17 cm^-2 — 4-6x above the most extreme TROPOMI/OMI megacity tropospheric VCDs (~2-3e16 cm^-2) and ~10-25x typical urban values (~5e15-1e16 cm^-2). Even a clean-suburban 10 ug/m3 produces 3.2e16 cm^-2, already extreme-megacity level. The hidden profile assumption (surface concentration extended over 2.4 km effective depth, on top of an unrealistically clean 0.3 ug/m3 baseline that inflates the multiplicative factor) is exactly the surface-to-column fallacy: a point measurement cannot give a column without a boundary-layer-height assumption, and real urban NO2 is confined to ~0.5-1 km. At sigma_NO2(435nm) ~ 6e-19 cm^2 (Vandaele et al. 1998) the spurious column adds vertical tau ~0.08 in blue, systematically dimming modeled blue twilight radiance in any city.
finding.recommendation: Replace whole-profile scaling with an explicit boundary-layer model: add the observed surface density over an assumed mixing height (~800 m, documented), leave the free-troposphere/background profile untouched, and raise the standard surface baseline to a realistic ~1-2 ug/m3 background. Cap the implied tropospheric VCD at ~3e16 cm^-2.

verdict.reasoning:
I read all cited code and recomputed every number independently; all of them reproduce exactly.

(1) Code does what the finding says. /Users/mostafamahdi/twilight/crates/twilight-data/src/builder.rs:471-481: `let factor = target_surface / current_surface; for s in 0..gas_profile.num_shells { gas_profile.shells[s].no2_density *= factor; }` — the entire profile is multiplied by the surface ratio with no clamp or sanity bound anywhere. Notably the O3 branch in the same subsystem DOES clamp (mapping.rs:196, `du.clamp(220.0, 450.0)`); the NO2 branch has nothing.

(2) Profile numbers verified. /Users/mostafamahdi/twilight/crates/twilight-core/src/gas_absorption_data.rs:26904-26930 (STD_NO2_DENSITY) with the STD_ALT_KM grid at line 26831: surface density 4.0e15 m^-3 = 0.306 ug/m3; trapezoidal column = 9.698e18 m^-2 = 9.7e14 cm^-2; effective thickness column/surface = 2.42 km. All three match the finding.

(3) Mapping numbers verified. /Users/mostafamahdi/twilight/crates/twilight-weather/src/mapping.rs:214-216 converts ug/m3 to molecules/m3 correctly (the unit conversion itself is fine), and line 213 indeed labels 40 ug/m3 "moderate urban". 40 ug/m3 -> 5.237e17 m^-3, factor 130.9, scaled column 1.270e17 cm^-2; 10 ug/m3 -> 3.17e16 cm^-2; tau(435nm) at sigma=6e-19 cm^2 (Vandaele et al. 1998 gives ~5.5-6e-19 there at 294K) = 0.076. All match the finding's 131x / 1.27e17 / 3.2e16 / ~0.08 figures.

(4) The path is live and the absorption matters: map_gas_composition is called from twilight-weather/src/lib.rs:109, fed into builder::build_full_with_gas at twilight-cli/src/main.rs:669 and twilight-cpu/src/pipeline.rs:363, and gas_absorption.rs:785,801 adds the NO2 term to shell extinction as pure absorption (scattering preserved, SSA lowered), so the spurious column directly dims modeled blue sky radiance.

(5) Physics reasoning holds. Pinning a point surface measurement and scaling a fixed-shape profile is the surface-to-column fallacy: the implied effective depth here is 2.4 km vs the real ~0.5-1 km urban boundary layer, and the baseline is unrealistically clean (0.3 ug/m3), so the multiplicative factor is inflated ~10-100x. Resulting columns (1.27e17 cm^-2 at 40 ug/m3) exceed the most extreme TROPOMI/OMI megacity tropospheric NO2 VCDs (~2-3e16 cm^-2, e.g. Krotkov et al. 2016 / van Geffen et al. 2020) by 4-6x and typical urban values (~5e15-1.5e16) by 10-25x — i.e. the model produces NO2 loadings never observed anywhere on Earth from a routine urban reading. This is not a standard RT approximation (standard practice, e.g. libRadtran, scales to a target COLUMN, not a surface pin). A secondary aggravator I noted: STD_NO2_DENSITY is zero above 35 km and ~5e10 m^-3 at 25 km, so it also lacks the real stratospheric NO2 layer, making the profile shape doubly unsuitable for surface-pinned scaling.

Severity: high is correct, not critical. The spurious vertical tau ~0.08 (40 ug/m3) to ~0.2 (100 ug/m3) in the blue dims twilight radiance ~8-18% in cities — a real systematic bias on threshold-crossing times (order tens of seconds), but the code runs and the effect is not minutes-scale, so it does not meet the "materially shifts prayer times" bar for critical.

reviewed.summary: The pipeline's architecture is real, not fabricated: aerosols/clouds/weather-derived O3/NO2, terrain, skyglow, and polarization are all genuinely threaded into the single `compute_prayer_times` entry point, the two-pass coarse(0.5°)/fine(0.1°) scan exists as documented, and the SZA-to-clock-time bisection (SPA, morning [0,12]/evening [12,24] branches, bracket check) is correct. However, two findings are severe: (1) the pipeline reproducibly panics/aborts for any polar-summer location (max SZA < 90°) because `determine_prayer_times` index-underflows on an empty scan — exactly the persistent-twilight case the code claims to handle; (2) the CLI's default mode (hybrid MC, 100 rays) finds threshold crossings on a function with CV≈0.4-0.5 at the crossing region — empirically, Isha al-ahmar moves 5.2 minutes when going 100→400 photons, Isha al-abyad moves 1.7 minutes from a 10% SZA-grid shift, and at defaults al-ahmar lands before al-abyad (physically inverted). Deterministic sza-bit seeding makes this look reproducible while actually freezing an arbitrary noise realization. Several smaller integration seams (skyglow injected after refine-region selection, Metal seed masking collapsing the per-SZA seeds to a constant, DE440 azimuth time clamping) round out the picture.

allFindings.title: Pipeline aborts (index-out-of-bounds) for any polar-summer location instead of reporting persistent twilight
allFindings.evidence: threshold.rs:190-191: `for i in 0..(analyses.len() - 1) { let a0 = &analyses[i];` — with len()==0 the usize subtraction wraps in release and `analyses[0]` panics. Fed by pipeline.rs:566 `let sza_upper = max_sza_deg.map(|s| s.min(108.0)).unwrap_or(108.0);` + simulation.rs:325 `while sza <= sza_end + 1e-6` which yields an EMPTY scan when max SZA < 90°. Reproduced: `cargo run --release -p twilight-cli -- pray --lat 78.2 --lon 15.6 --date 2024-06-21 --tz 2 --scattering single --cpu` → "thread 'main' panicked at crates/twilight-threshold/src/threshold.rs:191:27: index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0" (workspace has panic="abort").
allFindings.why_wrong: The doc on compute_prayer_times (pipeline.rs:389) explicitly advertises "Also detects persistent twilight at high latitudes in summer", and high-latitude users (Tromsø, Murmansk, Svalbard — where fiqh guidance on twilight is most needed) are a primary audience for a physically-based Fajr/Isha engine. For any date/latitude where the sun stays above the horizon all day (lat ≳ 67° near solstice), the coarse scan starting at SZA 90° is empty, and determine_prayer_times crashes the whole process rather than returning the persistent_twilight result that was already computed at pipeline.rs:556.
allFindings.recommendation: Guard `determine_prayer_times` with `if analyses.len() < 2 { return PrayerTimeResult { fajr_sza_deg: None, ... } }`, and in the pipeline short-circuit to a persistent-twilight output when sza_upper <= 90 instead of running the scan.

allFindings.title: Default hybrid MC mode finds the threshold crossing on a noisy function: prayer times move 1-5 minutes with innocuous parameter changes and produce physically inverted Isha ordering
allFindings.evidence: CLI default is the noisy path (main.rs:154-159): `#[arg(long, value_enum, default_value = "hybrid")] scattering` and `#[arg(short, long, default_value = "100")] photons`. Measured (Mecca 2024-03-15, clear sky, CPU): defaults → Fajr 05:27:47 / abyad 19:30:36 / ahmar 19:28:09 (ahmar BEFORE abyad — physically inverted, red glow must outlast white); --sza-step 0.45 → abyad 19:28:54 (-1.7 min); --photons 400 → ahmar 19:33:22 (+5.2 min, crossing SZA 104.31°→105.52°). The pipeline's own coarse log shows non-monotone order-of-magnitude noise at the crossing region: "SZA 105.5: mesopic=3.8001e-4 ... SZA 107.0: mesopic=3.3160e-3 ... SZA 107.5: mesopic=1.6574e-5" (107.0° is 10x brighter than 105.5° and ABOVE the 3e-3 Isha threshold). The repo's own diagnostic (cargo test cv_baseline, simulation.rs:947) confirms: CV=0.40 at SZA 104, 0.44 at 105, 0.54 at 108 with 200 rays — twice the default budget. With the measured slope (~2.1x/degree), sigma_SZA ≈ CV/0.76 ≈ 0.5-0.7° ≈ 2-3 clock minutes (1-sigma).
allFindings.why_wrong: Standard MC RT codes (e.g. MYSTIC/libRadtran) report estimator standard error and require it to be small relative to the quantity being resolved; here a root-finding problem (threshold crossing) is solved on an unconverged estimator with no error estimate, no convergence check, and no adaptive photon allocation near the crossing. Worse, threshold.rs:196-198 takes the FIRST downward crossing (`isha_abyad_sza.is_none() && a0 >= thresh && a1 < thresh`), so over the ~13 independent fine-grid points before the true crossing, any single downward noise spike declares Isha early — a one-sided bias, not just jitter. The sza-bit-derived seeds (simulation.rs:216-218, 266-267) make reruns bit-identical, which masks the problem: the output is a frozen arbitrary noise realization, not a converged answer.
allFindings.recommendation: Either (a) raise the default photon budget until the estimator standard error at the crossing maps to <0.05° of SZA (and verify with the existing cv_baseline harness), (b) fit/smooth log-luminance vs SZA (it is near-exponential) across the fine grid and find the crossing on the fit instead of on raw adjacent pairs, and/or (c) use common random numbers across SZAs deliberately. Also add a sanity check that ahmar >= abyad.

allFindings.title: GPU dispatch seeds (sza_deg.to_bits) collapse to a single constant on the Metal hybrid path because all coarse-scan SZAs have zero low-32 mantissa bits
allFindings.evidence: gpu_dispatch.rs:160-163: `ScatteringMode::Hybrid => BatchKernel::Hybrid { secondary_rays: config.photons_per_wavelength as u32, seed: sza_deg.to_bits() }`. metal.rs:284: `let ray_seed = (seed & 0xFFFF_FFFF) | ((ray_start as u64) << 32);`. Verified bit patterns: 90.0→0x4056800000000000, 90.5→0x4056a00000000000, 104.5→0x405a200000000000, 108.0→0x405b000000000000 — low32 = 0x00000000 for EVERY half-degree coarse-scan SZA (any value needing ≤20 mantissa bits). So on GPU every coarse SZA gets ray_seed = (ray_start << 32) | 0, i.e. the identical RNG stream.
allFindings.why_wrong: The CPU path explicitly documents the seed scheme as "Include sza bits to decorrelate across SZA scan steps" (simulation.rs:217-218), and GPU is the default compute backend for `pray` when Metal is available (main.rs:1087-1097, twilight-cli default feature = ["gpu"]). On the GPU the decorrelation silently degenerates: coarse-scan MC noise is perfectly correlated across SZAs (only fine-scan fractional SZAs like 104.53 get nonzero low bits), so GPU and CPU runs have structurally different noise and cannot be parity-compared, and the effective seed entropy on the production path is zero.
allFindings.recommendation: Hash the full 64-bit seed before truncation (e.g. splitmix64(seed) in metal.rs before masking), or pass a per-SZA counter as the seed instead of raw f64 bits.

allFindings.title: Skyglow is injected after refine regions are chosen, so light-pollution-shifted crossings can fall outside the 0.1° fine window and land on the 0.5° coarse grid
allFindings.evidence: Refine regions come from skyglow-free coarse data (pipeline.rs:622-624: `let coarse_prayer = threshold::determine_prayer_times(coarse_analyses.clone(), ...)` with `let margin = input.sza_step + 0.1;` at line 628), but skyglow is added only afterwards at lines 692-698: `if let Some(ref sg) = input.skyglow { for sr in &mut deduped_results { ... sr.radiance[i] += sg.spectral_radiance[i]; } }` followed by re-analysis at line 702.
allFindings.why_wrong: The skyglow model itself estimates multi-minute shifts (pipeline.rs:761-765 calls `estimated_prayer_shift_minutes`; the CLI prints "Estimated prayer time shift: ~X minutes" for Bortle 5+). A multi-minute shift corresponds to >0.6° of SZA — larger than the refine margin (sza_step + 0.1 = 0.6° at defaults) — so for bright urban skies the final, skyglow-shifted crossing is interpolated between 0.5°-spaced coarse points instead of 0.1° fine points, silently degrading the advertised fine-pass precision exactly in the configuration where times shift most. Self-consistent would be to inject skyglow into the coarse analyses BEFORE choosing refine regions.
allFindings.recommendation: Add skyglow to coarse_results before computing coarse_analyses/coarse_prayer (it is a constant additive spectrum, so this is free), so refine regions bracket the actual shifted crossing.

allFindings.title: interpolate_crossing takes log() of luminance without guarding zero/negative values, which the MC estimator can produce at deep twilight
allFindings.evidence: `let log_lum0 = libm::log(lum0); let log_lum1 = libm::log(lum1); ... sza0 + frac * (sza1 - sza0)` with only a |lum1-lum0|<1e-30 equality guard. The repo's own diagnostic acknowledges negative MC totals: simulation.rs:1096-1097 `// Count negative seeds\n let neg_count = totals.iter().filter(|&&x| x < 0.0).count();` for the ALIS estimator used by the default `--fast` scalar path (simulation.rs:264-277).
allFindings.why_wrong: If the lower bracket luminance is exactly 0 the crossing pins to sza0 (frac→-0.0) — a silent edge bias; if it is negative (documented as occurring for ALIS seeds) log() returns NaN, the crossing SZA becomes NaN, and spa::find_zenith_crossing's bracket test `if sign_lo * sign_hi > 0.0 { return None; }` (spa.rs:715) does not reject NaN (all comparisons false), so the bisection degenerates and returns an endpoint-adjacent garbage clock time (spa.rs:738 `Some((lo + hi) / 2.0)`) instead of None. Standard practice is to clamp to a positive floor before log-space interpolation or fall back to linear interpolation for non-positive values.
allFindings.recommendation: Clamp luminances to a small positive floor (e.g. 1e-12 cd/m²) before log interpolation, and make find_zenith_crossing reject NaN targets (`if !target_zenith.is_finite() { return None; }`).

allFindings.title: End-to-end pipeline tests never exercise the CLI-default hybrid mode, and MC assertions tolerate 10x discrepancies; tracer.rs is dead code
allFindings.evidence: Every compute_prayer_times test uses `..PrayerTimeInput::default()` (pipeline.rs:920 etc.), whose default is `scattering_mode: ScatteringMode::Single` (pipeline.rs:115) — but the CLI ships `default_value = "hybrid"` (main.rs:155). MC validation is order-of-magnitude only: simulation.rs:734-736 `assert!(ratio < 10.0, "MC ... and single-scatter ... should be same order of magnitude")`. And `trace_photons_parallel` (tracer.rs:12) has zero call sites outside its own tests (grep across workspace), while README.md:232 lists "parallel tracer convergence" among covered test areas.
allFindings.why_wrong: The production path users actually run (hybrid, 100 rays, polarized) has no end-to-end test, so the variance and ordering pathologies demonstrated above (Isha ahmar before abyad, 5-minute photon-budget sensitivity) pass CI untouched. A 10x tolerance on MC-vs-deterministic agreement cannot catch errors that shift prayer times by many minutes (a 2x luminance error shifts the crossing ~1° ≈ 4 min). The CV diagnostics that DO measure the problem (cv_baseline/cv_deep_diag) assert nothing — they only eprintln. tracer.rs duplicates the photon-parallelism that simulation.rs implements differently (wavelength-parallel) and is dead weight.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a hybrid-mode end-to-end test asserting (a) ahmar >= abyad, (b) crossing SZA stable within 0.1° across two photon budgets; turn cv_baseline into an asserting test with a CV ceiling at the crossing SZAs; delete or wire up tracer.rs.

allFindings.title: Persistent-twilight flag uses a hardcoded 106° cutoff that is independent of the configured thresholds it claims to represent
allFindings.evidence: `// Step 4: Check maximum SZA to detect persistent twilight\n let max_sza_deg = engine.compute_max_sza();\n let persistent_twilight = max_sza_deg.map(|sza| sza < 106.0).unwrap_or(false);` while the output doc (pipeline.rs:160) defines it as "sun never drops below threshold".
allFindings.why_wrong: The actual thresholds are config-dependent and empirically cross at SZA 104.3-105.5° (measured Mecca runs), so a date with max SZA of 105.7° yields persistent_twilight=true even though valid Fajr/Isha crossings are still found and returned — contradictory output the CLI then prints as a warning (main.rs:1199-1223). Conversely, a stricter custom threshold crossing at 107° with max SZA 106.5° gives persistent_twilight=false with None times. The flag should be derived from whether the threshold crossing was actually found vs max_sza, not from a constant.
allFindings.recommendation: Set persistent_twilight per-threshold after determine_prayer_times: crossing not found AND max_sza < scan upper bound reached by the sun.

allFindings.title: DE440 azimuth_at_hour clamps negative UTC hours to 0, returning the wrong azimuth for terrain lookups when local→UTC conversion crosses midnight
allFindings.evidence: `let utc_hour = fractional_hour - self.spa_input.timezone; de.solar_position(... (utc_hour as i32).max(0), (((utc_hour - (utc_hour as i32) as f64) * 60.0) as i32).max(0), 0, ...)` — a sunrise at 04:30 local with tz=+5 gives utc_hour=-0.5, clamped to 00:00 UTC of the SAME date instead of 23:30 of the previous day (and hours >24 for negative timezones are passed through unwrapped).
allFindings.why_wrong: The azimuth is used to look up the terrain horizon angle at the sun's position (pipeline.rs:521-523), so with DE440 + terrain enabled in eastern-hemisphere timezones the horizon angle is sampled at an azimuth that can be tens of degrees off (sun moves ~15°/h in hour angle), corrupting the terrain-adjusted sunrise SZA. The SPA fallback path handles the same conversion correctly via set_time_from_fractional_hour.
allFindings.recommendation: Normalize utc_hour into [0,24) with a day offset passed to DE440 (or reuse the day-rollover-safe conversion used elsewhere), instead of `.max(0)` clamping.

allFindings.title: Module doc claims 2° coarse steps (actual: 0.5°) and the scan silently caps at SZA 108°, precluding darker custom thresholds
allFindings.evidence: pipeline.rs:11: `//! 4. MCRT Pass 1: coarse scan (2° steps) to locate threshold regions` vs pipeline.rs:56-57 `/// Default: 0.5` and main.rs:143-144 `#[arg(long, default_value = "0.5")] sza_step`. pipeline.rs:566: `let sza_upper = max_sza_deg.map(|s| s.min(108.0)).unwrap_or(108.0);`
allFindings.why_wrong: Minor doc drift, plus a functional edge: a user-supplied ThresholdConfig dark enough to cross beyond 108° (e.g. calibrating against 18°+ conventions at altitude, where the crossing sits at the cap) silently returns None for Fajr/Isha with no indication that the scan ceiling, not the sky, was the limit. ISNA/MWL 18° = SZA 108.0 sits exactly on the boundary point of the scan.
allFindings.recommendation: Fix the doc comment; extend the cap modestly (e.g. 110°) or emit a diagnostic when the threshold remains uncrossed at the scan ceiling while luminance is still above threshold.

allFindings.title: Library pipeline unconditionally dumps per-SZA debug lines to stderr
allFindings.evidence: Inside the library function compute_prayer_times_inner: `eprintln!("  SZA {:.1}: mesopic={:.4e} total_rad={:.4e}", sr.sza_deg, analysis.luminance_mesopic, ...)` plus `eprint!("Coarse scan: {} points ... ")` — printed for every coarse SZA on every call, with no verbosity gate (confirmed in CLI output without --verbose).
allFindings.why_wrong: A library crate (also consumed by twilight-ffi) should not write unconditional progress/debug output to stderr; the CLI already has a --verbose flag that this ignores. This pollutes any embedding application's logs and makes the FFI surface noisy.
allFindings.recommendation: Gate behind a verbosity flag in PrayerTimeInput or use the log crate.

verdict.reasoning: Independently verified every link in the chain and reproduced the crash. (1) threshold.rs:190-191 reads exactly `for i in 0..(analyses.len() - 1) { let a0 = &analyses[i];` with no emptiness guard; with len()==0 the usize subtraction wraps to usize::MAX in release (overflow checks off) and `analyses[0]` panics. (2) The empty input is real: pipeline.rs:329-345 `compute_max_sza` returns the day's maximum SZA (~78° for lat 78.2 at June solstice, since the sun never drops below ~11.6° altitude); pipeline.rs:566 clamps `sza_upper` to that value; pipeline.rs:598 calls the scan with start=90.0 > end≈78; simulation.rs:325 `while sza <= sza_end + 1e-6` never executes, returning an empty Vec. (3) No guard exists: grep shows `persistent_twilight` (pipeline.rs:556, correctly true for this case) is only copied into the output struct at line 743 — determine_prayer_times at pipeline.rs:623-624 runs unconditionally. (4) Cargo.toml:41 has `panic = "abort"` in [profile.release]. (5) Reproduced with the prebuilt binary: `./target/release/twilight-cli pray --lat 78.2 --lon 15.6 --date 2024-06-21 --tz 2 --scattering single --cpu` → "Coarse scan ... 1.2µs" then "panicked at crates/twilight-threshold/src/threshold.rs:191:27: index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0". The panic occurring at the index (line 191) rather than the subtraction (line 190) empirically confirms the release-mode wrap. (6) pipeline.rs:389 doc comment "Also detects persistent twilight at high latitudes in summer" confirms this is an advertised capability that instead aborts the process for its target input class (any location with midnight sun, lat ≳ 66.6° near solstice: Tromsø max SZA ≈ 87°, Svalbard ≈ 78°). Minor refinement only: the crash requires max SZA < 90° (true polar day); white-night cases with 90° < max SZA < 106° produce a non-empty scan and do not panic — consistent with the reviewer's wording. Critical severity is justified: deterministic process abort for a whole class of valid inputs in an explicitly advertised capability, precisely where physically-based Fajr/Isha guidance matters most.

finding.title: Default hybrid MC mode finds the threshold crossing on a noisy function: prayer times move 1-5 minutes with innocuous parameter changes and produce physically inverted Isha ordering
finding.evidence: CLI default is the noisy path (main.rs:154-159): `#[arg(long, value_enum, default_value = "hybrid")] scattering` and `#[arg(short, long, default_value = "100")] photons`. Measured (Mecca 2024-03-15, clear sky, CPU): defaults → Fajr 05:27:47 / abyad 19:30:36 / ahmar 19:28:09 (ahmar BEFORE abyad — physically inverted, red glow must outlast white); --sza-step 0.45 → abyad 19:28:54 (-1.7 min); --photons 400 → ahmar 19:33:22 (+5.2 min, crossing SZA 104.31°→105.52°). The pipeline's own coarse log shows non-monotone order-of-magnitude noise at the crossing region: "SZA 105.5: mesopic=3.8001e-4 ... SZA 107.0: mesopic=3.3160e-3 ... SZA 107.5: mesopic=1.6574e-5" (107.0° is 10x brighter than 105.5° and ABOVE the 3e-3 Isha threshold). The repo's own diagnostic (cargo test cv_baseline, simulation.rs:947) confirms: CV=0.40 at SZA 104, 0.44 at 105, 0.54 at 108 with 200 rays — twice the default budget. With the measured slope (~2.1x/degree), sigma_SZA ≈ CV/0.76 ≈ 0.5-0.7° ≈ 2-3 clock minutes (1-sigma).
finding.why_wrong: Standard MC RT codes (e.g. MYSTIC/libRadtran) report estimator standard error and require it to be small relative to the quantity being resolved; here a root-finding problem (threshold crossing) is solved on an unconverged estimator with no error estimate, no convergence check, and no adaptive photon allocation near the crossing. Worse, threshold.rs:196-198 takes the FIRST downward crossing (`isha_abyad_sza.is_none() && a0 >= thresh && a1 < thresh`), so over the ~13 independent fine-grid points before the true crossing, any single downward noise spike declares Isha early — a one-sided bias, not just jitter. The sza-bit-derived seeds (simulation.rs:216-218, 266-267) make reruns bit-identical, which masks the problem: the output is a frozen arbitrary noise realization, not a converged answer.
finding.recommendation: Either (a) raise the default photon budget until the estimator standard error at the crossing maps to <0.05° of SZA (and verify with the existing cv_baseline harness), (b) fit/smooth log-luminance vs SZA (it is near-exponential) across the fine grid and find the crossing on the fit instead of on raw adjacent pairs, and/or (c) use common random numbers across SZAs deliberately. Also add a sanity check that ahmar >= abyad.

verdict.reasoning: I verified every code citation and reproduced the empirical claims by running the binary myself. (1) Defaults confirmed: crates/twilight-cli/src/main.rs:154-159 sets `default_value = "hybrid"` for scattering and `default_value = "100"` for photons — while the library's own doc (crates/twilight-cpu/src/simulation.rs:74) says "Recommended: 10000+ for converged results, 1000 for quick estimates" and `SimulationConfig::default()` uses 10_000. (2) First-crossing logic confirmed: threshold.rs:195-198 (and 209-211, 225-227) latch the FIRST adjacent-pair downward crossing via `is_none() && a0 >= thresh && a1 < thresh`; pipeline.rs:568-714 runs a coarse 0.5° scan then a 0.1° fine scan (margin = sza_step+0.1 → ~13 points/region, my run logged "Fine scan: 16 points") and calls determine_prayer_times on raw per-point MC estimates. grep over pipeline.rs/simulation.rs/threshold confirms NO variance estimate, standard error, or convergence check anywhere — unlike standard MC RT practice (MYSTIC/libRadtran report estimator std error). (3) Deterministic sza-bit seeds confirmed at simulation.rs:216-223 and 266-267; each grid point is an independent frozen noise realization. (4) Empirics reproduced exactly (Mecca 2024-03-15, --cpu): defaults → Fajr 05:27:47, abyad 19:30:36, ahmar 19:28:09 (bit-identical to the finding); --sza-step 0.45 → abyad 19:28:54 (-1.7 min); --photons 400 → ahmar 19:33:22, SZA 105.52° (+5.2 min). The quoted coarse log is verbatim real: SZA 105.5 mesopic=3.8001e-4, 107.0 mesopic=3.3160e-3 (10x brighter and above the 0.003 cd/m² abyad threshold of threshold.rs:87), 107.5 mesopic=1.6574e-5 — order-of-magnitude non-monotone noise exactly where the root is found. cv_baseline test exists as cited (simulation.rs:947). Slope from my log is ~2.6-2.8x/degree, so sigma_SZA ≈ 0.4-0.6° ≈ 2-3 min, consistent with the observed 1.7-5.2 min shifts. HOWEVER, one evidence sub-claim is backwards: the reviewer calls the DEFAULT run's ordering (ahmar 19:28 before abyad 19:30) "physically inverted, red glow must outlast white". That inverts the standard convention: in evening twilight the red shafaq (al-ahmar, ~9-12° depression) disappears BEFORE the white shafaq (al-abyad, ~15-18°); that is precisely why Abu Hanifa's abyad-based Isha is the later one (the CLI's own labels say so). So ahmar-before-abyad is the CORRECT ordering. Ironically, a genuine physical inversion DOES occur — in the --photons 400 run I reproduced, ahmar (19:33:22) lands 3.6 min AFTER abyad (19:29:47), proving the noise produces non-physical orderings under innocuous parameter changes; the reviewer just attached the inversion to the wrong run with reversed physics reasoning. The 2.4-min default ahmar/abyad gap (should be tens of minutes for 12° vs 15-18° conventions) is itself suspect, but for threshold-config reasons outside this finding. Core mechanism, magnitude, and severity all stand.
verdict.correction: The default hybrid MC mode (100 photons, vs the library's own recommendation of 10,000+) solves a root-finding problem on an unconverged estimator with no error estimate or convergence check, and threshold.rs takes the first downward noise crossing — a one-sided early-Isha bias frozen in place by deterministic sza-bit seeds. Reproduced: prayer times shift 1.7-5.2 minutes under innocuous parameter changes (--sza-step 0.45, --photons 400), and the coarse log shows order-of-magnitude non-monotone noise at the crossing (105.5°: 3.8e-4 vs 107.0°: 3.3e-3). One correction to the evidence: the DEFAULT run's ordering (ahmar 19:28:09 before abyad 19:30:36) is physically and jurisprudentially CORRECT — the red shafaq disappears before the white one, which is why abyad-based (Hanafi) Isha is later; "red glow must outlast white" is backwards. The genuine physically inverted ordering appears in the --photons 400 run, where ahmar (19:33:22) lands 3.6 minutes AFTER abyad (19:29:47) purely due to MC noise — which still demonstrates the headline claim that noise produces non-physical Isha orderings.

reviewed.summary: The unit-test suite is more substantive than typical "AI slop" — only ~71 of 1090 #[test] fns (6.5%) assert nothing stronger than finiteness/non-negativity, and twilight-solar (NREL SPA Table A5, JPL Horizons vectors), twilight-threshold (CIE 555/507 nm peaks), twilight-data (US Standard Atmosphere values) and gas_absorption (Serdyuchenko/HITRAN magnitudes) carry real literature-anchored golden values. However, the headline claims are dishonest: the "978 passing / ~14 seconds" badge matches no buildable configuration (actual ~1050 default-feature tests; README's own table sums to 991; the run takes minutes-to-tens-of-minutes, not 14 s; there is no CI workflow behind the badge), the advertised cross-backend GPU parity coverage is structurally unrunnable (19 tests behind features that cannot compile, 16 more guaranteed no-ops in the default build, 14 Metal tests that silently pass when the device/shader fails to init), and when the Metal tests actually execute on real Apple Silicon, two of them FAIL with a GPU dispatch error. Most damning for a prayer-times engine: no test in the workspace asserts that fajr_time or isha_time is ever actually produced — all end-to-end assertions are wrapped in if-let guards that vacuously pass if the pipeline returns None, and the radiance engine itself has zero external reference validation (no libRadtran/DISORT/measured-twilight comparison), only self-consistency.

allFindings.title: Advertised cross-backend GPU parity tests are structurally unrunnable: 19 tests behind features that cannot compile, and the parity tests require >=2 backends when at most 1 (Metal) can ever build
allFindings.why_wrong: The 11 vulkan + 4 cuda + 4 webgpu tests (tests.rs:1068-1495) are gated behind features that fail to compile because the shader sources they include were deleted (orchestrator-confirmed: "couldn't read ... No such file or directory"). The 3 cross-backend parity tests additionally early-return unless >=2 backends initialize — impossible when only Metal can build. So the README's central GPU-correctness claim ("all backends produce identical physics") is backed by tests that can never execute a single assertion on any buildable configuration. This is a fabricated capability presented as real validation.
allFindings.recommendation: Either restore the deleted CUDA/WGSL/SPIR-V shaders so the features compile, or delete the vulkan/cuda/webgpu backends, their tests, and every README claim about cross-backend parity. Replace silent `return` guards with `panic!`/`#[ignore]` so unrunnable parity tests are visible as skipped, not green.

allFindings.title: On real Apple Silicon with --features metal, the test suite is RED: hybrid_scatter_v2 Metal dispatch errors fail two tests, contradicting the 'tests-978_passing' badge
allFindings.evidence: Observed run of `cargo test -p twilight-gpu --features metal`: "thread 'tests::layer4_metal::metal_multi_hybrid_matches_serial_chunk' ... panicked at crates/twilight-gpu/src/tests.rs:1032:18: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Dispatch(\"Metal command buffer error in hybrid_scatter_v2 chunk: Impacting Interactivity (0000000e:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorImpactingInteractivity)\")" — "test result: FAILED. 13 passed; 1 failed". A prior full-suite run on the same machine also showed "metal_single_hybrid_matches_one_item_batch ... FAILED" and "metal_multi_hybrid_matches_serial_chunk ... FAILED".
allFindings.why_wrong: The README badge claims all tests pass, but the only GPU backend that compiles produces real failures when a Metal device is present: the v2 hybrid kernel's command buffer is killed by the macOS GPU watchdog. This corroborates the maintainer's report that the Metal shader path is broken (git log itself admits "v2 NaN under investigation", "GPU timeout detection"). The failures are load-sensitive (one test passed on re-run) which makes them flaky as well as failing.
allFindings.recommendation: Fix or chunk the hybrid_scatter_v2 dispatch so it stays under the GPU watchdog budget (smaller dispatches, command-buffer splitting), or mark these tests as known-failing. Do not publish a green badge while the only runnable GPU configuration fails.

allFindings.title: 30 GPU tests pass as silent no-ops: 16 default-build tests guard on an unconditionally-empty backend list, and 14 Metal tests swallow init errors with .ok() then `else { return }`
allFindings.why_wrong: Because `default = []`, every cfg(feature) block inside init_all_backends() is compiled out in `cargo test --workspace` (the exact command the README quotes), so init_all_backends() unconditionally returns an empty Vec and all 16 tests that guard on it are mathematically guaranteed to pass without executing one assertion — including the README-advertised "benchmarks" and "cross-backend physics". The 14 metal-gated tests use `.ok()` which discards the init error: if the Metal shader fails to compile at runtime, every Metal test still passes green. Standard practice (e.g. wgpu, rust-gpu CI) is to emit a skip marker or panic when required hardware is absent, never to silently pass.
allFindings.recommendation: Convert device-unavailable paths to explicit skips (e.g. `eprintln!` + `#[ignore]`-by-default, or a custom harness that reports SKIPPED), and make try_init failure (as opposed to no-device) a hard test failure so a broken shader cannot produce a green suite.

allFindings.title: No test in the workspace asserts that fajr_time or isha_time is ever produced — every end-to-end prayer-time assertion is wrapped in an if-let that vacuously passes on None
allFindings.evidence: pipeline.rs:971-977: "if let Some(dep) = output.fajr_depression_deg {\n            assert!(\n                dep > 12.0 && dep < 18.0, ...". pipeline.rs:995: "if let (Some(fajr), Some(sunrise)) = (output.fajr_time, output.sunrise_time) {". compute_prayer_times_mecca_produces_results (910-952) asserts only sunrise_time/sunset_time .is_some() and !persistent_twilight; grep across the workspace finds no `fajr_time.is_some()` or `isha_time.is_some()` assertion anywhere.
allFindings.why_wrong: The project's entire purpose is computing Fajr/Isha. If the radiance pipeline regressed so the threshold crossing is never found (fajr_time = None for Mecca at equinox — a non-polar, must-succeed case), the full "pipeline end-to-end (Mecca, London)" suite advertised in the README would stay green. The headline physics check (depression 12-18 deg, the "~15 deg" claim in the README) is likewise unenforced: it only runs if the value happens to exist. This is the canonical conditional-assertion anti-pattern; the load-bearing capability has zero enforced coverage.
allFindings.recommendation: In the Mecca/London tests, replace if-let guards with `let fajr = output.fajr_time.expect("Fajr must be found at Mecca equinox");` and assert the depression band unconditionally. Add at least one pinned regression value (date, lat/lon -> expected Fajr time +/- tolerance).

allFindings.title: README test counts are wrong in every direction: total '978' does not equal its own table sum (991) nor the actual count (~1050); per-crate numbers are stale and the gpu figure (139) is unreachable in any buildable configuration
allFindings.evidence: README.md:225: "978 tests, ~14 seconds. `cargo test --workspace`". Table rows: "`twilight-core` | 311", "`twilight-gpu` | 139", "`twilight-cpu` | 82", "`twilight-solar` | 73" — these sum to 991, not 978. Measured via `cargo test -p <crate> -- --list`: core=394 (not 311), data=154, gpu=120 default / 134 with metal (139 matches neither; 139 = 120 + exactly the 19 vulkan/cuda/webgpu tests that cannot compile), cpu=75 default (9 more behind the non-default `gpu` feature), solar=74. Workspace default-feature unit-test total ≈ 1050, of which 15 are #[ignore]d (so they would report 'ignored', not 'passing').
allFindings.why_wrong: A correctness-marketing table that disagrees with itself (978 vs 991) and with the code (core off by 83 tests; gpu count only reconstructable by including tests behind non-compiling features) shows the numbers were written, not measured. The badge text "978 passing" is unverifiable by any single `cargo test` invocation that exists.
allFindings.recommendation: Regenerate the table from an actual `cargo test --workspace` run, state which features were enabled, and report ignored/skipped counts separately. Automate it so it cannot drift.

allFindings.title: '978 tests, ~14 seconds' is false by more than an order of magnitude: twilight-cpu alone consumed 582 s of CPU in release without finishing, and assertion-free MC diagnostics dominate the runtime
allFindings.evidence: README.md:225: "978 tests, ~14 seconds. `cargo test --workspace`". Measured: `/usr/bin/time cargo test -p twilight-cpu --release` was still running when killed at "369.77 real 582.37 user"; the debug-mode workspace run's twilight_cpu binary accumulated >35 CPU-minutes without completing; a 14-test metal subset of twilight-gpu took "finished in 483.66s"; gpu tests print "test tests::statistical_hybrid_gpu_vs_cpu_deep_twilight has been running for over 60 seconds".
allFindings.why_wrong: `cargo test --workspace` as quoted builds in debug and includes heavyweight Monte Carlo jobs disguised as unit tests (cv_baseline: 50-200 seeds x 200 rays x 16 SZAs; cv_deep_diag: 500 seeds), so the real wall time is minutes to tens of minutes, not ~14 s. Even granting that the machine was contended during measurement (2-3 concurrent suites), 582 s of user CPU for one crate in release cannot fit a 14 s workspace budget on any consumer machine.
allFindings.recommendation: Move cv_baseline/cv_deep_diag and the statistical GPU comparisons behind `#[ignore]` or a `--features diagnostics` gate, then re-measure and publish an honest timing with the build profile stated.

allFindings.title: The 'tests-978_passing' badge is a hardcoded static shields.io badge linking to a GitHub Actions page, but the repo contains no CI workflow at all
allFindings.evidence: README.md:6: "" — `ls .github/workflows` returns "NO .github/workflows" (no .github directory exists).
allFindings.why_wrong: This mimics a CI status badge (green, links to /actions) while being a free-text static badge whose value no system verifies. Convention (shields.io/GitHub Actions docs) is that a passing-tests badge reflects an automated run; hand-writing 'passing' into a badge that nothing checks is a fabricated trust signal — especially for a project marketed to a religious community on correctness.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a real GitHub Actions workflow running `cargo test --workspace` and use the actions workflow status badge, or remove the badge.

allFindings.title: Heavy Monte Carlo diagnostics with zero assertions are registered as #[test] (cv_baseline, cv_deep_diag, plus weather zero_visibility_handled), inflating the count and dominating suite runtime
allFindings.evidence: simulation.rs:947 `fn cv_baseline()` runs `photon::hybrid_scatter_radiance_alis` for 16 SZAs x 50-200 seeds x 200 rays and ends with only `eprintln!` calls — an automated scan of its body finds no assert!/unwrap/expect. cv_deep_diag ("500 seeds, dump distribution stats") likewise contains no assertion (its only unwrap is the sort comparator `a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap()`); doc comment says "Run with: cargo test -p twilight-cpu --release -- cv_deep_diag --nocapture".
allFindings.why_wrong: These are profiling/diagnostic scripts, not tests: they cannot fail no matter what the estimator returns (including all-zero or wildly divergent CV), yet they count toward the advertised test number and consume the bulk of `cargo test --workspace` wall time. A variance-characterization run that asserts nothing about variance is exactly the 'test theater' the maintainer suspects.
allFindings.recommendation: Mark them #[ignore] (run on demand) or convert to real tests by asserting a CV ceiling per SZA (e.g. CV < 0.3 at SZA 105 with N seeds) so variance regressions actually fail the suite.

allFindings.title: The radiance engine — the component that actually determines prayer times — has zero external golden validation; all RT tests are internal self-consistency
allFindings.evidence: Workspace grep for "libradtran|disort|mystic|sbdart|modtran|reference radiance|golden" matches nothing except comments about Golden, CO in spa.rs. The single_scatter test list is entirely invariants: "radiance_positive_for_sunlit_atmosphere", "radiance_decreases_with_deeper_twilight", "spectrum_matches_individual_radiance", "ground_reflection_non_negative"... The GPU "CPU f64 oracle" (README:239) is the same Rust code the GPU ports, so GPU-vs-oracle parity is also self-referential.
allFindings.why_wrong: By contrast with the inputs (SPA has the NREL Table A5 case, cross-sections cite Serdyuchenko/HITRAN magnitudes, vision cites CIE peaks), no sky-radiance value is ever pinned against an independent code (libRadtran/DISORT/MYSTIC twilight benchmarks, e.g. Emde et al. 2017 IPRT cases) or measurement. A sign/normalization error in the scattering integral that scales all radiance smoothly would satisfy every monotonicity/non-negativity/self-consistency test while shifting the threshold crossing — i.e., shifting Fajr/Isha — undetected. Calling the CPU implementation an 'oracle' overstates it: it is a reference for f32 parity, not for physics.
allFindings.recommendation: Add at least a handful of pinned single-scatter zenith radiance values from libRadtran/MYSTIC (or published twilight radiance, e.g. Patat et al. 2006) at 2-3 SZAs/wavelengths with documented tolerances, plus a pinned regression value for the final Mecca Fajr time.

allFindings.title: 15 #[ignore]d tests — including the README-advertised 'DE440 vs Horizons' validation — never run in the quoted command and depend on a 114 MB gitignored file, so they can never run in CI or fresh clones
allFindings.why_wrong: These are genuinely good golden tests (hardcoded JPL Horizons state vectors; I ran them with the local .bsp and all 10 passed in 0.01 s), but they are doubly skipped — #[ignore] AND silent-return when the gitignored data file is absent — so they contribute nothing to the '978 passing' figure or to any CI, while the README presents them as part of the per-crate coverage. The double skip also means `cargo test -- --ignored` on a fresh clone silently passes them without testing anything.
allFindings.recommendation: Document the de440.bsp download step, use an env var (no hardcoded user path), and make the --ignored run fail loudly when the file is missing rather than silently returning.

allFindings.title: Leftover temporary review scratch file committed as an integration test ('Delete after use') with a hardcoded user home path
allFindings.evidence: Line 1: "//! Temporary verification test (adversarial review). Delete after use." Lines 5-7: "fn bsp() -> Option<String> {\n    let p = \"/Users/mostafamahdi/twilight/data/de440.bsp\".to_string();".
allFindings.why_wrong: The file self-identifies as temporary scratch that should have been deleted, contributes one more #[ignore]d, machine-specific test to the count, and bakes an absolute path to the maintainer's home directory into the repository — it can never run anywhere else.
allFindings.recommendation: Delete the file, or fold its zenith-crossing comparison into de440.rs tests using the DE440_PATH env var.

finding.title: Advertised cross-backend GPU parity tests are structurally unrunnable: 19 tests behind features that cannot compile, and the parity tests require >=2 backends when at most 1 (Metal) can ever build
finding.why_wrong: The 11 vulkan + 4 cuda + 4 webgpu tests (tests.rs:1068-1495) are gated behind features that fail to compile because the shader sources they include were deleted (orchestrator-confirmed: "couldn't read ... No such file or directory"). The 3 cross-backend parity tests additionally early-return unless >=2 backends initialize — impossible when only Metal can build. So the README's central GPU-correctness claim ("all backends produce identical physics") is backed by tests that can never execute a single assertion on any buildable configuration. This is a fabricated capability presented as real validation.
finding.recommendation: Either restore the deleted CUDA/WGSL/SPIR-V shaders so the features compile, or delete the vulkan/cuda/webgpu backends, their tests, and every README claim about cross-backend parity. Replace silent `return` guards with `panic!`/`#[ignore]` so unrunnable parity tests are visible as skipped, not green.

verdict.reasoning: I verified every load-bearing claim by reading the code myself. (1) Shader sources: `ls crates/twilight-gpu/shaders/` shows only twilight.metal; there is no build.rs in twilight-gpu, yet vulkan.rs:50-53 does `include_bytes!("../shaders/single_scatter.spv")` (+ mcrt_trace.spv, hybrid_scatter.spv, garstang_zenith.spv), cuda.rs:25 does `include_str!("../shaders/twilight.cu")`, and wgpu_backend.rs:16 does `include_str!("../shaders/twilight.wgsl")`. These macros resolve at compile time, so the vulkan/cuda/webgpu features cannot compile — matching the orchestrator-confirmed "couldn't read ... No such file or directory". `git show --stat ad46e1c` confirms that commit deleted twilight.cu (1296 lines), twilight.wgsl (1222), twilight.comp (1247), and all four .spv binaries, while keeping only twilight.metal. (2) Test counts: tests.rs mod layer4_vulkan (`#[cfg(feature = "vulkan")]`, lines 1068-1381) contains exactly 11 #[test] fns (verified by awk count), layer4_cuda (lines 1385-1429) has 4, layer4_wgpu (lines 1433-1477) has 4 — 19 tests gated behind features that cannot build. (3) Parity early-returns: cross_backend_single_scatter_parity (tests.rs:1548-1552), cross_backend_mcrt_sign_agreement (tests.rs:1697-1700), and cross_backend_deep_night_all_agree_zero (tests.rs:1754-1757) all contain `if backends.len() < 2 { return; }`. Since init_all_backends() (tests.rs:1493-1541) only pushes backends behind the same per-feature cfg gates and only Metal can compile, backends.len() can never exceed 1 on any buildable configuration, so no pairwise parity assertion can ever execute. A fourth test, cross_backend_physics_monotonicity_all_agree (tests.rs:1783-1791), requires only a non-empty backend list, but it checks each backend independently (monotonicity vs SZA) — it performs no cross-backend comparison, so it does not rescue the parity claim. (4) README claims verified verbatim: README.md:131 "Four hand-tuned backends with native shaders written from scratch for each API. ... Cross-backend parity tests with CPU f64 oracle ensure all backends produce identical physics." and README.md:231 "| `twilight-gpu` | 139 | Buffer packing, f64 oracle, Metal + Vulkan parity, cross-backend physics, 11 parity tests, benchmarks |". The README also has a 4-backend feature matrix (README.md:142-155) and README.md:215 advertising "Metal, Vulkan, CUDA, wgpu ... cross-backend parity tests". So the README's GPU-correctness claim is backed exclusively by code that either fails to compile or unconditionally early-returns: a fabricated capability presented as real validation. The reviewer's characterization is accurate in every checked detail (the only trivial nuance: there are 4 cross_backend_* tests, but only the 3 cited ones are actual parity comparisons, and those are exactly the ones with the >=2-backend guard).

finding.evidence: Observed run of `cargo test -p twilight-gpu --features metal`: "thread 'tests::layer4_metal::metal_multi_hybrid_matches_serial_chunk' ... panicked at crates/twilight-gpu/src/tests.rs:1032:18: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Dispatch(\"Metal command buffer error in hybrid_scatter_v2 chunk: Impacting Interactivity (0000000e:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorImpactingInteractivity)\")" — "test result: FAILED. 13 passed; 1 failed". A prior full-suite run on the same machine also showed "metal_single_hybrid_matches_one_item_batch ... FAILED" and "metal_multi_hybrid_matches_serial_chunk ... FAILED".
finding.why_wrong: The README badge claims all tests pass, but the only GPU backend that compiles produces real failures when a Metal device is present: the v2 hybrid kernel's command buffer is killed by the macOS GPU watchdog. This corroborates the maintainer's report that the Metal shader path is broken (git log itself admits "v2 NaN under investigation", "GPU timeout detection"). The failures are load-sensitive (one test passed on re-run) which makes them flaky as well as failing.
finding.recommendation: Fix or chunk the hybrid_scatter_v2 dispatch so it stays under the GPU watchdog budget (smaller dispatches, command-buffer splitting), or mark these tests as known-failing. Do not publish a green badge while the only runnable GPU configuration fails.

verdict.reasoning: Independently reproduced on this Apple M2 Pro: `cargo test -p twilight-gpu --features metal --release` finished "131 passed; 3 failed". Both cited tests failed with the exact error quoted in the finding: metal_multi_hybrid_matches_serial_chunk panicked at crates/twilight-gpu/src/tests.rs:1032 and metal_single_hybrid_matches_one_item_batch panicked at tests.rs:968, both with `Dispatch("Metal command buffer error in hybrid_scatter_v2 chunk: Impacting Interactivity (0000000e:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorImpactingInteractivity)")` — the macOS GPU watchdog killing the command buffer. A third test the finding didn't mention also failed: statistical_hybrid_gpu_vs_cpu_deep_twilight (tests.rs:3521, GPU/CPU ratio 1.3239 outside [0.8,1.3], one GPU seed a 4x outlier), further corroborating Metal hybrid instability. The mechanism is visible in source: metal.rs dispatch_hybrid_v2_chunk (lines 704-771) encodes all chunks into ONE command buffer (loop at 742-752) and commits once with waitUntilCompleted (755-756), so total GPU time exceeds the watchdog limit; the error check at 758-768 only detects the failure, it does not prevent it, despite commit "Fix 5000-ray Metal prayer: split dispatch + GPU timeout detection". Git log confirms known breakage ("Use v1 kernel for hybrid_scatter dispatch (v2 NaN under investigation)"). README line 6 badge claims "tests-978_passing" and line 225 says "978 tests, ~14 seconds. cargo test --workspace" — but that count comes from the default-features path where try_metal() (tests.rs:607-613) returns None and every GPU test silently no-ops. On the only GPU backend that compiles, with a real device present, the suite is red. Minor nuance: failures are load-sensitive/flaky (one cited test passed on the reviewer's re-run), but in a full-suite run on real hardware both cited tests plus one more failed, so the finding's core claim holds exactly as stated.

finding.title: 30 GPU tests pass as silent no-ops: 16 default-build tests guard on an unconditionally-empty backend list, and 14 Metal tests swallow init errors with .ok() then `else { return }`
finding.why_wrong: Because `default = []`, every cfg(feature) block inside init_all_backends() is compiled out in `cargo test --workspace` (the exact command the README quotes), so init_all_backends() unconditionally returns an empty Vec and all 16 tests that guard on it are mathematically guaranteed to pass without executing one assertion — including the README-advertised "benchmarks" and "cross-backend physics". The 14 metal-gated tests use `.ok()` which discards the init error: if the Metal shader fails to compile at runtime, every Metal test still passes green. Standard practice (e.g. wgpu, rust-gpu CI) is to emit a skip marker or panic when required hardware is absent, never to silently pass.
finding.recommendation: Convert device-unavailable paths to explicit skips (e.g. `eprintln!` + `#[ignore]`-by-default, or a custom harness that reports SKIPPED), and make try_init failure (as opposed to no-device) a hard test failure so a broken shader cannot produce a green suite.

verdict.reasoning:
I read /Users/mostafamahdi/twilight/crates/twilight-gpu/src/tests.rs, metal.rs, Cargo.toml, README.md, and ran the tests. Every load-bearing claim holds.

(1) UNCONDITIONAL NO-OPS IN DEFAULT BUILD: twilight-gpu/Cargo.toml has `default = []`. init_all_backends (tests.rs:1493-1541) consists solely of four #[cfg(feature = "metal"/"vulkan"/"cuda"/"webgpu")] blocks pushing into `backends`; with default features all four are compiled out, so it unconditionally returns an empty Vec — the function even carries `#[allow(dead_code, unused_mut)]` (tests.rs:1492) because `backends` is never mutated in that configuration. Exactly 16 ungated #[test] fns call it and early-return before any assertion: `len() < 2` guards at 1549, 1698, 1755 and `is_empty()` guards at 1789, 1840, 1891, 1941, 2006, 2080, 2150, 2178, 2228, 2303, 2851, 3395, 3548. I verified bodies (e.g. cross_backend_physics_monotonicity_all_agree 1784-1822, benchmark_single_scatter_gpu_latency 1833+) — all assertions sit after the guard.

(2) EMPIRICAL: `cargo test -p twilight-gpu cross_backend` → "4 passed ... finished in 0.00s"; `... benchmark` → "5 passed ... 0.00s"; `... statistical` → "1 passed ... 0.00s". All green no-ops under the exact default-feature configuration the README's quoted command (`cargo test --workspace`, README.md:225 "978 tests, ~14 seconds") uses. README.md:231 explicitly advertises these as twilight-gpu coverage: "cross-backend physics ... benchmarks", and the repo badge claims "tests-978_passing".

(3) ERROR-SWALLOWING METAL TESTS: try_metal (tests.rs:607-613) is `crate::try_init(&config).ok()`; 13 tests use `let Some(gpu) = try_metal() else { return };` (lines 617, 633, 641, 648, 655, 665, 701, 733, 761, 817, 882, 940, 1000), and a 14th metal-gated test (tests.rs:1613-1615) uses `let Ok(mut gpu) = crate::try_init(&config) else { return; }` — identical error-discarding semantics, so the count of 14 is correct. Metal init compiles the MSL shader at runtime via newLibraryWithSource (metal.rs:84-99, SHADER_SOURCE include_str! at :35), so a shader compile failure yields Err from try_init and every Metal test silently passes green.

(4) Combined with the orchestrator ground truth that vulkan/cuda/webgpu features cannot even compile, the three `len() < 2` cross-backend parity tests (1549/1698/1755) can never execute on ANY machine — at most one backend (Metal) can exist — so the README's "cross-backend parity tests ... ensure all backends produce identical physics" (README.md:131) describes a capability that is structurally untestable.

Minor corrections to the finding's framing: the cited guard line list omits the len<2 guard at 1549 (count of 16 is still right); 13 of the 14 Metal tests use `.ok()` while the 14th uses `let Ok(..) else { return }`; and "standard practice ... never to silently pass" overstates ecosystem uniformity (early-return on missing GPU hardware is a common, if criticized, Rust pattern — wgpu uses a custom harness for skip reporting). None of this weakens the core point: under the README's own quoted command the no-op is compile-time guaranteed, not hardware-dependent, and these tests are counted in the advertised "978 passing".
verdict.correction: Accurate as stated, with three small detail fixes: (a) the 16 init_all_backends-guarded tests comprise 13 `is_empty()` guards plus THREE `len() < 2` guards (1549, 1698, 1755 — line 1549 was omitted from the cited list); (b) 13 of the 14 Metal tests swallow errors via `try_metal()`'s `.ok()`, the 14th (tests.rs:1613-1615) via `let Ok(..) = crate::try_init(..) else { return; }` — same effect; (c) silent early-return on missing GPU hardware is a known Rust-ecosystem pattern rather than universally condemned, but here the no-op is unconditional at compile time under the README-quoted `cargo test --workspace`, and the tests are marketed as "cross-backend physics" and "benchmarks" within the "978 passing" claim, which is the genuine honesty defect.

finding.title: No test in the workspace asserts that fajr_time or isha_time is ever produced — every end-to-end prayer-time assertion is wrapped in an if-let that vacuously passes on None
finding.evidence: pipeline.rs:971-977: "if let Some(dep) = output.fajr_depression_deg {\n            assert!(\n                dep > 12.0 && dep < 18.0, ...". pipeline.rs:995: "if let (Some(fajr), Some(sunrise)) = (output.fajr_time, output.sunrise_time) {". compute_prayer_times_mecca_produces_results (910-952) asserts only sunrise_time/sunset_time .is_some() and !persistent_twilight; grep across the workspace finds no `fajr_time.is_some()` or `isha_time.is_some()` assertion anywhere.
finding.why_wrong: The project's entire purpose is computing Fajr/Isha. If the radiance pipeline regressed so the threshold crossing is never found (fajr_time = None for Mecca at equinox — a non-polar, must-succeed case), the full "pipeline end-to-end (Mecca, London)" suite advertised in the README would stay green. The headline physics check (depression 12-18 deg, the "~15 deg" claim in the README) is likewise unenforced: it only runs if the value happens to exist. This is the canonical conditional-assertion anti-pattern; the load-bearing capability has zero enforced coverage.
finding.recommendation: In the Mecca/London tests, replace if-let guards with `let fajr = output.fajr_time.expect("Fajr must be found at Mecca equinox");` and assert the depression band unconditionally. Add at least one pinned regression value (date, lat/lon -> expected Fajr time +/- tolerance).

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading /Users/mostafamahdi/twilight/crates/twilight-cpu/src/pipeline.rs lines 900-1121 and grepping the whole workspace. (1) fajr_time appears in test code exactly once, at pipeline.rs:995, wrapped in `if let (Some(fajr), Some(sunrise))` — vacuously passing when None. (2) isha_abyad_time appears in tests only at pipeline.rs:1020, also if-let wrapped; isha_ahmar_time has zero test references. (3) The 12-18 deg depression check at pipeline.rs:971-977 is inside `if let Some(dep) = output.fajr_depression_deg`, so the README's "~15 deg" claim is unenforced. (4) compute_prayer_times_mecca_produces_results (910-952) hard-asserts only sunrise_time/sunset_time is_some and !persistent_twilight — all from SPA solar geometry, not the radiance pipeline — despite its own comment "should produce valid Fajr and Isha times". The London test (1077-1097) is the same. compute_prayer_times_has_spectral_data only checks vectors are non-empty, which survives arbitrarily wrong radiance magnitudes. (5) The sole positive crossing assertion in the workspace is isha_abyad_sza_deg.is_some() at twilight-threshold/src/threshold.rs:500, fed by a hand-built synthetic exponential luminance curve — unit-level threshold-interpolation coverage, not pipeline output; even there the Fajr positive case (threshold.rs:593) is if-let wrapped, and fajr_sza_deg is only ever asserted .is_none(). (6) README line 232 advertises "pipeline end-to-end (Mecca, London)" under the 978-test badge. So a regression yielding fajr_time = None for Mecca at equinox would keep the suite green. The finding's facts and reasoning are exactly right.

reviewed.summary: The CPU physics stack (twilight-core/solar/data/threshold/cpu) is substantially real code with a large genuinely-passing test suite (394 tests pass in twilight-core alone; ~1072 runnable tests workspace-wide), but the project is wrapped in a layer of fabricated marketing: 3 of the 4 advertised GPU backends (~2,400 lines of Vulkan/CUDA/WebGPU host code) reference shader files that do not exist and cannot compile, the README perf table is refuted by direct measurement on the very M2 Pro it cites (single-scatter 7x slower than claimed, hybrid 19x faster, GPU batch ~440x slower end-to-end), a flagship documented flag (--polarized) does not exist, and the 'cross-backend parity' tests are structurally guaranteed no-ops. Slop ratio: roughly 25-30% of the GPU crate is dead/uncompilable fabrication and most external claims (badges, perf, parity, FFI) are unreliable, while the core RT/solar/threshold code and its tests are largely legitimate. Five worst offenders: (1) ghost Vulkan/CUDA/WebGPU backends, (2) the M2 Pro performance table, (3) cross-backend parity claims backed by tests that silently return, (4) the nonexistent --polarized flag in the README quick start, (5) the 'exp-multiplication transmittance split' precision claim that the Metal shader explicitly does the opposite of.

allFindings.title: Vulkan, CUDA, and WebGPU backends are fabricated: ~2,400 lines of host code for shader files that do not exist
allFindings.evidence: vulkan.rs:50: `const SPV_SINGLE_SCATTER: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../shaders/single_scatter.spv");` ... cuda.rs:25: `const CUDA_SOURCE: &str = include_str!("../shaders/twilight.cu");` ... wgpu_backend.rs:16: `const WGSL_SOURCE: &str = include_str!("../shaders/twilight.wgsl");` — `find crates -name "*.comp" -o -name "build.rs" -o -name "*.wgsl" -o -name "*.cu" -o -name "*.spv"` returns nothing; shaders/ contains only twilight.metal. vulkan.rs:43 even documents a phantom GLSL source: "Must match HYBRID_THREADGROUP_SIZE in twilight.comp".
allFindings.why_wrong: include_bytes!/include_str! of missing files is a compile error, so --features vulkan/cuda/webgpu cannot build (confirmed by orchestrator). Yet README.md:8 badges "GPU-Metal | Vulkan | CUDA | WebGPU", README.md:140 claims "Each backend has hand-written shaders tuned for its native GPU API", the table at README.md:142-155 fabricates per-backend intrinsic details for nonexistent shaders ("subgroupAdd", "__shfl_down_sync"), and README.md:251 checks off "[x] GPU backends (Metal, Vulkan, CUDA, wgpu) with cross-backend parity". There is no build pipeline (no build.rs, no glslc invocation) that could ever have produced the .spv files — this is capability presented as shipped that never existed in this tree.
allFindings.recommendation: Either commit the actual .cu/.wgsl/GLSL sources plus a build script and make the features compile, or delete cuda.rs/vulkan.rs/wgpu_backend.rs and rewrite the README/badges to say Metal-only. Add `cargo build --features vulkan,cuda,webgpu` to CI so uncompilable features can never be advertised again.

allFindings.title: "Cross-backend parity" tests are structurally guaranteed no-ops; Metal tests silently skip without a device
allFindings.evidence: tests.rs:1548-1551: `let mut backends = init_all_backends(); if backends.len() < 2 { // Need at least 2 backends to compare\n return; }` and tests.rs:618: `let Some(gpu) = try_metal() else { return };` — while README.md:131 claims "Cross-backend parity tests with CPU f64 oracle ensure all backends produce identical physics" and README.md:231 advertises "Metal + Vulkan parity, cross-backend physics, 11 parity tests".
allFindings.why_wrong: Since only the Metal backend can compile (the other three reference missing shader files), `init_all_backends()` can never return 2 backends on any machine in existence, so cross_backend_single_scatter_parity, cross_backend_mcrt_sign_agreement, cross_backend_deep_night_all_agree_zero, and cross_backend_physics_monotonicity_all_agree always pass as empty functions. The same silent-skip pattern means every Metal integration/benchmark test reports "ok" on CI machines with no GPU. Tests that cannot fail provide zero evidence; counting them in "978 tests passing" is misleading. Standard practice (e.g. libRadtran/DISORT validation suites, or Rust's #[ignore] convention) is to mark unavailable-hardware tests as ignored/skipped, not green.
allFindings.recommendation: Convert silent `return`s to `#[ignore]` plus an explicit runtime skip message, or panic when a GPU is expected (env-gated). Remove the vulkan/cuda/webgpu parity claims from the README until a second backend actually compiles.

allFindings.title: README performance table is refuted by direct measurement on the same M2 Pro hardware it cites; no benchmark harness exists
allFindings.evidence: README.md:181-183: "Single-scatter, 1 SZA | ~32 ms | CPU baseline", "Single-scatter batch, 50 SZA | ~8.4 ms GPU | 2.5x faster than serial", "Hybrid, 100 photons, 1 SZA | ~8.9 s | CPU, rayon parallel, 843% utilization". Measured on this machine (sysctl: "Apple M2 Pro", release build): single-scatter 1 SZA --cpu = "Simulation completed in 219.43ms"; hybrid 100 photons --cpu = 398ms (SZA 95) / 477ms (SZA 105); 51-SZA GPU scan = "Simulation completed in 3.72s".
allFindings.why_wrong: The repo has no benchmark harness at all (no criterion/bencher dependency, no benches/ directory, zero #[bench]) — the only timing code is inside silently-skipped GPU tests (tests.rs:810-873 metal_batch_speedup, which asserts only `speedup > 0.8`). On the exact hardware named, the claimed CPU single-scatter is ~7x faster than reality, the claimed hybrid time is ~19x slower than reality, and the end-to-end 50-SZA GPU scan is seconds, not 8.4 ms (the 8.4 ms could only describe the bare scan_batch call on the small oracle test atmosphere, not the pipeline a user runs). "843% utilization" appears nowhere in any measurement code (grep "utilization" matches nothing in crates). These are stale or invented one-off anecdotes formatted as a benchmark table.
allFindings.recommendation: Delete the perf table or regenerate it from a committed criterion benchmark with the exact command lines and what is included in each timing (atmosphere build vs dispatch). Never state utilization percentages without a reproducible source.

allFindings.title: README documents a --polarized flag that does not exist; the documented command errors out
allFindings.evidence: README.md:91-93: `./target/release/twilight-cli mcrt ... --scattering hybrid --polarized` and README.md:121: "full Stokes vector polarized RT ... toggled via `--polarized` flag". Running it: `error: unexpected argument '--polarized' found`. The real CLI has the inverse flag: main.rs:648 `let polarized = !fast;` (`--fast` per `--help`).
allFindings.why_wrong: A quick-start command in the README was never executed before being committed — the toggle is actually `--fast` (polarization ON by default). Additionally, on the GPU path the flag is admitted to be a no-op: twilight-gpu/src/lib.rs:154-155 "NOTE: GPU shaders currently always run Stokes internally. This flag is reserved for a future scalar shader path optimization", while the CLI help still promises "Use --fast for ~10% speedup". The polarization physics itself is implemented (Stokes/Mueller code exists in twilight.metal:418-520 and twilight-core), but the documented interface is fabricated.
allFindings.recommendation: Fix the README to use --fast (or add a real --polarized/--no-polarized pair), and either implement the scalar GPU path or remove the speedup promise from the --fast help text when GPU is active.

allFindings.title: "tests-978_passing" badge is a hardcoded shields badge with no CI behind it, and disagrees with both the README's own table (991) and the actual count (~1072)
allFindings.evidence: README.md:6: `img.shields.io/badge/tests-978_passing-brightgreen` linking to github.com/Muno459/twilight/actions — but `.github/` does not exist in the repo (no workflows). README.md:225: "978 tests, ~14 seconds", yet the per-crate table at README.md:229-237 sums to 991 (311+153+139+82+73+72+69+47+45). Actual `cargo test --workspace -- --list` counts 1072 tests; per-crate: twilight-core 394 (claimed 311), twilight-data 154 (claimed 153), twilight-gpu 134 with metal (claimed 139), twilight-cpu 75 (claimed 82).
allFindings.why_wrong: Three mutually inconsistent numbers (978 badge, 991 table sum, ~1072 actual) prove none of them was ever generated from a real test run, and a static shields badge styled as a CI status badge is decorative fabrication. Mitigating: the real count is higher than claimed, and the suite genuinely passes where verified (twilight-core: "394 passed; 0 failed"). Note also ~139 of the GPU tests pass vacuously on machines without a Metal device (see parity-tests-noop).
