allFindings.recommendation: Add a real GitHub Actions workflow and use its badge, or drop the badge. Regenerate the test-count table from `cargo test` output, and footnote which tests skip without GPU hardware.

allFindings.title: README precision-engineering claim #5 (exp-multiplication transmittance split) is contradicted by the shader, which deliberately does the opposite
allFindings.evidence: README.md:170: "Exp-multiplication transmittance split. Instead of `exp(-(tau + delta))` ... the shaders compute `exp(-tau) * exp(-delta)`" (also a checked row for all 4 backends in the feature table at README.md:148). The shader: twilight.metal:966 "// Single exp(-(tau + half_step)) is both faster and more precise" then `float t_obs = exp(-(tau_obs.result() + op.extinction * ds * 0.5f));`, and twilight.metal:2022-2025 "// exp(a)*exp(b) = exp(a+b), but the product loses precision when both are small" + `t_obs = exp(-(tau_obs + my_op.extinction * ds * 0.5f));`. tests.rs:39-41 doubles down: "Confirmed: ... Kahan compensated summation (sum+comp), and exp-multiplication split all applied."
allFindings.why_wrong: Grepping every `exp(` in twilight.metal shows no multiplied-exponential transmittance anywhere; the code comments explicitly argue the single-exp form is superior (which is the correct numerical judgment — splitting exp adds a rounding step and helps nothing in f32). So the README and the tests.rs tolerance-derivation comment describe an optimization that was either never implemented or was removed, and the "Confirmed: ... all applied" provenance note is false. This is documentation fabricated independently of the code.
allFindings.recommendation: Delete claim #5 from the README and fix the tests.rs comment to describe what the shader actually does (single fused exponent, which is fine).

allFindings.title: ~255 lines of dead v1 hybrid kernels in the Metal shader, plus a v2 header comment that lies about a tau_prefix buffer
allFindings.evidence: metal.rs:103-106 creates pipelines only for "single_scatter_spectrum", "mcrt_trace_photon", "hybrid_scatter_v2", "garstang_zenith" — kernels `hybrid_scatter` (twilight.metal:1657) and `hybrid_los_prefix` (twilight.metal:1855) are never instantiated by any host. The hybrid_scatter_v2 header claims "Buffer 3 (tau_prefix) is precomputed by hybrid_los_prefix and reused across split-dispatch chunks", but the v2 signature has only buffers 0-2 and instead recomputes tau in an O(steps^2) loop (`for (uint j = 0; j < step_idx; j++)`, twilight.metal:2009). Also a dangling transcript note at 2113-2118: "// Debug: track how many non-finite chain values were dropped // (Remove after debugging)" with no code attached.
allFindings.why_wrong: Git history ("Use v1 kernel for hybrid_scatter dispatch (v2 NaN under investigation)", "fix v2 pipeline name") shows v1 was superseded but never deleted. Dead kernels still compile at runtime (newLibraryWithSource compiles the whole MSL source), wasting init time and inviting drift; the v2 doc-comment describes an architecture (prefix-scan buffer) that was abandoned, so anyone reading it will misunderstand the actual O(N^2) tau recomputation cost.
allFindings.recommendation: Delete hybrid_scatter (v1) and hybrid_los_prefix, or re-wire the prefix buffer as the comment claims; fix the v2 header to match the real buffer list; remove the 'Remove after debugging' remnant.

allFindings.title: Voigt function named/documented as "Weideman (1994)" and "Humlicek w4" but implements neither; derivation comments are chat-transcript style
allFindings.evidence: Line 359-364: "/// Weideman (1994) N=32 approximation for the Faddeeva function. /// w(z) = (L + i*z)/(L^2 + z^2) * sum + corrections /// Actually uses the simpler approach: transform to w(z) via the Laplace continued fraction". Line 315-317: "Humlicek's region 2 formula uses: w = t1 / (0.5625 + t) ... Let me use the known 2-term rational approximation." — followed by an asymptotic series, not a rational approximation. Line 341: "Humlicek's w4 Region 3" — followed by `return weideman_voigt(x, y);` which is the continued fraction. Line 511: "// Actually let's use the standard formula more carefully:".
allFindings.why_wrong: The function `weideman_voigt` does not implement Weideman (1994)'s rational expansion (J. Atmos. Sci. 51, 1146) nor Humlicek (1982)'s w4 regions (JQSRT 27, 437); it implements the Laplace/Gauss continued fraction with backward recurrence — a legitimate but different algorithm (it is the classic CF whose poor small-|z| convergence is the reason Humlicek/Weideman exist; here it compensates with up to 80 terms and a y<1e-6 Gaussian guard). The doc comment self-corrects mid-sentence ("Actually uses the simpler approach"), and "Let me use..." is an LLM working-aloud artifact left in shipped physics code. README.md:119 then advertises "HITRAN line-by-line Voigt" on this misattributed foundation. Misattributed citations in a scientific code erode trust in every other citation (Bodhaine 1999, Serdyuchenko 2014, ...).
allFindings.recommendation: Rename to laplace_cf_voigt (or implement actual Weideman/Humlicek), rewrite the comments to describe the implemented algorithm and its accuracy domain, and strip all "Let me/Actually let's" transcript phrasing. Add a reference-value test against known w(z) tabulations (e.g., Zaghloul & Ali 2011 test points).

allFindings.title: twilight-ffi is a 45-line single-function stub but is presented as the iOS/Android/Flutter integration layer
allFindings.evidence: The entire crate is one function: `pub extern "C" fn twilight_solar_zenith(...) -> f64` wrapping spa::solar_position. README.md:217: "twilight-ffi | C FFI. `cdylib` + `staticlib` for iOS/Android/Flutter." and README.md:202: "twilight-ffi/ C FFI for iOS/Android/Flutter". README.md:220: "Same physics code runs on a phone, in a browser, or on a GPU."
allFindings.why_wrong: No prayer-time, atmosphere, or radiance computation is exposed over FFI — only a solar zenith angle, which any SPA library provides. A mobile app cannot obtain Fajr/Isha through this interface, so the crate table's implication of a working mobile bridge (and the "runs on a phone" line) overstates a placeholder. (The roadmap's unchecked "Mobile SDKs (iOS/Android), WASM demo" is honest; the crate table is not.)
allFindings.recommendation: Mark twilight-ffi as a stub in the README crate table, or expose the actual pipeline (twilight_compute_prayer_times) over FFI.

allFindings.title: Solar/vision LUTs packed and uploaded to GPU at init in all four backends but never bound by any kernel ("reserved for Phase 11f")
allFindings.evidence: metal.rs:58-63: "// Solar and vision LUTs uploaded at init. Reserved for spectral weighting // kernels in Phase 11f pipeline integration. #[allow(dead_code)] buf_solar ... #[allow(dead_code)] buf_vision" — the identical comment is copy-pasted into vulkan.rs, cuda.rs and wgpu_backend.rs. metal.rs:109-113 actually packs and allocates the buffers (`PackedSolarSpectrum::pack(); PackedVisionLuts::pack(); create_buffer_from_f32(...)`) on every init.
allFindings.why_wrong: No shader kernel ever binds these buffers (grep of twilight.metal kernel signatures: only atm/params/output/sources/config). Allocating and filling GPU memory for a phase of an internal AI project plan ("Phase 11a/11f/11g" numbering also leaks into lib.rs:440 "stubs for Phase 11a" — a stale header above fully-implemented init functions — and tests.rs:9) is dead weight quadruplicated by copy-paste, the signature pattern of generated scaffolding.
allFindings.recommendation: Delete buf_solar/buf_vision and their packing until a kernel consumes them; purge "Phase 11x" references or move the plan to an issue tracker.

allFindings.title: garstang_zenith GPU kernel and GpuConfig.polarized are implemented-but-unwired capabilities
allFindings.evidence: lib.rs:276-280 defines `fn garstang_zenith(&self, ...) -> Result<f64, GpuError>` on the GpuBackend trait and twilight.metal:2163 implements it, but grep shows zero callers outside twilight-gpu — the CLI/pipeline light-pollution path uses CPU `twilight_skyglow::quick_estimate_at_angle` (main.rs:1028). lib.rs:154-156: "NOTE: GPU shaders currently always run Stokes internally. This flag is reserved for a future scalar shader path optimization. pub polarized: bool".
allFindings.why_wrong: A whole GPU kernel plus host dispatch (metal.rs pso_garstang, dispatch path, buffer packing PackedLightSource) exists purely to be exercised by its own tests; the product never calls it. Together with the admitted no-op polarized flag, this inflates the apparent GPU surface area ("Four ... kernels" per wgpu_backend.rs:3) beyond what the application uses.
allFindings.recommendation: Either route the skyglow estimate through the GPU kernel when a backend is active, or delete the kernel and trait method; implement or remove the scalar GPU path for `polarized: false`.

allFindings.title: Miscellaneous slop: empty twilight-clouds crate husk, stale TODO contradicting adjacent code, working-notes comments
allFindings.evidence: `crates/twilight-clouds/` contains only an empty `src/` directory and is absent from the workspace Cargo.toml. main.rs:699-701: "// TODO: GPU dispatch currently sends one SZA at a time synchronously. Batching all SZA points into a single dispatch would significantly improve GPU throughput" — yet 35 lines below (main.rs:734) the code calls `simulate_twilight_scan_gpu` which uses the batched `scan_batch` (gpu_dispatch.rs:115), so the TODO describes a solved problem. main.rs:1566-1568: "// If we scale by 2.0 / max_val, then max value becomes 2.0. Reinhard: 2.0 / 3.0 = 0.66. ... Let's scale by 5.0 / max_val so max is 5.0." scattering.rs:1206: "// Our HG Mueller approximation is diagonal".
allFindings.why_wrong: An empty crate directory is abandoned scaffolding; a TODO that contradicts the line below it will mislead contributors about whether batching exists (it does); first-person deliberation comments ("Let's scale...", "Our HG...", "We'll parse..." in geotiff.rs:184-197) are LLM session residue rather than documentation. Individually trivial, collectively they mark unreviewed generated code.
allFindings.recommendation: rm -r crates/twilight-clouds; delete or update the stale TODO at main.rs:699; rewrite deliberation comments as declarative documentation.

finding.title: Vulkan, CUDA, and WebGPU backends are fabricated: ~2,400 lines of host code for shader files that do not exist
finding.evidence: vulkan.rs:50: `const SPV_SINGLE_SCATTER: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../shaders/single_scatter.spv");` ... cuda.rs:25: `const CUDA_SOURCE: &str = include_str!("../shaders/twilight.cu");` ... wgpu_backend.rs:16: `const WGSL_SOURCE: &str = include_str!("../shaders/twilight.wgsl");` — `find crates -name "*.comp" -o -name "build.rs" -o -name "*.wgsl" -o -name "*.cu" -o -name "*.spv"` returns nothing; shaders/ contains only twilight.metal. vulkan.rs:43 even documents a phantom GLSL source: "Must match HYBRID_THREADGROUP_SIZE in twilight.comp".
finding.why_wrong: include_bytes!/include_str! of missing files is a compile error, so --features vulkan/cuda/webgpu cannot build (confirmed by orchestrator). Yet README.md:8 badges "GPU-Metal | Vulkan | CUDA | WebGPU", README.md:140 claims "Each backend has hand-written shaders tuned for its native GPU API", the table at README.md:142-155 fabricates per-backend intrinsic details for nonexistent shaders ("subgroupAdd", "__shfl_down_sync"), and README.md:251 checks off "[x] GPU backends (Metal, Vulkan, CUDA, wgpu) with cross-backend parity". There is no build pipeline (no build.rs, no glslc invocation) that could ever have produced the .spv files — this is capability presented as shipped that never existed in this tree.
finding.recommendation: Either commit the actual .cu/.wgsl/GLSL sources plus a build script and make the features compile, or delete cuda.rs/vulkan.rs/wgpu_backend.rs and rewrite the README/badges to say Metal-only. Add `cargo build --features vulkan,cuda,webgpu` to CI so uncompilable features can never be advertised again.

verdict.reasoning: Read all three cited files myself. vulkan.rs:50-53 contains four include_bytes! directives for single_scatter.spv, mcrt_trace.spv, hybrid_scatter.spv, garstang_zenith.spv; cuda.rs:25 has include_str!("../shaders/twilight.cu"); wgpu_backend.rs:16 has include_str!("../shaders/twilight.wgsl"). crates/twilight-gpu/shaders/ contains only twilight.metal. A tree-wide find returns zero build.rs, .spv, .cu, .wgsl, or .comp files; there are no Makefiles, scripts, or CI workflows, and .gitignore does not exclude shader artifacts, so the missing files are not untracked build products — no pipeline in this tree could ever have produced them. include_bytes!/include_str! of a missing file is a hard compile error, matching the orchestrator-confirmed build failures for --features vulkan/cuda/webgpu. vulkan.rs:43-44 indeed references a phantom "twilight.comp". The three host files total 2,388 lines (~2,400 as claimed). README fabrication verified: line 8 badge "GPU-Metal | Vulkan | CUDA | WebGPU"; line 19 "GPU-accelerated on Metal, Vulkan, CUDA, and WebGPU"; line 140 "Each backend has hand-written shaders tuned for its native GPU API"; table at 142-155 lists per-backend intrinsics (subgroupAdd, __shfl_down_sync) for nonexistent shaders; line 231 claims "Metal + Vulkan parity ... 11 parity tests"; line 251 checks off "[x] GPU backends (Metal, Vulkan, CUDA, wgpu) with cross-backend parity". Only mitigating nuance: these backends are behind non-default cargo features (Cargo.toml:10-13, lib.rs:29-37), so the default build passes — but that does not refute the fabrication: capability is presented as shipped and parity-tested when it cannot even compile. Severity rubric explicitly classifies "fabricated capability presented as real" and "won't compile" as critical.

finding.title: "Cross-backend parity" tests are structurally guaranteed no-ops; Metal tests silently skip without a device
finding.evidence: tests.rs:1548-1551: `let mut backends = init_all_backends(); if backends.len() < 2 { // Need at least 2 backends to compare\n return; }` and tests.rs:618: `let Some(gpu) = try_metal() else { return };` — while README.md:131 claims "Cross-backend parity tests with CPU f64 oracle ensure all backends produce identical physics" and README.md:231 advertises "Metal + Vulkan parity, cross-backend physics, 11 parity tests".
finding.why_wrong: Since only the Metal backend can compile (the other three reference missing shader files), `init_all_backends()` can never return 2 backends on any machine in existence, so cross_backend_single_scatter_parity, cross_backend_mcrt_sign_agreement, cross_backend_deep_night_all_agree_zero, and cross_backend_physics_monotonicity_all_agree always pass as empty functions. The same silent-skip pattern means every Metal integration/benchmark test reports "ok" on CI machines with no GPU. Tests that cannot fail provide zero evidence; counting them in "978 tests passing" is misleading. Standard practice (e.g. libRadtran/DISORT validation suites, or Rust's #[ignore] convention) is to mark unavailable-hardware tests as ignored/skipped, not green.
finding.recommendation: Convert silent `return`s to `#[ignore]` plus an explicit runtime skip message, or panic when a GPU is expected (env-gated). Remove the vulkan/cuda/webgpu parity claims from the README until a second backend actually compiles.

verdict.reasoning: Read tests.rs myself. Lines 1548-1551 contain exactly the quoted guard `if backends.len() < 2 { return; }`; the same guard is in cross_backend_mcrt_sign_agreement (1698) and cross_backend_deep_night_all_agree_zero (1755). init_all_backends() (1493-1541) only adds backends behind feature cfgs, and per established ground truth only the Metal feature compiles, so it can never return 2 backends — those three cross-backend tests are empty passes on every machine in every configuration. The Metal silent-skip is real: `let Some(gpu) = try_metal() else { return };` appears at line 617 (finding cited 618, trivial off-by-one) and 13 more sites. README:131 and README:231 claims are verbatim as quoted and contradicted by the code (Vulkan parity cannot even compile). The finding actually UNDERSTATES the problem: twilight-gpu/Cargo.toml:9 has `default = []`, so the default `cargo test --workspace` run that README:225 credits with "978 tests" compiles NO backend at all — all 16 tests calling init_all_backends() (guards at 1549-3548) pass as no-ops and the layer4_metal module isn't compiled. Also, the README's GitHub Actions badge claims 978 passing but .github/workflows/ does not exist. Two minor caveats that don't change the verdict: (1) cross_backend_physics_monotonicity_all_agree (1784) uses `is_empty()` not `len() < 2`, so with --features metal on a GPU Mac it does run per-backend monotonicity assertions — though it never performs any cross-backend comparison despite its name, and it is still a no-op in the default-feature run; (2) the "11 parity tests" (test_parity_* at 2401-3037) are mostly genuine CPU-side tests of the crate::parity Rust port of shader logic and do execute without a GPU, but they validate a re-implementation rather than the shaders, and test_parity_hybrid_single_scatter_component (2849) is itself an is_empty() no-op without a GPU. The convention argument is sound: Rust's #[ignore] reports hardware-unavailable tests as ignored, not green.
verdict.correction: Accurate as stated, with two refinements: (a) cross_backend_physics_monotonicity_all_agree uses an is_empty() guard, so it can execute single-backend monotonicity checks on a Metal machine with --features metal (its cross-backend aspect still never executes); (b) the situation is worse than described in the default configuration: twilight-gpu's default features are empty, so the `cargo test --workspace` run behind the "978 tests passing" badge compiles zero GPU backends, making every init_all_backends-based test a guaranteed no-op and excluding the Metal module entirely — and the Actions badge points to a .github/workflows directory that does not exist.

finding.title: README performance table is refuted by direct measurement on the same M2 Pro hardware it cites; no benchmark harness exists
finding.evidence: README.md:181-183: "Single-scatter, 1 SZA | ~32 ms | CPU baseline", "Single-scatter batch, 50 SZA | ~8.4 ms GPU | 2.5x faster than serial", "Hybrid, 100 photons, 1 SZA | ~8.9 s | CPU, rayon parallel, 843% utilization". Measured on this machine (sysctl: "Apple M2 Pro", release build): single-scatter 1 SZA --cpu = "Simulation completed in 219.43ms"; hybrid 100 photons --cpu = 398ms (SZA 95) / 477ms (SZA 105); 51-SZA GPU scan = "Simulation completed in 3.72s".
finding.why_wrong: The repo has no benchmark harness at all (no criterion/bencher dependency, no benches/ directory, zero #[bench]) — the only timing code is inside silently-skipped GPU tests (tests.rs:810-873 metal_batch_speedup, which asserts only `speedup > 0.8`). On the exact hardware named, the claimed CPU single-scatter is ~7x faster than reality, the claimed hybrid time is ~19x slower than reality, and the end-to-end 50-SZA GPU scan is seconds, not 8.4 ms (the 8.4 ms could only describe the bare scan_batch call on the small oracle test atmosphere, not the pipeline a user runs). "843% utilization" appears nowhere in any measurement code (grep "utilization" matches nothing in crates). These are stale or invented one-off anecdotes formatted as a benchmark table.
finding.recommendation: Delete the perf table or regenerate it from a committed criterion benchmark with the exact command lines and what is included in each timing (atmosphere build vs dispatch). Never state utilization percentages without a reproducible source.

verdict.reasoning: The core finding is real: I read README.md:21 and 177-185 (table present exactly as quoted, attributed to "M2 Pro, release build"), confirmed there is no benchmark harness (grep: no criterion/bencher in any Cargo.toml, no benches/ dir, zero #[bench]), confirmed "843"/"utilization" appears in no measurement code (only gas cross-section data and an unrelated shader comment), and confirmed the only timing code is tests.rs:810-873 metal_batch_speedup, which is behind the NON-default `metal` feature (twilight-gpu Cargo.toml: default = []), silently skips via try_metal(), and asserts only speedup > 0.8. Running it on this M2 Pro prints "serial 20.8ms vs batch 11.4ms (1.8x speedup)" — confirming the reviewer's hypothesis that "~8.4 ms / 2.5x" describes the bare scan_batch micro-test on the oracle atmosphere ("serial" = serial GPU dispatches, not CPU), with 2.5x lifted from the optimistic end of a code comment ("1.2-2.5x"). HOWEVER, the reviewer's own counter-measurements are substantially wrong because they ran the wrong scattering mode: (1) their "single-scatter 1 SZA --cpu = 219.43 ms" is impossible for single-scatter mode — I measured 0.29-0.47 ms (sim timer; ~15 ms whole-process wall) with `--scattering single --cpu`; 219 ms matches the DEFAULT hybrid mode (I got 149 ms at SZA 96, 316 ms at SZA 105). So their claim "the claimed CPU single-scatter is ~7x faster than reality" is backwards — the README's 32 ms is ~100x SLOWER than current reality. (2) Their "51-SZA GPU scan = 3.72 s" was also default hybrid mode (I reproduced 3.43 s with defaults); the single-scatter 51-SZA GPU scan the table row describes is 57-65 ms end-to-end. (3) Their hybrid direction was right: README's ~8.9 s vs my 149-316 ms is ~30-60x stale (roadmap line 256 even notes "hybrid reparallelization"). Net: every table row fails to match current code on the named hardware, but mostly in the self-deprecating (stale) direction, and the genuinely misleading element is narrower than claimed — the GPU row presents an internal micro-test as pipeline performance while end-to-end CPU (14 ms for 51 SZA) actually beats the GPU (57-65 ms) for that workload, and zsh `time` prints figures like "745% cpu", so "843% utilization" is plausibly a stale one-off shell anecdote rather than pure invention.
verdict.correction: The README performance table (README.md:177-185) is stale and unreproducible rather than refuted in the direction the reviewer claims. Measured on the same M2 Pro (release, current code): single-scatter 1 SZA CPU = 0.3-0.5 ms simulation time (README's ~32 ms is ~100x slower than reality, not 7x faster); hybrid 100 photons 1 SZA CPU = 149-316 ms (README's ~8.9 s is ~30-60x stale); the 51-SZA single-scatter GPU scan = 57-65 ms end-to-end (not seconds — the reviewer's 3.72 s came from running default hybrid mode, not the mode the row describes). The "~8.4 ms GPU / 2.5x faster than serial" row describes the bare scan_batch micro-test on the small oracle atmosphere (tests.rs:810-873; today it prints 11.4 ms, 1.8x), where "serial" means serial GPU dispatches — and end-to-end the CPU (14 ms) actually beats the GPU (57-65 ms) for this batch, contradicting the table's implied GPU advantage. Confirmed: no benchmark harness exists (no criterion/bencher, no benches/, no #[bench]); the only timing code is a feature-gated (default = [], so excluded from `cargo test --workspace`), device-dependent, silently-skipping test asserting only speedup > 0.8; "843% utilization" is generated by no code and is at most a stale shell-`time` anecdote (zsh reports e.g. "745% cpu" for the hybrid run). The table should be regenerated from a real harness or deleted.

finding.title: README documents a --polarized flag that does not exist; the documented command errors out
finding.evidence: README.md:91-93: `./target/release/twilight-cli mcrt ... --scattering hybrid --polarized` and README.md:121: "full Stokes vector polarized RT ... toggled via `--polarized` flag". Running it: `error: unexpected argument '--polarized' found`. The real CLI has the inverse flag: main.rs:648 `let polarized = !fast;` (`--fast` per `--help`).
finding.why_wrong: A quick-start command in the README was never executed before being committed — the toggle is actually `--fast` (polarization ON by default). Additionally, on the GPU path the flag is admitted to be a no-op: twilight-gpu/src/lib.rs:154-155 "NOTE: GPU shaders currently always run Stokes internally. This flag is reserved for a future scalar shader path optimization", while the CLI help still promises "Use --fast for ~10% speedup". The polarization physics itself is implemented (Stokes/Mueller code exists in twilight.metal:418-520 and twilight-core), but the documented interface is fabricated.
finding.recommendation: Fix the README to use --fast (or add a real --polarized/--no-polarized pair), and either implement the scalar GPU path or remove the speedup promise from the --fast help text when GPU is active.

verdict.reasoning: Every factual claim checks out. README.md:90-93 documents `twilight-cli mcrt ... --polarized` and README.md:121 says polarization is "toggled via `--polarized` flag"; I ran the documented command against the built binary and reproduced `error: unexpected argument '--polarized' found`. The real interface is the inverse flag: main.rs:113-117 defines `--fast` and main.rs:648/950 compute `let polarized = !fast;` — polarization is ON by default, which also makes README:90's "(default is scalar for speed)" backwards. The GPU no-op admission is verbatim in twilight-gpu/src/lib.rs (~154-156): "GPU shaders currently always run Stokes internally. This flag is reserved for a future scalar shader path optimization," while CLI help still promises "~10% speedup" from --fast. The underlying physics is genuinely implemented (StokesVector at twilight-core/src/scattering.rs:163, MuellerMatrix at :243, Rayleigh Mueller scattering with tests), so the reviewer correctly scoped this as a fabricated interface rather than a fabricated capability. The only correction is severity: unlike the nonexistent GPU backends, the advertised capability exists and runs by default, the failure is loud (clap hard error, never silently wrong prayer times), computed output is unaffected, and the fix is a one-line doc change. That fits "medium" (quality/accuracy concern), not "high".
verdict.correction: The finding is factually accurate but overstated as high severity. Accurate statement: README.md:90-93 and :121 document a `--polarized` flag that does not exist (the documented quick-start command hard-errors with "unexpected argument '--polarized'"), and README:90 misstates the default as scalar when the CLI default is full Stokes (`let polarized = !fast;`, main.rs:648 — the real toggle is `--fast`). On the GPU path `--fast` is a no-op (twilight-gpu/src/lib.rs ~154-156). However, the polarized RT capability itself is real and runs by default, the error is loud rather than silent, and prayer-time output is unaffected — a documentation/interface bug, severity medium.

libradtran.approach: Three-tier differential validation of twilight against libRadtran 2.0.6, ordered so each tier isolates one block of physics before the next adds complexity. Tier A (no scattering): direct-beam spectral transmittance from twilight's exact shell tracer (shadow_ray_transmittance_spectrum, crates/twilight-core/src/single_scatter.rs:477) vs uvspec `edir` — tests Rayleigh cross sections (Bodhaine 1999 style, crates/twilight-core/src/spectrum.rs:10-42), O3 Chappuis column (~347 DU default, crates/twilight-data/src/builder.rs:408 + gas_absorption.rs:737), NO2/O2/H2O/O4 with zero geometric ambiguity. Tier B (sun above horizon, SZA 60-85°): spectral sky radiance at zenith and along the solar principal plane vs DISORT 32-stream — tests the Rayleigh phase function, surface-albedo coupling (Lambertian albedo/π, single_scatter.rs:243-272), and HG aerosol, where plane-parallel DISORT is a trusted gold standard. Tier C (twilight, SZA 90-108°, the regime that sets Fajr/Isha): spectral radiance vs MYSTIC in fully spherical 1D geometry (`rte_solver montecarlo` + `mc_spherical 1D`, the Emde & Mayer 2007 configuration), the only community-standard solver that is apples-to-apples with twilight's 50-shell spherical MC. Comparisons are done in SUN-NORMALIZED units (radiance/E0, sr^-1) to eliminate the solar-spectrum dependency, and separately in absolute W/m²/sr/nm using twilight's TSIS-1 table exported as the libRadtran `source solar` file (uvspec output units follow the solar-file units, so supplying W/m²/nm makes uu directly comparable to twilight's SpectralResult, simulation.rs:24-33). A final layer feeds the MYSTIC spectra through twilight-threshold's own CIE V(λ)/V'(λ) luminance code so the vision/threshold mapping is validated independently of the RT, and the radiance error is converted into the metric the ummah actually cares about: minutes of Fajr/Isha shift. Key matching facts established by reading the code: twilight's default pipeline does NOT enable refraction (build_clear_sky/build_full never call compute_refractive_indices — confirmed by grep; refractive_index defaults to 1.0, atmosphere.rs:102), so default runs are straight-line transport and match MYSTIC's default (no refraction) — refraction must be compared as a separate twilight-internal A/B, not against libRadtran. Twilight's grid is 41 monochromatic wavelengths 380-780 nm at 10 nm (builder.rs:20-25), Earth radius 6371 km (atmosphere.rs:8), US Standard 1976 profile on 51 levels 0-100 km (builder.rs:30-36), spectrally flat albedo 0.15 default.
comparison_quantities: 1. Direct-beam spectral transmittance T(λ,SZA)=edir/(E0·cos SZA) at SZA∈{60,75,85}, four configs: Rayleigh-only, +O3(347 DU), +NO2, +aerosol. Tests extinction column only (Bodhaine Rayleigh, Chappuis O3, Angstrom AOD scaling) with no scattering geometry — the tightest possible check.

2. Zenith spectral sky radiance I(λ; VZA=0) at SZA∈{60,75,85}, Rayleigh-only with albedo 0.0 and 0.15, vs DISORT 32 streams. Tests single+multiple scattering magnitude and ground-reflection coupling in a regime where DISORT is exact.

3. Principal-plane radiance scan I(λ∈{450,550,650}; VZA −85°..+85°, φ−φ0∈{0°,180°}) at SZA 75°. Tests the Rayleigh phase function shape (twilight currently omits depolarization in the phase function — King factor is in the cross section only) and, in aerosol runs, the Henyey-Greenstein phase with libRadtran forced to the same g via aerosol_modify set gg/ssa/tau550.

4. Twilight spectral radiance I(λ) at zenith AND at VZA 75° toward the solar azimuth (twilight's hard-wired geometry, simulation.rs:127-142) for SZA 90-108° step 2°, clear sky, vs MYSTIC mc_spherical 1D with ≥1e6 photons. This is the money test: spherical shadow geometry, limb transmission of the shadow ray, O3 Chappuis darkening of zenith twilight (the dominant effect on twilight color, Hulburt 1953), and growth of the multiple-scatter fraction with depression angle.

5. Multiple-scatter fraction f_MS(SZA,λ) = (hybrid − single)/hybrid from twilight vs (MYSTIC total − MYSTIC mc_maxscatters 1) if that option is available in the installed build; otherwise vs an independent ~100-line Python single-scatter quadrature run on twilight's dumped per-shell extinction table. Directly tests the MC estimator the maintainer distrusts.

6. MC variance: coefficient of variation of repeated twilight hybrid runs (≥10 seeds) at matched photon budget vs MYSTIC's reported standard deviation (mc_std). Quantifies the 'excessive variance' claim with numbers; twilight already has cv_baseline/cv_deep_diag harnesses (simulation.rs:947, :1025) to reuse.

7. Photopic/scotopic/mesopic luminance L(SZA) computed by twilight-threshold from BOTH spectra (twilight's and MYSTIC's), plus the threshold-crossing SZA* for the Fajr/Isha thresholds. Isolates the CIE vision layer from the RT and yields the end-user error in minutes via dt = ΔSZA*/ (dSZA/dt ≈ 0.15-0.25°/min depending on latitude/season).

8. Polarization delta: twilight default Stokes vs --fast scalar, compared against MYSTIC mc_polarisation 1 vs 0 (Rayleigh scalar-vs-vector radiance errors of 1-5% are documented, Mishchenko et al. 1994) — checks the claimed 0.5-2% correction is real and the right sign.

9. Absolute literature anchors needing no libRadtran: Rayleigh τ(550)≈0.0973/τ(400)≈0.36 (Bodhaine 1999, already unit-tested in spectrum.rs:105-129), IPRT phase-A pure-Rayleigh polarized radiance tables (Emde et al. 2015) for case-level absolute checks, and published zenith twilight luminance curves (Koomen et al. 1952; Patat et al. 2006) for order-of-magnitude sanity of the L(SZA) curve.
libradtran.libradtran_setup:
Three deck templates generated by tools/validate_libradtran.py. Shared files: wl_grid_41.dat (one wavelength per line: 380 390 ... 780, matching builder.rs DEFAULT_WAVELENGTHS_NM) and twilight_tsis1.dat (two columns λ_nm E0 in W/m²/nm dumped verbatim from twilight-data/src/solar_spectrum.rs SOLAR_IRRADIANCE; uvspec output then comes out in W/m²/(nm sr), the same units as twilight's SpectralResult).

--- A) Direct transmittance + plane-parallel radiance reference (SZA ≤ 85°) ---
# disort_sza75.inp
data_files_path  $LIBRADTRAN/data/
atmosphere_file  US-standard          # afglus (Anderson et al. 1986) — same US Std 1976 family as twilight
source solar     ./twilight_tsis1.dat per_nm
mol_modify O3    347. DU              # pin to twilight's default column (builder.rs docstring ~347 DU)
mol_modify NO2   0. DU                # tier-1: gases off except O3; re-enable per phase
no_absorption    mol H2O              # exclude H2O lines; twilight's smooth 10nm xsec can't match lines
crs_model rayleigh Bodhaine           # explicit (also the default) — matches spectrum.rs
albedo           0.15
earth_radius     6371.0               # matches EARTH_RADIUS_M (atmosphere.rs:8)
sza              75.0
phi0             0.0
wavelength       380 780
wavelength_grid_file ./wl_grid_41.dat
rte_solver       disort
number_of_streams 32
pseudospherical
zout             0.0
umu  -0.9999 -0.5 -0.258819           # VZA ~0°, 60°, 75°, ground sensor looking up (umu<0)
phi  0 90 180
output_user      lambda sza edir edn uu
quiet

--- B) Twilight geometry, the apples-to-apples MC case (SZA 90-108°) ---
# mystic_sza100.inp
data_files_path  $LIBRADTRAN/data/
atmosphere_file  US-standard
source solar     ./twilight_tsis1.dat per_nm
mol_modify O3    347. DU
albedo           0.15
earth_radius     6371.0
sza              100.0
phi0             0.0
wavelength_grid_file ./wl_grid_41.dat
rte_solver       montecarlo
mc_spherical     1D                   # fully spherical geometry — required for SZA>90 (Emde & Mayer 2007)
mc_photons       1000000              # raise to 1e7 for SZA>104
mc_polarisation  0                    # phase 1: scalar, compare against twilight --fast
mc_vroom         on                   # variance reduction; essential for HG aerosol runs
mc_std                                # emit standard deviation for the statistical comparison
mc_basename      ./out/mystic_sza100
zout             0.0
umu  -0.9999 -0.258819                # zenith + VZA 75°
phi  0
output_user      lambda uu

--- C) Matched-aerosol variant (append to A or B) ---
aerosol_default                       # activates Shettle profile…
aerosol_modify set tau550 0.20        # …then override to twilight's exact AOD,
aerosol_modify set ssa    0.95        # SSA and asymmetry; 'set gg' forces an HG
aerosol_modify set gg     0.70        # phase function = twilight's HG (scattering.rs)

CONVENTION CHECKS baked into the harness (do not trust memory): (1) libRadtran radiance directions — umu<0 is a ground sensor looking up; the manual defines phi−phi0=0 as sensor looking INTO the sun's azimuth; the harness verifies this empirically by confirming the solar aureole maximum sits at the expected (umu,phi) in a SZA 75° DISORT run before any twilight comparison. (2) For sun-normalized comparisons run a second pass with `output_quantity transmittance`, which returns uu/E0 in sr⁻¹ — directly comparable to twilight with apply_solar_irradiance=false (simulation.rs:157-160).
libradtran.twilight_changes_needed: All hooks are small and additive. (1) New `twilight dump` subcommand in crates/twilight-cli/src/main.rs with three modes: `dump solar-file` (writes SOLAR_WAVELENGTHS_NM/SOLAR_IRRADIANCE as a 2-column libRadtran solar file), `dump atmosphere` (per-shell z_inner/z_outer [km], and per-λ extinction [1/m], ssa, g, rayleigh_fraction, plus albedo — everything in AtmosphereModel.optics — so the Python harness can build matched inputs and run the independent SS integrator), `dump transmittance --sza S1,S2,...` (calls shadow_ray_transmittance_spectrum from the observer toward the sun, single_scatter.rs:477, printing T(λ); this is the Tier-A observable and requires zero new physics). (2) Extend `twilight mcrt` with: `--view-azimuth <deg>` — currently compute_geometry hard-wires the view azimuth to config.solar_azimuth (crates/twilight-cpu/src/simulation.rs:127-142), so only the principal plane is reachable; add view_azimuth to SimulationConfig and thread it through; `--view-zenith` accepting a comma list so one run produces a VZA scan; `--json <path>` emitting the FULL 41-wavelength spectrum per (SZA, VZA, phi) — today cmd_mcrt prints only 5 hand-picked columns (main.rs:761-783) which is useless for machine comparison; `--no-solar` exposing apply_solar_irradiance=false, which exists in SimulationConfig (simulation.rs:69) but is hard-coded true in the CLI (main.rs:692) — this gives sun-normalized radiance in sr⁻¹ matching libRadtran's `output_quantity transmittance`; `--seed <u64>` — currently the RNG seed is derived deterministically from the SZA bits (simulation.rs:216-223 and :265-267), so independent replicates for variance estimation are impossible from the CLI; XOR the user seed into the existing hash. (3) JSON output should also report, for hybrid mode, the single-scatter and MS components separately (the hybrid integrator already computes order 1 deterministically, so this is bookkeeping) — needed for comparison quantity 5. No changes to physics code are required; that is deliberate, so the validation measures the code as it ships.
libradtran.tolerances: Tier A (direct transmittance, no scattering): Rayleigh-only |Δln T| ≤ 0.005 (0.5%) at every λ — twilight uses Peck & Reeder index with a linearized King factor F=1.0480+0.00013(550−λ)/150 (spectrum.rs:28) vs libRadtran's exact Bodhaine tables, worth ~0.1-0.3%; +O3(347 DU pinned): ≤1% for 450-700 nm (residual = O3 xsec dataset differences, twilight's parameterization vs libRadtran's Serdyuchenko/Molina); λ ∈ [700,780] excluded or compared only with H2O/O2 disabled in both, because twilight's smooth pseudo-monochromatic O2/H2O cross sections at a 10 nm grid are not physically comparable to line absorption (O2 A-band 760 nm) under monochromatic uvspec runs. Tier B (DISORT radiance, SZA ≤ 85°): Rayleigh-only ≤2% per λ (covers twilight's 50-shell discretization and 200-step LOS quadrature, single_scatter.rs:28); +O3/NO2 ≤3%; matched-HG aerosol ≤5%. A persistent few-percent uniform offset here would indicate a normalization bug (e.g. 4π factor); a VZA-dependent shape error indicates the phase function — note twilight's rayleigh_phase has no depolarization term, a known ~1.5% shape effect (Chandrasekhar Ch. X), which the plan measures rather than hides. Tier C (MYSTIC spherical, twilight): pass criterion |Δ| ≤ max(tol·I_ref, 3·σ_combined) where σ_combined stacks MYSTIC's mc_std and twilight's seed-to-seed std; tol = 10% for SZA 90-96°, 15% for 96-102°, 25% for 102-108°. These translate to prayer time as follows: measured zenith twilight luminance falls about one decade per 2.2-2.5° of SZA in the nautical/astronomical range (d ln L/dSZA ≈ 0.9-1.05 per degree; consistent with Patat et al. 2006), so a 25% radiance error shifts the threshold-crossing SZA* by ≤0.25°, i.e. ≤1.0-1.7 minutes at dSZA/dt ≈ 0.15-0.25°/min. End-to-end acceptance: |ΔSZA*| ≤ 0.2° (≲1 min) for each Fajr/Isha threshold when MYSTIC spectra are pushed through twilight-threshold. Vision layer in isolation: luminance computed by twilight-threshold from an identical input spectrum must match an independent Python CIE integration to ≤0.5% (pure quadrature, no physics excuse for more).
blockers: libRadtran is source-only (libradtran.org, v2.0.6): needs gfortran/flex/netcdf/GSL on macOS; plan ~half a day or use a prebuilt Docker image and run via container. REPTRAN/spectral data packages are separate downloads (only needed if band-averaged gas comparison is attempted).

MYSTIC availability: 1D MYSTIC and mc_spherical 1D ship in the public libRadtran, but some MYSTIC features (full 3D, some polarization/refraction combinations) are restricted to collaborations with the Mayer group. Must verify `mc_spherical 1D` + `mc_polarisation` and the existence of `mc_maxscatters` in the installed build during step 1; the plan has fallbacks (scalar comparison, independent Python SS integrator) if either is missing.

DISORT is plane-parallel: nothing in Tier B works past SZA≈90°; even `pseudospherical` only stretches to ~92°. All twilight-regime conclusions rest on MYSTIC, so its photon budget (1e6-1e7/λ at SZA 105+ where the shadow kills most paths) is the main compute cost — budget hours, not minutes, for Tier C sweeps.

Solar-spectrum mismatch: libRadtran's default atlas_plus_modtran differs from twilight's 41-point TSIS-1 table by a few percent in places and is in mW/m²/nm; neutralized by exporting twilight's table as the `source solar` file AND by doing primary comparisons sun-normalized (output_quantity transmittance vs --no-solar). Both paths must agree or the harness flags a units bug.

Refraction: twilight's production builder never enables refraction (no call to compute_refractive_indices outside tests), so default comparisons are clean; BUT if refraction is later switched on, libRadtran cannot follow (MYSTIC refraction is not generally available) — refraction validation must then be a twilight-internal A/B against the known ~0.57° horizontal refraction benchmark, not part of this harness.

O2 A-band (760 nm) and H2O (~720 nm): twilight's 10 nm pseudo-monochromatic Voigt-table cross sections (gas_absorption.rs:539,603) are structurally incomparable to monochromatic line-by-line or band-model references; these bands carry little weight in V(λ) luminance, so they are excluded from tight tolerance rather than blocking the plan.
Twilight CLI gaps (no full-spectrum dump, view azimuth hard-wired to solar azimuth, no seed control, solar weighting hard-coded on) block any comparison until the small CLI PR in step 2 lands.
phi/umu sign conventions in uvspec radiance output are an infamous foot-gun; the harness self-checks them with an aureole-position test before trusting any number.
steps: 1. Install libRadtran 2.0.6 (./configure --prefix=$HOME/libRadtran && make -j && make check); run examples/UVSPEC_CLEAR.INP and a MYSTIC example; confirm `mc_spherical 1D` runs at sza 100 and record whether `mc_maxscatters` and `mc_polarisation` are accepted by the installed build.

2. Land the twilight CLI PR: `twilight dump solar-file|atmosphere|transmittance`, and `mcrt --json --no-solar --seed --view-azimuth --view-zenith <list>` as specified above (touches crates/twilight-cli/src/main.rs and crates/twilight-cpu/src/simulation.rs only; no physics changes).

3. Create tools/validate_libradtran.py: scenario matrix in YAML (sza, vza list, phi, gases on/off, aerosol params, solver, photons, tolerance tier) → generates wl_grid_41.dat, twilight_tsis1.dat, uvspec .inp files → runs uvspec and the twilight CLI → parses both into a common (case, sza, vza, phi, lambda, I, sigma) table → emits per-case relative-difference CSV, plots, and a pass/fail report against the tier tolerances. Include the aureole-position convention self-check and the dual absolute/sun-normalized consistency check.

4. Write tools/ss_reference.py (~100 lines): independent single-scatter quadrature over the dumped per-shell atmosphere with exact ray-sphere shell path lengths — a second implementation of single_scatter.rs used to validate twilight's SS integral to <0.5% and to serve as the MS-fraction fallback if mc_maxscatters is unavailable.

5. Run Tier A: `twilight dump transmittance` vs disort edir at SZA 60/75/85 for (a) Rayleigh-only [set 0 DU O3 + no_absorption in uvspec; rebuild twilight atm via build_clear_sky path], (b) +O3 347 DU, (c) +NO2, (d) +aerosol tau550=0.2. Gate: tolerances per Tier A. Any failure here is a cross-section or column bug — fix before proceeding.

6. Run Tier B: disort 32-stream zenith + principal-plane scans at SZA 60/75/85, albedo 0.0 and 0.15, Rayleigh-only then +O3 then matched-HG aerosol; compare twilight --scattering single AND hybrid (hybrid must agree with disort, single must undershoot by the expected MS fraction ~10-30%). Gate: Tier B tolerances; diagnose any uniform offset (normalization) separately from VZA-shaped error (phase function/depolarization).

7. Run Tier C: MYSTIC mc_spherical 1D at SZA 90-108 step 2 (1e6 photons, 1e7 for SZA>104), zenith + VZA 75 principal plane, scalar; twilight hybrid --fast with 10 seeds × the default 100 secondary rays and with 10× rays to test convergence; statistical comparison per the tiered criterion; record twilight CV vs MYSTIC mc_std at matched cost to adjudicate the variance claim; if mc_maxscatters exists, also compare SS/MS decomposition.

8. Vision layer + end-to-end: push MYSTIC spectra through twilight-threshold (small Rust bin or CSV import) to get L(SZA) and threshold-crossing SZA* for each Fajr/Isha criterion; compare with twilight's own SZA*; convert ΔSZA* to minutes for 3 reference sites (Mecca 21°N, mid-lat 48°N, high-lat 56°N); acceptance |ΔSZA*| ≤ 0.2°.

9. If the installed MYSTIC supports mc_polarisation 1: repeat one Tier C SZA sweep polarized vs twilight default Stokes mode; verify the polarization correction magnitude/sign matches the claimed 0.5-2%.

10. Commit harness + scenario YAML + golden CSVs under tools/; wire Tiers A/B (cheap, deterministic) into CI behind a LIBRADTRAN_HOME env guard; document Tier C as a manual weekly job with expected runtimes; write up the first full report including every tolerance breach as a tracked issue.

integration.current_dataflow:
`twilight pray` (crates/twilight-cli/src/main.rs:120-208, cmd_pray at :845) executes this real path:

1. OPTIONAL INPUTS resolved in the CLI, not the pipeline: (a) weather: twilight_weather::fetch_atmospheric_params(lat,lon) (main.rs:897) hits Open-Meteo with `current=` only (twilight-weather/src/api.rs:67,72) — no date/hour parameter; (b) terrain: resolve_source + horizon::compute_horizon (main.rs:972-1014) builds a HorizonProfile; (c) skyglow: bortle_to_radiance + quick_estimate_at_angle(radiance, led_fraction, 10.0) (main.rs:1017-1043) — Falchi power law + canned HPS/LED spectra, NOT the Garstang module.

2. GPU init: try_init_gpu (main.rs:313-352, 1092-1097). twilight-cli/Cargo.toml enables ONLY `twilight-gpu features=["metal"]`; GPU is the default compute, --cpu opts out.

3. pipeline::compute_prayer_times[_gpu] (twilight-cpu/src/pipeline.rs:393, 413): build_atmosphere → twilight_data::builder::build_full[_with_gas] (pipeline.rs:354-379) bakes gas/aerosol/cloud into the 50-shell model ONCE; SolarEngine (pipeline.rs:197-233) uses DE440 when --de440 given (silent SPA fallback on open error), else NREL SPA.

4. Sunrise/sunset via find_zenith_crossing at SZA 90.8333° (pipeline.rs:509-510); terrain adjusts ONLY these two events via effective_sunrise_sza (pipeline.rs:519-552, twilight-terrain/src/horizon.rs:201) — the horizon profile never touches the RT or the Fajr/Isha thresholds.

5. Coarse scan SZA 90→min(max_sza,108°) at sza_step (default 0.5°), SimulationConfig{view_zenith:85°, solar_azimuth:evening azimuth} (pipeline.rs:565-601). One evening-geometry radiance(SZA) curve is reused for BOTH Isha and Fajr by symmetry (threshold.rs:177-178, 222-224).

6. RT per SZA: simulation::simulate_at_sza (twilight-cpu/src/simulation.rs:114-124) → single_scatter_spectrum / trace_photon backward-MC / hybrid_scatter_radiance[_alis] in twilight-core; default mode is HYBRID with photons=100 (main.rs:154-159), polarized Stokes by default (--fast switches to scalar ALIS). GPU path goes through gpu_dispatch::simulate_twilight_scan_gpu / _szalist_gpu batched scan_batch (gpu_dispatch.rs:69-185) with CPU fallback on dispatch error. RNG seeds are pure functions of (sza_bits, wavelength, photon idx) (simulation.rs:216-223, 265-289), so a given config is run-to-run deterministic.

7. Spectral radiance ×TSIS solar irradiance → W/m²/sr/nm (simulation.rs:144-170); threshold::analyze_twilight computes CIE photopic (683 lm/W), scotopic (1700 lm/W), mesopic luminance + spectral centroid (threshold.rs:96-121, luminance.rs:9-14); determine_prayer_times finds the FIRST downward crossing of fixed luminance thresholds (Fajr 0.001, abyad 0.003, ahmar-red 0.0005 cd/m²) with log-linear interpolation (threshold.rs:179-259).

8. Fine pass: 0.1° rescan around coarse crossings (pipeline.rs:627-672); skyglow spectral radiance is added AFTER refine-region selection (pipeline.rs:689-699); re-analysis → final crossing SZAs → clock times via engine.find_zenith_crossing morning 0-12h / evening 12-24h (pipeline.rs:717-727); CLI prints times + fixed-angle comparison.

VERIFIED RUNS (Mecca 2024-03-15): single-scatter CPU 36 ms, Fajr 05:29:55/SZA 104.60°; GPU single-scatter parity within 1 s. Default hybrid: CPU Fajr 05:27:47, GPU(Metal M2 Pro) 05:27:20; Isha-abyad CPU 19:30:36 vs GPU 19:28:18 (2.3 min apart).

ACTUALLY COMBINED IN pray: aerosols, clouds, live-current weather (incl. O3/NO2 gas overrides), DE440, terrain (sunrise/sunset only), skyglow injection (broken, see gaps), Stokes polarization, Metal GPU, hybrid scattering. NOT wired / fabricated: CUDA/Vulkan/WebGPU (--gpu-backend cuda|vulkan|wgpu options exist at main.rs:299-309 but those features cannot compile and the CLI never enables them); the Garstang skyglow model (garstang.rs:98,128 zenith_brightness/directional_brightness/bin_sources never called outside the crate; lib.rs:141 references `garstang::compute_skyglow` which DOES NOT EXIST); VIIRS data sources ("Embedded lookup", "World Bank S3 COG tiles", "MCRT ground-source tracer" claimed in twilight-skyglow/src/lib.rs:13-27 — no HTTP or embedded data code exists, only ConstantRadiance); crates/twilight-clouds is an empty directory (no Cargo.toml, empty src/, not a workspace member); README's `--polarized` flag (README:90-93) does not exist — the real flag is `--fast` and polarized is the default, the opposite of README's "default is scalar".

gaps.problem: spectrum::mixed_spectrum (twilight-skyglow/src/spectrum.rs:200-219, 244-257) injects the FULL VIIRS ground-level upward radiance (1 nW/cm²/sr = 1e-5 W/m²/sr) into the sky spectrum, then quick_estimate_at_angle multiplies by a 6.2x horizon factor (lib.rs:168-186, angular.rs:61-87). But the crate's own zenith-luminance model says artificial sky brightness is only 0.092·R^0.72 mcd/m² (bortle.rs:120-127). For Bortle 5 (R=6) the injected spectrum has photopic luminance ~25 mcd/m² vs the model's own 0.33 mcd/m² — ~75x too bright, as if the atmosphere scattered 100% of city light into the line of sight. VERIFIED: `pray --skyglow --bortle 5` prints 'zenith 0.33 mcd/m^2 ... ~7 minutes shift' then returns Fajr/Isha-abyad/Isha-ahmar all 'N/A (threshold not crossed)' because injected luminance (~0.1 cd/m² at the 85° view) never drops below the 0.003 cd/m² threshold.
gaps.impact: CRITICAL — the advertised light-pollution feature destroys all prayer times for any urban/suburban user instead of shifting them ~7 min; the printed shift estimate and the actual pipeline contradict each other.
gaps.fix: Normalize the injected spectrum so its photopic luminance equals the model's directional luminance: scale = directional_luminance_cd / (683·Σ V(λ)·SPD(λ)·Δλ). Add an integration test asserting analyze_twilight(skyglow-only spectrum).luminance_photopic ≈ radiance_to_zenith_luminance(R)·enhancement_factor within 5%.

gaps.problem: When max daily SZA < 90° (midnight sun), sza_upper = max_sza.min(108) < 90 makes the coarse scan empty (pipeline.rs:566, 598), and determine_prayer_times indexes into an empty Vec: `for i in 0..(analyses.len() - 1)` (threshold.rs:190-191). VERIFIED: `pray --lat 78 --lon 15 --date 2024-06-21` panics: 'index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0' at threshold.rs:191.
gaps.impact: CRITICAL — the binary crashes exactly where physically-based prayer times matter most (high-latitude summer); the existing persistent-twilight detection (pipeline.rs:554-556) does not guard this path.
gaps.fix: Early-return a PrayerTimeOutput with persistent_twilight=true when sza_upper <= 90, and make determine_prayer_times handle len<2 (`for i in 0..analyses.len().saturating_sub(1)`).

gaps.area: MC variance feeding the threshold search
gaps.problem: Default `pray` is hybrid with photons=100 (main.rs:158), 100x below the code's own convergence guidance ('Recommended: 10000+ for converged results', simulation.rs:74). Seeds are decorrelated per SZA (simulation.rs:216-223), so the luminance(SZA) curve is jagged at exactly the 0.1° fine-scan resolution where the FIRST-crossing detector interpolates (threshold.rs:190-237) — no smoothing, no monotone fit, no convergence check, no error bar. VERIFIED spread on identical Mecca input: default-CPU Fajr 05:27:47 / Isha-abyad 19:30:36; --fast 05:26:03 / 19:29:36; --photons 200 05:27:51 / 19:28:38; GPU 05:27:20 / 19:28:18. Isha-abyad moves 2.3 min between CPU and GPU defaults, and the abyad/ahmar ORDERING flips between runs (CPU-100: ahmar before abyad; GPU/200: ahmar after abyad). Output is reproducible only because seeds are frozen, not because it converged. The cv_deep_diag test (simulation.rs:1097) even counts NEGATIVE-total seeds from the ALIS estimator, and interpolate_crossing takes log of luminance with no guard for ≤0 values (threshold.rs:248-259) → NaN crossing SZA possible.
gaps.impact: HIGH — the announced prayer minute depends on photon count, polarization mode, and which compute backend happens to initialize (GPU is default on macOS, CPU elsewhere). A 1-2.5 minute hardware-dependent disagreement is material for Fajr/Isha.
gaps.fix: (1) Use correlated seeds across SZA (common random numbers) so curve shape is smooth; (2) fit a monotone/log-linear model to luminance(SZA) over the fine window instead of first-crossing on raw points; (3) adaptive sampling: increase photons until the crossing-SZA confidence interval < 0.025° (~6 s); (4) clamp/floor non-positive luminance before log interpolation; (5) make CPU the reference and gate GPU behind a parity check at the crossing region.

gaps.problem: CLI exposes --gpu-backend cuda|vulkan|wgpu (main.rs:299-309) and README badges/tables advertise 'Four hand-tuned backends ... Metal | Vulkan | CUDA | WebGPU' with 'cross-backend parity tests' (README:8,19,131-160,215,251), but crates/twilight-gpu/shaders/ contains only twilight.metal; cuda/vulkan/webgpu features fail to compile (missing twilight.cu/twilight.wgsl/*.spv — orchestrator-verified), the CLI only enables the metal feature (twilight-cli/Cargo.toml: features=["metal"]), and GPU tests no-op silently without a device (`let Some(gpu) = try_metal() else { return }`). Selecting --gpu-backend cuda silently warns and falls back to CPU.
gaps.impact: HIGH — three of four advertised backends are fabricated; parity claims are untested in CI. Note: the Metal backend itself DOES work at the integration level (verified single-scatter GPU/CPU prayer-time parity within 1 second).
gaps.fix: Delete cuda/vulkan/webgpu modules, CLI enum variants, and README claims until shaders exist; make GPU tests fail (or report skipped) when no device is present; add a CI-runnable CPU-vs-Metal crossing-SZA parity test.

gaps.problem: fetch_atmospheric_params(lat, lon) requests Open-Meteo `current=` conditions only (api.rs:67,72) with no date/hour parameter, but `pray --weather --date YYYY-MM-DD` computes times for an arbitrary date (main.rs:896-933). The instantaneous AOD/cloud/O3/NO2 snapshot at fetch time is applied to both the requested date and to BOTH twilights (one baked atmosphere serves dawn Fajr and dusk Isha, pipeline.rs:354-379, 569-579).
gaps.impact: MEDIUM-HIGH — README markets 'the engine accounts for today's actual ... cloud cover' (README:43), but cloud cover hours before dawn vs after dusk routinely differs by 100%; for any non-today date the weather is simply wrong.
gaps.fix: Use Open-Meteo's hourly forecast/archive endpoints keyed to the requested date; fetch separate snapshots at (sunset, sunrise) and run two scans (the pipeline already computes morning and evening azimuths); warn or refuse --weather for dates outside the forecast window.

gaps.area: Skyglow architecture: dead Garstang model + phantom function
gaps.problem: twilight-skyglow/src/lib.rs:13-27 claims a two-model architecture (Garstang analytical + 'MCRT ground-source tracer') and VIIRS data sources ('Embedded lookup ~10km', 'World Bank S3 ~750m COG tiles'); lib.rs:141 directs users to `garstang::compute_skyglow` which does not exist (garstang.rs exports zenith_brightness/directional_brightness/viirs_to_flux/bin_sources at :98,:128,:354,:385). None of the 796-line garstang.rs nor SkyglowConfig is called from the CLI or pipeline — `pray` uses only quick_estimate_at_angle (power law + canned spectra). README:125,201,214 repeats 'Garstang RT skyglow model'.
gaps.impact: MEDIUM — fabricated capability claims; the actually-used model is a 2-parameter empirical fit, and 800 lines of unwired code rot.
gaps.fix: Either wire garstang::directional_brightness into quick_estimate_at_angle (it would also fix the spectral normalization, since it produces a physically scaled brightness) or delete the dead module and correct the docs/README.

gaps.area: Pipeline ordering: skyglow added after refine-region selection; scan capped at 108°
gaps.problem: Skyglow radiance is injected at pipeline.rs:689-699, AFTER coarse crossings selected the 0.1° refine regions at pipeline.rs:624-638, so a skyglow-shifted crossing can fall outside the refined window and be resolved only at the 0.5° coarse grid (~2 min quantization), or beyond the hard sza_upper cap of 108° (pipeline.rs:566) and silently return N/A — skyglow/cloud cases are exactly the ones pushing Isha past 18°.
gaps.impact: MEDIUM — degraded precision or silent N/A precisely when the headline features (--skyglow, --cloud) are used.
gaps.fix: Inject skyglow before the coarse analysis, and extend the scan cap to min(max_sza, 110-112°) so threshold crossings beyond 18° depression remain detectable.

gaps.problem: SolarEngine::azimuth_at_hour converts local→UTC then clamps `(utc_hour as i32).max(0)` and `(... minutes ...).max(0)` (pipeline.rs:267-268). For east-of-Greenwich users (e.g., tz=+9, sunrise 06:00 local → UTC −3 h) the time collapses to 00:00 UTC, returning the wrong solar azimuth, which feeds the terrain horizon lookup at sunrise (pipeline.rs:521-526) and the evening view geometry (pipeline.rs:559-563). The DE440 zenith path is unaffected (de440.rs zenith_at_hour handles negative fractional hours linearly).
gaps.impact: MEDIUM — wrong terrain obstruction angle and view azimuth when --de440 is combined with --terrain at eastern longitudes; silently degrades the 'precise ephemeris' configuration.
gaps.fix: Pass the fractional hour straight through (add a De440::azimuth_at_hour mirroring zenith_at_hour) instead of clamped h/m/s decomposition.

gaps.problem: Weather/atmosphere resolution and GPU dispatch logic are duplicated between cmd_mcrt (main.rs:601-684, 731-753) and cmd_pray (main.rs:896-941, 1118-1126) and again inside compute_prayer_times_gpu (pipeline.rs:413-470); the Solar subcommand's doc comment is misattached so `Render` inherits both help lines and `Solar` has none (main.rs:24-26); crates/twilight-clouds/ is an empty directory not in the workspace (cloud physics actually lives in twilight-data/src/cloud.rs); README quick-start `--polarized` flag does not parse (real flag is --fast, polarized is default — README:90-93 says the opposite).
gaps.impact: LOW-MEDIUM — drift between the two commands (already visible: mcrt defaults view_zenith=75 vs pray's hardcoded 85), broken documented commands, and misleading help output.
gaps.fix: Move atmosphere resolution + compute-backend selection into a single shared builder in twilight-cpu; delete crates/twilight-clouds; fix the doc comments and README flags.

integration.variance_assessment: The MC path is run-to-run DETERMINISTIC for a fixed configuration (RNG seeds are pure functions of sza_bits/wavelength/photon index — simulation.rs:216-223, 265-289; two identical hybrid runs produced byte-identical times), so the prayer minute does not jitter between repeated invocations. However the determinism masks unconverged variance rather than removing it: with the default photons=100 (100x below the code's own 10,000+ recommendation at simulation.rs:74), the announced minute shifts materially across equivalent estimators on the same input — Mecca 2024-03-15 Isha-abyad: 19:30:36 (CPU polarized), 19:29:36 (--fast ALIS), 19:28:38 (photons=200), 19:28:18 (Metal GPU); Fajr spans 05:26:03–05:27:51. That is a ~2.3-minute hardware-dependent spread because GPU is the default backend when present and CPU otherwise, and the abyad/ahmar ordering even flips between configurations. Mechanism: per-SZA decorrelated seeds make the luminance(SZA) curve jagged at the 0.1° fine-scan scale, and determine_prayer_times does a raw first-crossing with log interpolation (threshold.rs:190-259) with no smoothing, no confidence interval, no convergence criterion, and no guard against the non-positive luminance values the ALIS estimator demonstrably produces (cv_deep_diag counts negative seeds, simulation.rs:1097) — log(≤0) yields NaN crossings. By contrast the deterministic single-scatter path is solid: CPU and Metal GPU agree on the final prayer times to within 1 second, so the variance problem is in the hybrid/MC estimator and its coupling to the threshold search, not in the cross-backend seam.
integration.recommended_architecture:
Target: a single trustworthy library entry point with the CLI as a thin shell.

1. ONE pipeline crate API: `twilight_cpu::pipeline::compute_prayer_times(input: PrayerTimeInput, backend: ComputeBackend) -> Result<PrayerTimeOutput, PipelineError>` — no panics (fix the empty-scan path), errors instead of silent fallbacks, and an explicit `EngineReport` recording backend used, photon count, estimated crossing-SZA uncertainty, and all silent substitutions (SPA-for-DE440, CPU-for-GPU, clear-sky-for-weather-failure).

2. Atmosphere resolution as a shared stage: `ResolveAtmosphere { manual | weather(date, hour) } -> SceneSpec`, used by both `mcrt` and `pray` (delete the duplicated blocks in main.rs). Weather keyed to the requested date with separate dawn/dusk snapshots feeding two scans; the pipeline already has both azimuths.

3. RT stage behind one trait `RadianceEngine { fn scan(&self, atm, geometry, sza_list) -> Vec<Spectrum> }` with exactly two implementations: CpuRayon (reference, f64) and Metal (accelerated). Delete cuda/vulkan/webgpu stubs and CLI options until real. Promote the existing fallback closures in compute_prayer_times_gpu into this trait. Add a mandatory startup parity probe: run 3 SZAs on both engines in single-scatter mode and refuse GPU if relative error > 0.5%.

4. Threshold stage made noise-aware: correlated seeds across SZA, monotone log-linear fit of luminance(SZA) over the refine window, crossing reported with a confidence interval, adaptive photon escalation until CI < 0.025° SZA (~6 s of clock time), luminance floored at a small positive epsilon before any log. Skyglow injected BEFORE the coarse analysis; scan ceiling raised above 108° so shifted crossings are not silently lost.

5. Skyglow rebuilt on consistent units: one function produces directional spectral radiance whose photopic luminance equals the Falchi/Garstang brightness at the pipeline's actual view elevation (5°, derived from view_zenith=85 — passed in, not hardcoded 10°); either wire garstang::directional_brightness or delete the module and the VIIRS/S3/MCRT-tracer claims.

6. Truth-in-docs pass: README and rustdoc claims regenerated from what compiles and runs (remove four-backend tables, --polarized, compute_skyglow, twilight-clouds), and a CI job that executes every README command verbatim.
priority_roadmap: 1. Fix the two user-facing breakages: (a) skyglow spectral normalization so injected luminance matches the model's own mcd/m² (spectrum.rs:200-257 + lib.rs:168-186) — currently --skyglow erases all prayer times; (b) empty-scan panic at threshold.rs:190-191 / pipeline.rs:566 — pray crashes for midnight-sun latitudes. Add regression tests for both (Bortle 5 Mecca must yield times shifted by minutes, lat 78 June must report persistent daylight, not panic).

2. Make the default invocation converged and hardware-independent: correlated seeds across SZA, monotone fit + confidence interval on the threshold crossing, adaptive photons (default budget that achieves <0.025° crossing CI instead of the flat photons=100), guard log-interpolation against non-positive luminance. Acceptance: CPU vs Metal vs --fast all agree on the printed minute for a 10-city test matrix.

At 14 deg depression the Earth-shadow screening height over the observer is ~190 km, far above the model top, so the threshold crossing sits within ~1-2 deg of a pure geometry cliff. Absolute radiometric calibration in the threshold regime: at SZA 90-96 the engine's luminance is plausible (599 cd/m2 at 90 deg, 4.0 cd/m2 at 96 deg vs literature ~300-700 and ~3), but at SZA 102 (-12 deg) it produces 2.4e-4 cd/m2 vs ~5e-3 to 1e-2 cd/m2 in published twilight curves (Rozenberg 1966; Patat et al. 2006) - a 20-40x shortfall exactly where the Fajr/Isha thresholds are evaluated. critic.overall_assessment: The 14-dimension review has strong breadth on fabrication (GPU backends, skyglow, terrain, weather, test honesty) and on the scalar MC estimator, but it systematically under-invested in three places.
